title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
萬曆巳卯秋八月天下士復
□□□惟廣東則巡按監察
□□□□□□臨之恪奉
□□□□□□□□□□
□□□□□□□鷹鸇之屆
□□□□□□聘自四方至
===
□□□□□□及訓導唐師
□□□試學正趙之垣教諭
侯必恭梁學奎李一元分祭
明訓導劉世節席一唯司考
試而提調則右布政使錢藻
左參議漆彬監試則按察使
莊國禎副使趙志臯一切內
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序
萬曆巳卯秋八月，天下士復□□□，惟廣東則巡按監察□□□□□□臨之。恪奉□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□鷹鸇之屆。□□□□□□聘自四方至，□□□□□□及訓導唐師□□□試，學正趙之垣，教諭侯必恭、梁學奎、李一元、分祭明，訓導劉世節、席一唯司考試；而提調則右布政使錢藻、左參議漆彬，監試則按察使莊國禎、副使趙志臯，一切內
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the jimao year of the Wanli era (1579), the scholars of the realm once again [gathered for the examinations…]. In Guangdong, the Regional Inspector, Investigating [Censor…] presided as Supervising Official. Reverently upholding […], at this season when hawks and falcons strike [i.e., mid-autumn]. […] invited from the four quarters arrived: […] and Assistant Instructor Tang Shi[…] to serve as Examiners; Department Director of Studies Zhao Zhiyuan, District Directors of Studies Hou Bigong, Liang Xuekui, Li Yiyuan, and Fen Jiming [?], and Assistant Instructors Liu Shijie and Xi Yiwei took charge of the examination [as Associate Examiners]. Serving as Proctors were Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Qian Zao and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Qi Bin; serving as Monitoring Officials were Surveillance Commissioner Zhuang Guozhen and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhao Zhigao. All the inner…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
外百執事庀僚分寄咸充其
選旣復羣百執事齋籲而盟
惟公惟慎期綜材實而收之
以不虛
簡任至意越日進提學副使孫錦
□□提學副使舒大猷所遴
□□□□奇試之三而
===
功令率循無爲文具文學校閱
不令旁干則御史尤諄諄焉
于是遵
制拔其雋七十五人幷彙其文之
如式者以
獻錄成御史顧日休宜序諸首日
休不佞猥以職事獲與掄材
punctuated: 外百執事，庀僚分寄，咸充其選。旣，復羣百執事齋籲而盟，惟公惟慎，期綜材實而收之，以不虛簡任至意。越日，進提學副使孫錦、□□提學副使舒大猷所遴□□□□奇，試之三，而功令率循，無爲文具；文學校閱，不令旁干，則御史尤諄諄焉。于是遵制拔其雋七十五人，幷彙其文之如式者以獻。錄成，御史顧日休宜序諸首。日休不佞，猥以職事，獲與掄材
translation_en: … and outer functionaries of all ranks; in preparing the subordinate staff and assigning their responsibilities, all fulfilled the requirements of their selection. Thereupon, all the functionaries were assembled to fast, invoke the spirits, and swear an oath to act solely with impartiality and prudence, hoping to gather and select men of genuine talent and substance so as not to betray the utmost intent of the imperial appointment. After a day had passed, the [candidates] selected by Surveillance Vice Commissioner cum Education Intendant Sun Jin 孫錦 and […?] Surveillance Vice Commissioner cum Education Intendant Shu Dayou 舒大猷, numbering […?] odd, were brought in and examined in three sessions. The statutory regulations were strictly followed without becoming mere formalities, and in the evaluation of literary compositions no outside interference was permitted—in these matters the Regional Inspector was especially earnest and tireless. Thereupon, in compliance with the imperial system, seventy-five outstanding candidates were selected, and their compositions that conformed to the prescribed models were compiled to be presented to the Throne. When the record was completed, the Regional Inspector looked to me, Rixiu 日休, deeming it fitting that I write a preface at its head. Unworthy though I, Rixiu, am, having by virtue of my official duties had the fortune to participate in the grand affair of selecting talent…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之盛敢不唯唯盖自周制天
子命侯國建學造士士之有
造而秀者鄕論之第升之天
子銓敘材品而祿爵之當其
時上弘薪槱之道賓賢之典
罔或不虔士以賢見賓登之
論選罔或不適考信於王制
===
以跡其盛則聖世人文可遡
而窺也
明興準周甄士三載賓賢方之爲
烈肆東粵士競爽稱文繇其
文評隲其材豈不贇贇然秀
哉夫士挾材不難際時難際
時不難遇君難懿我
punctuated: 之盛，敢不唯唯？盖自周制，天子命侯國建學造士，士之有造而秀者，鄕論之，第升之天子，銓敘材品而祿爵之。當其時，上弘薪槱之道，賓賢之典罔或不虔；士以賢見賓，登之論選，罔或不適。考信於《王制》，以跡其盛，則聖世人文可遡而窺也。明興，準周甄士，三載賓賢，方之爲烈。肆東粵士競爽稱文，繇其文評隲其材，豈不贇贇然秀哉！夫士挾材不難，際時難；際時不難，遇君難。懿我
translation_en: … such a grand occasion, how could I dare not respectfully assent? Indeed, under the system of the Zhou dynasty, the Son of Heaven commanded the feudal states to establish schools to cultivate scholars. Those scholars who were accomplished and outstanding were evaluated in their local districts and graded to be promoted to the Son of Heaven, who assessed and ranked their talents and character, and bestowed upon them emoluments and titles of nobility. At that time, those above broadened the Way of gathering firewood and stacking it—that is, recruiting and nurturing talent—and the rites of welcoming the worthy as guests were never anything less than reverent; scholars were welcomed as guests on account of their worthiness, and when raised to evaluation and selection, none failed to be suited to their posts. By verifying this in the Royal Regulations (Wangzhi) to trace that flourishing era, one can look back and glimpse the cultural brilliance of a sage age. When the Ming arose, it modeled itself on the Zhou in discerning scholars; welcoming the worthy as guests every three years, its achievements are even more illustrious by comparison. Thus the scholars of Guangdong (Dongyue) vie in brilliance and are renowned for their literary refinement; judging and ranking their talents through their writings, how could they not be splendidly outstanding! Now, for a scholar to possess talent is not difficult, but to meet with the right era is difficult; to meet with the right era is not difficult, but to encounter the right ruler is difficult. Admirable is our …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上睿喆秉籙
經幃不輟
御幸學右文廣厲多士斂琱還樸
無言逖邇菁英躍於聽覩藻
采新於風問夫孰不願爲材
曩東粤棘兵士無寧業
詔趣文武大吏不崇朝而清之卽
===
今文治同風要以轉呻讙而
絃誦寔惟粤士不無幸者是
以日休從鎖院後繙據多士
所爲文大都淹六籍漱衆流
指事陳政不卑卑吐華此非
帝德焜燿宜不及此夫士偃蓬蒿
抱藝媒合惟恐不得當有司
punctuated: 皇上睿喆秉籙，經幃不輟，御幸學、右文、廣厲多士，斂琱還樸，無言逖邇。菁英躍於聽覩，藻采新於風問，夫孰不願爲材？曩東粤棘兵，士無寧業。詔趣文武大吏，不崇朝而清之。卽今文治同風，要以轉呻讙而絃誦，寔惟粤士不無幸者。是以日休從鎖院後，繙據多士所爲文，大都淹六籍、漱衆流，指事陳政，不卑卑吐華。此非帝德焜燿，宜不及此。夫士偃蓬蒿，抱藝媒合，惟恐不得當有司。
translation_en:
…August Emperor holds the imperial mandate with sagely wisdom. He is unceasing in attending the Classics Colloquium, visits the Imperial University in person, exalts literary culture, and broadly encourages the multitude of scholars, restraining ornate carving and returning to simplicity, making no distinction between far and near. Outstanding talents leap at what they hear and see, and literary brilliance is renewed through the spread of his transforming influence—who then would not wish to become a man of talent?

Previously, when eastern Yue (Guangdong) suffered the thorny troubles of war, scholars had no peaceful livelihood. By imperial edict, senior civil and military officials were urged into action, and before a morning had passed they pacified the region. Now civil governance shares a unified風 (ethos), turning groans and clamor into the strumming of instruments and chanting of classics; truly, the scholars of Guangdong are not without good fortune in this. Therefore, after entering the locked examination compound, as I, Rixiu, leafed through and examined the essays composed by the many scholars, I found that for the most part they are steeped in the Six Classics and rinsed in the various schools of thought, pointing to real affairs and setting forth governance without merely spouting superficial flowery phrases. Were it not for the radiant brilliance of the Emperor's virtue, things would surely not have reached this level.

Now, when scholars lie hidden amid wildbrush and mugwort, cherishing their literary arts in hopes of finding a match, their only fear is failing to satisfy the authorities…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有司業以士進矣吹一映以
快里耳折楊皇華則噤無與
和績緝緒言以詭世資竟之
實不揜名履不循素至令主
司廩廩懷懼則何以稱哉先
是言官
上正文體五事又悉重試務而顓
===
之監臨委寄內簾以湛衡鑑
皇上嘉與元輔疏
聞輒下禮卿條便宜
頒之郡國搜羅雋彥誠急之也鄉
始論士卽注
聖衷如此士灑心以應
明德趣安所决哉在昔文治初闢
punctuated: 有司業以士進矣，吹一映以快里耳，折楊皇華則噤無與和；績緝緒言以詭世資，竟之實不揜名，履不循素，至令主司廩廩懷懼，則何以稱哉？先是，言官上正文體五事，又悉重試務而顓之監臨，委寄內簾以湛衡鑑。皇上嘉與元輔疏聞，輒下禮卿條便宜，頒之郡國，搜羅雋彥，誠急之也。鄉始論士，卽注聖衷如此，士灑心以應明德，趣安所决哉？在昔文治初闢，
translation_en: Once the officials have advanced these scholars, if they merely blow a tiny puff of wind on a sword-guard to please vulgar ears—or when it comes to "Breaking the Willow" and "Imperial Blossoms" [?], fall silent with none harmonizing—and if they piece together leftover words to fraudulently gain worldly qualifications, in the end their reality will not match their reputation and their conduct will not follow their erstwhile principles, to the point of making the chief examiners tremble with fear; how then could they measure up? Earlier, a speaking official submitted a memorial on five matters for rectifying literary style, and furthermore emphasized all aspects of examination administration, placing sole responsibility on the Supervising Official and entrusting the inner examination compound to clarify the scales and mirror of evaluation. Whenever His Majesty the Emperor approved what the Senior Grand Secretary reported by memorial, he immediately sent it down to the Minister of Rites to itemize appropriate measures and promulgate them to the prefectures and principalities; in seeking out and gathering outstanding talents, he has truly treated this as urgent! At the very start of evaluating scholars in the provinces, the Imperial mind is already focused on it like this; when scholars cleanse their hearts to respond to His Illustrious Virtue, where should their aspirations be directed? In past times, when civil governance was first opened up, …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
區冊趙德才能不逾中人猶
然附青雲以有聲此一時也
非馳騖勩思抗蹟嵬伐則不
足以軼前徽照後禩何者
主上明聖則當意之難遘會
熈明則表見未易也吾聞廉吏綰
綬而鍾乳復賢守剖符而明
===
珠還彼守長耳至於山靈告
祥淵光生媚矧我
皇上儼然以
純德臨照之而
嘉禮慶成關雎歌洽則羔羊在位
兔罝在野其應不爽多士資
適逢世當令蚌胎讓采乳穴
punctuated: 區冊、趙德才能不逾中人，猶然附青雲以有聲，此一時也。非馳騖勩思，抗蹟嵬伐，則不足以軼前徽、照後禩。何者？主上明聖，則當意之難；遘會熈明，則表見未易也。吾聞廉吏綰綬而鍾乳復，賢守剖符而明珠還。彼守長耳，至於山靈告祥，淵光生媚；矧我皇上儼然以純德臨照之，而嘉禮慶成，關雎歌洽，則羔羊在位，兔罝在野，其應不爽。多士資適逢世，當令蚌胎讓采，乳穴…
translation_en: …Ou Ce and Zhao De had talents and abilities not surpassing those of average men, yet they still attached themselves to high eminence to gain renown—that was one era. Now, unless one gallops forth with painstaking thought, elevating one's conduct to lofty achievements, it will not suffice to surpass the fine models of the past and shine upon future generations. Why is this? When the Sovereign is enlightened and sage, it is difficult to meet His expectations; when one encounters an era of resplendent clarity, it is not easy to distinguish oneself. I have heard that when an incorrupt official tied on his seal-ribbon, the stalactite milk returned to the caves, and when a worthy Prefect split the tally of office, the bright pearls came back to the waters. Those were merely local magistrates and prefects, yet the mountain spirits announced auspicious signs and the gleaming depths grew radiant with charm. How much more so when our August Emperor solemnly shines down upon the realm with His pure virtue, and when the auspicious wedding rites have been felicitously accomplished and the song of "Guanju" (The Osprey's Cry) resounds in harmony! Then officials pure as the "Lambskin" ode will occupy their posts, and men of talent like those of the "Rabbit Snare" ode will be found in the countryside—this response will never fail. As the many scholars have native gifts that happen to meet with such an age, they should cause the pearl-oysters to yield their luster and the stalactite caverns…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
遴珍其所自效宜何如者言
蘄成信不弁髦其先資事蘄
當功不虛恢於注厝宣猶展
采直與素絲一節公侯匹體
詎兎罝野人下哉惟多士决
策焉異時抽
天府賢書論讚其盛如所爲追頌
===
王制者必在
今日矣是舉也先總督兩廣軍
務都察院右都御史今陞南
京兵部尚書凌雲翼今總督
兩廣軍務兵部右侍郎劉堯
誨後先節鎮捄武宣文提督
南贛汀韶軍務都察院右僉
punctuated:
遴珍。其所自效，宜何如者？言蘄成信，不弁髦其先資；事蘄當功，不虛恢於注厝。宣猶展采，直與素絲一節，公侯匹體，詎兎罝野人下哉？惟多士决策焉。異時抽天府賢書，論讚其盛，如所爲追頌王制者，必在今日矣。
是舉也，先總督兩廣軍務都察院右都御史、今陞南京兵部尚書凌雲翼，今總督兩廣軍務兵部右侍郎劉堯誨，後先節鎮，捄武宣文；提督南贛汀韶軍務都察院右僉
translation_en:
…and the stalactite caves yield their choicest treasures. How, then, ought they to dedicate themselves in service? In their words, they should strive to establish trustworthiness, not casting aside like a worn-out cap the initial pledges with which they entered service; in their deeds, they should strive for tangible achievement, not engaging in empty boasting in their administrative measures. By setting forth their plans and displaying their talents, they will match the integrity of the "Plain Silk" (Susi) ode and stand as counterparts to dukes and marquises—how could they be any less than the rustic men of the "Rabbit Snare" (Tuju) ode? Let the many scholars resolve upon this course! In the future, when the rolls of the worthy are drawn from the imperial archives to discuss and praise their flourishing achievements, just as the Royal Regulations (Wangzhi) were celebrated in retrospect, it will surely look back to this very day!

In this examination, the former Supreme Commander of Military Affairs of Liangguang and Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, now promoted to Nanjing Minister of War, Ling Yunyi 凌雲翼, and the current Supreme Commander of Military Affairs of Liangguang and Right Vice Minister of War, Liu Yaohui 劉堯誨, successively held the regional command, pacifying through military might and spreading civil culture; the Grand Coordinator of Military Affairs of Nan'gan and Tingshao and Right Assistant…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
都御史蒙詔風猷表士而右
參政劉經緯徐時可張明正
右參議王來賢副使劉世賞
張堯年僉事馬千乘熊惟學
侯應爵右都督總兵官張元
勳副總兵陳璘侯繼高參將
楊瑄夏尚忠季金顧宗文遊
===
擊金丹韓沛朱文達葉歡署
都指揮僉事祖萬松咸防範
惟周先期入
賀則左參政孫光祖僉事劉倬
署都指揮僉事成大儒遷秩
則左布政使今陞順天府府
尹施堯臣與聞
punctuated: 都御史蒙詔，風猷表士；而右參政劉經緯、徐時可、張明正，右參議王來賢，副使劉世賞、張堯年，僉事馬千乘、熊惟學、侯應爵，右都督總兵官張元勳，副總兵陳璘、侯繼高，參將楊瑄、夏尚忠、季金、顧宗文，遊擊金丹、韓沛、朱文達、葉歡，署都指揮僉事祖萬松，咸防範惟周；先期入賀，則左參政孫光祖、僉事劉倬、署都指揮僉事成大儒；遷秩，則左布政使今陞順天府府尹施堯臣，與聞
translation_en: … [Right Assistant] Censor-in-Chief Meng Zhao 蒙詔, who served as models of moral conduct for the scholars; while Right Administration Vice Commissioners Liu Jingwei 劉經緯, Xu Shike 徐時可, and Zhang Mingzheng 張明正; Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Wang Laixian 王來賢; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Liu Shishang 劉世賞 and Zhang Yaonian 張堯年; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Ma Qiancheng 馬千乘, Xiong Weixue 熊惟學, and Hou Yingjue 侯應爵; Commissioner-in-Chief of the Right and Regional Commander Zhang Yuanxun 張元勳; Regional Vice Commanders Chen Lin 陳璘 and Hou Jigao 侯繼高; Assistant Regional Commanders Yang Xuan 楊瑄, Xia Shangzhong 夏尚忠, Ji Jin 季金, and Gu Zongwen 顧宗文; Mobile Corps Commanders Jin Dan 金丹, Han Pei 韓沛, Zhu Wenda 朱文達, and Ye Huan 葉歡; and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Zu Wansong 祖萬松 all maintained thorough security precautions; those who departed ahead of time to offer congratulations at court were Left Administration Vice Commissioner Sun Guangzu 孫光祖, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Liu Zhuo 劉倬, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Cheng Daru 成大儒; and among those transferred to new ranks was Left Administration Commissioner Shi Yaochen 施堯臣, now promoted to Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture 順天府, who participated in hearing of …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
盛典例得並書
浙江杭州府海寧縣儒學敎
諭鄭日休謹序
punctuated:
盛典，例得並書。
浙江杭州府海寧縣儒學敎諭鄭日休謹序。
translation_en:
… this grand ceremony; by precedent, their names may all be recorded together.

Respectfully prefaced by Zheng Rixiu 鄭日休, Instructor in the Confucian School of Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
萬曆七年廣東鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史龔懋賢〔晉甫四川內江縣人戊辰進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使錢藻〔自文直隸如皋縣人乙未進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參議漆彬〔中甫江西南昌縣人辛未進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使莊國禎〔君祉福建晉江縣人壬戌進士〕
廣東等處提刑按察司副使趙志皐〔汝邁浙江蘭谿縣人戊辰進士〕
===
考試官
浙江杭州府海寧縣儒學教諭鄭日休〔德卿福建閩縣人甲子貢士〕
浙江湖州府儒學訓導唐師錫〔邦魯福建莆田縣人丁卯貢士〕

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
經筵時
御禮獨切于隆儒
講幄日
親心尤勤于向道
學三王
學二帝
聖功遠軼乎前脩
爲八體
爲六書
===
宸翰復臻于佳妙頃當
聽朝之暇俄驚
御墨之頒中使傳呼
雲章來于
天上羣工拜捧
華衮動乎人間謂臣等職分殊司乃
命字各爲寓義保衡宅揆交歡道協虞殷夾輔
同心
簡畀榮符周召正巳率屬倣周官六典以阜成
punctuated: 經筵時御，禮獨切于隆儒；講幄日親，心尤勤于向道。學三王，學二帝，聖功遠軼乎前脩；爲八體，爲六書，宸翰復臻于佳妙。頃當聽朝之暇，俄驚御墨之頒。中使傳呼，雲章來于天上；羣工拜捧，華衮動乎人間。謂臣等職分殊司，乃命字各爲寓義。保衡宅揆，交歡道協虞、殷；夾輔同心，簡畀榮符周、召。正巳率屬，倣《周官》六典以阜成；
translation_en:
… As the Classics Colloquia are attended at the proper seasons, His Majesty's rites are uniquely earnest in exalting Confucian scholars; as the lecture curtains are approached day by day, his heart is ever more diligent in aspiring to the Way. Studying the Three Kings and studying the Two Emperors, his sagely achievements far surpass those of former worthies; practicing the eight calligraphic styles and practicing the six principles of script, the imperial brush further attains exquisite perfection.

Just recently, during a moment of leisure from holding court, we were suddenly awed by the bestowal of the imperial ink. Palace emissaries relayed the summons, and cloud-like writings descended from Heaven above; the assembled officials bowed to receive them in both hands, and the splendor of ceremonial robes stirred the realm of mortals below. Declaring that Your Majesty's servants hold responsibilities divided among distinct offices, You ordered that each inscription be imbued with a fitting meaning. For the Protector-Regulator and the occupant of the premiership, mutual joy and shared Way harmonize with the eras of Yu and Yin; assisting on either side with a single heart, the glorious charge of imperial selection matches that of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao. Rectifying ourselves to lead our subordinates, we model ourselves on the Six Canons of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) so as to bring about abundance and completion; …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書
稽于眾舍己從人不虐無告不廢困窮
伊洛瀍澗既入于河
自殷王中宗及高宗及祖甲及我周文王
茲四人迪哲
則亦有熊羆之士不二心之臣保乂王家
詩
春日載陽有鳴倉庚
樂只君子天子葵之
===
雝雝在宮肅肅在廟不顯亦臨無射亦保
四海來假來假祁祁景員維河殷受命咸
宜百祿是何
春秋
鄭人伐衞〔隱公二年〕
齊師宋師曹師次于聶北救邢　夏六月
邢遷于夷儀齊師宋師曹師城邢〔俱僖〕
〔公元年〕
衞人救陳〔宣公十有二年〕會于蕭魚〔襄公〕
punctuated:
《書》：
「稽于眾，舍己從人，不虐無告，不廢困窮。」
「伊、洛、瀍、澗，既入于河。」
「自殷王中宗，及高宗，及祖甲，及我周文王，茲四人迪哲。」
「則亦有熊羆之士，不二心之臣，保乂王家。」

《詩》：
「春日載陽，有鳴倉庚。」
「樂只君子，天子葵之。」
「雝雝在宮，肅肅在廟。不顯亦臨，無射亦保。」
「四海來假，來假祁祁。景員維河，殷受命咸宜，百祿是何。」

《春秋》：
「鄭人伐衞。」〔隱公二年〕
「齊師、宋師、曹師次于聶北，救邢。夏六月，邢遷于夷儀。齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。」〔俱僖公元年〕
「衞人救陳。」〔宣公十有二年〕「會于蕭魚。」〔襄公…
translation_en:

"He consulted the multitude, setting aside his own views to follow others; he did not oppress the helpless, nor did he neglect the destitute and poor."
"The Yi, Luo, Chan, and Jian rivers were conducted into the Yellow River."
"From the Yin king Zhongzong, down to Gaozong, to Zujia, and to our Zhou King Wen—these four men walked in wisdom."
"Then too there were warriors like bears and grisly bears, and ministers of undivided loyalty, who protected and regulated the royal house."

Book of Odes (Shi):
"In the spring days the warmth begins, and the orioles sing."
"Happy be the lord! The Son of Heaven measures his merits."
"Harmonious in the palace, reverent in the ancestral temple; though out of sight, as if under inspection; untiring in preservation."
"From the four seas they come in homage; they come in great multitudes. With the great circuit of the Yellow River as its boundary, Yin's receipt of the Mandate was wholly fitting, and it sustained the hundred blessings."

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:

禮記
君命大夫與士肄在官言官在府言府在
庫言庫在朝言朝
故人者天地之心也五行之端也
樂行而民鄉方可以觀德矣
君子恭儉以求役仁信讓以求役禮
第貳場

周家王業根本

「周家王業根本」

擬漢開籍田詔〔文帝二年〕

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:

年

官吏給由
攬納稅糧

私賣軍器

===

問君心唯在所養而培養之功必于學焉
伊昔哲王典學首稱殷高宗說命所陳
其辭可指而述歟厥後代有英辟或石
渠講經或臨雍拜老或弘文置館或崇
政說書其學亦有得于說命之要歟我
太祖高皇帝
聖神御極
萬幾暇卽與侍臣講論經史

官吏給由。
攬納稅糧。

私賣軍器。
詐爲瑞應。

第叁場

策五道：
問：君心唯在所養，而培養之功必于學焉。伊昔哲王典學，首稱殷高宗，《說命》所陳，其辭可指而述歟？厥後代有英辟，或石渠講經，或臨雍拜老，或弘文置館，或崇政說書，其學亦有得于《說命》之要歟？我太祖高皇帝聖神御極，萬幾暇卽與侍臣講論經史，

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承並崇
聖學其大要可得聞歟我
皇上
睿質天授
學問夙成而
經筵日講猶勤勤焉
紹庥闡繹直超殷宗上之一時講讀諸臣所納
誨必取衷于典學之撰矣夫
帝王之學與韋布不同其大本大原固有在也
===
攷之
會典所載進講後凡五府軍政六部要務詹
事等官皆得以次敷陳
今日可復行否耶宋儒在經筵有反覆開導
覬有啓悟者有講色莊嚴繼以諷諫者
今能有進於是乎諸士懷忠藎之忱素
矣願詳著于篇以為
聖學緝熙之助
問學術事功非二物也世之言學術者必
punctuated:
列聖相承，並崇聖學，其大要可得聞歟？我皇上睿質天授，學問夙成，而經筵、日講猶勤勤焉。紹庥闡繹，直超殷宗上之。一時講讀諸臣所納誨，必取衷于典學之撰矣。夫帝王之學與韋布不同，其大本大原固有在也。攷之《會典》所載，進講後，凡五府軍政、六部要務，詹事等官皆得以次敷陳，今日可復行否耶？宋儒在經筵，有反覆開導、覬有啓悟者，有講色莊嚴、繼以諷諫者，今能有進於是乎？諸士懷忠藎之忱素矣，願詳著于篇，以為聖學緝熙之助。

問：學術、事功非二物也。世之言學術者必
translation_en:
… The successive sage emperors have inherited this tradition and all revered sagely learning; may we hear of its main essentials? Our August Emperor has a perspicacious nature bestowed by Heaven and learning that reached maturity early, yet at the Classics Mat colloquia and daily lectures he remains ever diligent. Continuing the dynastic blessings and expounding their meaning, he directly surpasses Gaozong of Yin and rises above him. The admonitions offered by the various lecturing and reading officials of the present time must surely take as their standard the compositions on constant devotion to learning. Now, the learning of emperors and kings differs from that of commoners in coarse cloth; its great foundation and great source certainly lie somewhere. Examining what is recorded in the Collected Statutes (Huidian 會典), after the presentation of the lectures, in all matters of the military administration of the Five Chief Military Commissions and the important affairs of the Six Ministries, officials such as the Supervisor of the Household (zhanshi 詹事) were all permitted to set them forth in turn; can this be put into practice again today or not? Among the Song Confucians at the Classics Mat, there were those who repeatedly guided and explained in hopes of inspiring enlightenment, and there were those who lectured with a solemn countenance and followed up with indirect remonstrance; today, can one go even further than this? You gentlemen have long cherished sentiments of loyal devotion; I wish you to set them forth in detail in your essays, to serve as an aid to the bright continuation of sagely learning.

Question: Scholarly learning and practical achievement are not two separate things. Those in the world who speak of scholarly learning invariably…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
稱孔孟言事功者必曰伊周若岐而二
之何歟假令數聖賢者生同其時其所
建立發明亦有相符合者歟漢唐以來
有潜心大業罷黜百家者有攘斥異端
推尊孟氏者不謂非學術也而世儒何
每有訾言有運籌决勝佐成帝業者有
潜授豪賢卒正主器者不謂非事功也
而尚論者何猶有遺議歟若夫濂洛關
閩之學慶曆熈寧諸君子之勳班班史
冊稱盛矣視前數子者孰優其於孔孟
伊周之軌亦庶幾否耶然樹立俊偉者
不以理學稱而多所發明得理學之傳
者乃用之不果究焉豈所學不適於用
而用者無待於學歟諸生誦法孔孟亦
志伊周矣推學術以建事功此其時也
願質言之無隱
問吏數易置則民不安兩漢之盛也牧守
長子孫焉是非其效驗較著者歟我
punctuated:
稱孔、孟，言事功者必曰伊、周，若岐而二之，何歟？假令數聖賢者生同其時，其所建立發明，亦有相符合者歟？漢、唐以來，有潜心大業、罷黜百家者，有攘斥異端、推尊孟氏者，不謂非學術也，而世儒何每有訾言？有運籌决勝、佐成帝業者，有潜授豪賢、卒正主器者，不謂非事功也，而尚論者何猶有遺議歟？若夫濂、洛、關、閩之學，慶曆、熈寧諸君子之勳，班班史冊，稱盛矣。視前數子者孰優？其於孔、孟、伊、周之軌，亦庶幾否耶？然樹立俊偉者不以理學稱，而多所發明、得理學之傳者，乃用之不果究焉，豈所學不適於用，而用者無待於學歟？諸生誦法孔、孟，亦志伊、周矣，推學術以建事功，此其時也。願質言之無隱。

問：吏數易置則民不安。兩漢之盛也，牧守長子孫焉，是非其效驗較著者歟？我
translation_en:
… cite Confucius 孔子 and Mencius 孟子, while those who speak of practical achievements inevitably name Yi Yin 伊尹 and the Duke of Zhou 周公, as if dividing them into two separate paths—why is this? Suppose these several sages and worthies had lived in the same era: would what they established in deed and elucidated in teaching have agreed with one another? Since the Han and Tang dynasties, there was one who immersed his mind in the great enterprise of learning and dismissed the Hundred Schools [Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒], and one who repelled heterodoxies and exalted Mencius [Han Yu 韓愈]; one cannot say these were not matters of scholarly learning, yet why do scholars of the world so often find fault with them? There was one who devised strategies for decisive victory and assisted in founding the imperial enterprise [Zhang Liang 張良], and one who secretly recommended heroic worthies and ultimately restored the rightful heir to the throne [Di Renjie 狄仁傑]; one cannot say these were not practical achievements, yet why do those who evaluate the figures of history still have lingering criticisms of them? As for the learning of Lian 濂, Luo 洛, Guan 關, and Min 閩 [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤, the Cheng brothers 程顥/程頤, Zhang Zai 張載, and Zhu Xi 朱熹], and the meritorious deeds of the noble men of the Qingli (1041–1048) and Xining (1068–1077) eras, they are clearly recorded in the historical annals and praised as flourishing. Compared with the several figures mentioned previously, which are superior? And do they come close to the path of Confucius, Mencius, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou, or not? Yet those who established grand and distinguished achievements were not renowned for the Learning of Principle (lixue 理學), whereas those who elucidated much and received the transmission of the Learning of Principle were, when employed, unable to carry their application through to the end. Could it be that what is learned is unsuited for practical use, and that those who are employed for practical use have no need of learning? You students recite and model yourselves on Confucius and Mencius, and likewise set your ambitions on Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. To extend scholarly learning in order to establish practical achievements—this is the time for it. I hope you will speak plainly and hold nothing back.

Question: When officials are frequently replaced, the people are unsettled. During the flourishing of the Western and Eastern Han dynasties, regional governors and grand administrators raised sons and grandsons in office [taking their office names as surnames]; is this not a case where the efficacy of long tenure was clearly manifest? When Our…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上御寓之初首用輔臣議久任責成不驟遷
以奪其成效一時吏稱民安臻上理矣
而或者謂久任便民不便吏然歟夫置
吏爲民民誠便不便吏何傷顧使吏多
滯歎人懷厭心不有以鼓舞振作之亦
奚以厲世而磨鈍也乃其道安在歟先
正有言久任之法與超遷相表裏其說
可得聞歟
祖宗朝蓋兼用之矣其在
===
今日可踵而行之否也或又謂文法之拘勝
則顧慮多內外之勢懸則覬慕起斯二
患蓋自古已然玆欲使長民之吏皆樂
於久任以殫脩厥職而不負責成則將
何策而可
問象緯禨祥之說推天徵人多所牽合然
蓋尚矣乃孔子作春秋紀災異而不言
事應何歟考之星官彗孛飛流皆變星
也說者謂孛而不已繼之以彗而晏子
punctuated:
皇上御寓之初，首用輔臣議，久任責成，不驟遷以奪其成效，一時吏稱民安，臻上理矣。而或者謂久任便民不便吏，然歟？夫置吏爲民，民誠便，不便吏何傷？顧使吏多滯歎，人懷厭心，不有以鼓舞振作之，亦奚以厲世而磨鈍也？乃其道安在歟？先正有言：「久任之法，與超遷相表裏。」其說可得聞歟？祖宗朝蓋兼用之矣，其在今日，可踵而行之否也？或又謂文法之拘勝則顧慮多，內外之勢懸則覬慕起，斯二患蓋自古已然。玆欲使長民之吏，皆樂於久任，以殫脩厥職而不負責成，則將何策而可？

問：象緯禨祥之說，推天徵人，多所牽合，然蓋尚矣。乃孔子作《春秋》，紀災異而不言事應，何歟？考之星官，彗、孛、飛、流，皆變星也。說者謂孛而不已，繼之以彗；而晏子
translation_en:
…At the beginning of His Majesty's reign, he first adopted the counsel of his Grand Secretaries to keep officials in office for long terms and hold them accountable for results, not transferring them abruptly so as to deprive them of their accomplishments. For a time, officials were competent and the people were at peace, attaining supreme governance. Yet some say that long tenure is convenient for the people but inconvenient for the officials—is this so? Now, officials are appointed for the sake of the people; if the people are truly convenienced, what harm is there if it is inconvenient for the officials? Nevertheless, if it causes officials to frequently sigh over stagnation and everyone to harbor feelings of weariness, and there is no way to inspire and rouse them, how then can one encourage the world and sharpen the dull? Wherein, then, does that way lie? A former worthy had a saying: "The method of long tenure and that of rapid promotion complement each other as outside and inside." May we hear an explanation of this? The courts of our Ancestors indeed used both together; in the present day, can we follow in their footsteps and practice this or not? Others also say that when the constraints of written regulations prevail, misgivings multiply; when the status between the inner [capital] and outer [provincial] posts is vastly unequal, covetous longings arise. These two ills have indeed existed since antiquity. Now, if we wish to make all officials who govern the people happy to serve long terms, so as to exhaustively fulfill their duties and not fail the demand for results, what policy will suffice?

Question: The theories of celestial portents and auspicious or inauspicious signs, which infer human affairs from heaven, involve much forced correlation, yet they are of great antiquity. Why is it, then, that when Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), he recorded disasters and anomalies without speaking of the corresponding human events? Examining the astrological treatises,broom stars (sui), bushy stars (bo), flying stars (fei), and meteors (liu) are all anomalous stars. Commentators say that when a bushy star does not cease, it is followed by a broom star; yet Master Yan (Yanzi)…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則曰君不脩政孛星將出彗何懼焉則
孛又甚於彗矣然而建元元狩中有孛
于西北孛于東方者矣地節中有孛于
西方孛于參者矣永平建初中有孛于
天船孛于天市孛于紫宮者矣夫語中
興之業宜無二於四君者乃其變若此
而徵應不見豈史失其傳歟抑天道遠
而難言歟或四君者所以消弭之者有
道變不為災歟有言星變結和太上脩
===
德其次脩政其次脩救其次脩禳其亦
有當否我
皇上敬
天朝夕乾惕頃
書十二事
座右以備
觀省宜無容言者比以星變輒
警畏勵精
簡廷臣而科條之百司皇皇思過不暇雖知
punctuated: 則曰：「君不脩政，孛星將出，彗何懼焉？」則孛又甚於彗矣。然而建元、元狩中有孛于西北、孛于東方者矣；地節中有孛于西方、孛于參者矣；永平、建初中有孛于天船、孛于天市、孛于紫宮者矣。夫語中興之業，宜無二於四君者，乃其變若此，而徵應不見，豈史失其傳歟？抑天道遠而難言歟？或四君者所以消弭之者有道，變不為災歟？有言星變結和：太上脩德，其次脩政，其次脩救，其次脩禳。其亦有當否？我皇上敬天，朝夕乾惕，頃書十二事座右，以備觀省，宜無容言者。比以星變，輒警畏勵精，簡廷臣而科條之，百司皇皇，思過不暇，雖知
translation_en:
… said: "If the ruler does not cultivate his governance, a bushy star (boxing) will appear—what is there to fear from a broom star (hui)?" By this account, a bushy star is even worse than a broom star. Yet during the Jianyuan (140–135 BCE) and Yuanshou (122–117 BCE) eras [of Emperor Wu of Han], bushy stars appeared in the northwest and in the east; during the Dijie era (69–66 BCE) [of Emperor Xuan of Han], bushy stars appeared in the west and in the lunar lodge Shen (Orion); and during the Yongping (58–75 CE) and Jianchu (76–84 CE) eras [of Emperors Ming and Zhang of Han], bushy stars appeared in the constellations Tianshuan (Celestial Boat), Tianshi (Celestial Market), and Zigong (Purple Palace). Now, when speaking of achievements in dynastic restoration and flourishing rule, none should surpass these four monarchs; yet suchcelestial anomalies occurred, and no corresponding calamities were seen. Could it be that the histories lost record of them? Or is the Way of Heaven distant and difficult to speak of? Or did those four monarchs possess the way to dispel and avert them so that the anomalies did not turn into disasters? Some say that to resolve celestial anomalies and restore harmony, the highest course is to cultivate virtue, the next is to cultivate governance, the next is to cultivate relief measures, and the next is to cultivate exorcistic prayers. Is there validity to this view?

Our August Emperor reveres Heaven, remaining diligent and vigilant from morning to night. Recently He inscribed twelve precepts beside His throne for constant contemplation and self-examination, leaving nothing further that needs to be said. Lately, on account of a stellar anomaly, He immediately grew alarmed and strove with heightened vigor, selecting court officials and subjecting them to strict regulations, while all the bureaucracy was filled with trepidation, scarcely having enough time to reflect upon their faults. Although one knows…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天心仁愛之至而臣子無已之心猶有所願效
者諸士計必蓄於衷願詳言之吾將以
聞于
上
問語計安者非禦夷則弭盜夫夷狄非我
族類其有時爲梗不足怪者盜吾人也
人情莫不樂生而獨試其身于盜毋亦
有以驅之者耶說者謂盜有源然耶東
粵阻山濱海地廣邊夷又其民呰窳偷
===
生多盜邇荷
聖天子神武當事者經略山海之間足稱蕩平
然境內汰兵異省亡命往往窺伺其間
盜固滋有也他則澳夷結落隱然敵形
珠販連檣公肆剽掠瓊崖黎岐雖別生
也然十字之議未行桑土者憂焉羅旁
徭浪雖戡定也然漏刃之孽未殲衣袽
者戒焉吾慮廣之銷兵無日也夫廣用
兵有年矣剝閭閻實行伍以至筭及雞
punctuated:
天心仁愛之至，而臣子無已之心猶有所願效者，諸士計必蓄於衷，願詳言之，吾將以聞于上。

問：語計安者，非禦夷則弭盜。夫夷狄非我族類，其有時爲梗，不足怪者。盜，吾人也。人情莫不樂生，而獨試其身于盜，毋亦有以驅之者耶？說者謂盜有源，然耶？東粵阻山濱海，地廣邊夷，又其民呰窳偷生，多盜。邇荷聖天子神武，當事者經略山海之間，足稱蕩平。然境內汰兵、異省亡命，往往窺伺其間，盜固滋有也。他則澳夷結落，隱然敵形；珠販連檣，公肆剽掠；瓊、崖黎、岐，雖別生也，然十字之議未行，桑土者憂焉；羅旁徭、浪，雖戡定也，然漏刃之孽未殲，衣袽者戒焉。吾慮廣之銷兵無日也。夫廣用兵有年矣，剝閭閻，實行伍，以至筭及雞
translation_en:
… the utmost benevolence of Heaven's mind, yet the boundless devotion of ministers and subjects still has something it wishes to offer. You gentlemen must certainly have harbored plans in your hearts; I wish you to speak of them in detail, as I shall report them to the Emperor.

Question: Those who speak of plans for securing peace focus either on defending against foreign tribes or on suppressing bandits. Now, the foreign tribes are not of our kind, so that they sometimes cause obstruction is not to be wondered at. Bandits, however, are our own people. In human sentiment there is no one who does not take pleasure in life, yet if they alone risk their lives in banditry, is it not that there is something driving them to it? Commentators say that banditry has a source; is that so? Eastern Yue [Guangdong] is hemmed in by mountains and borders the sea; its territory is vast and adjoins foreign peoples, and moreover its people are indolent, living from moment to moment, and many become bandits. Recently, thanks to the divine martial prowess of the Sacred Son of Heaven, those in authority have managed campaigns between the mountains and the sea, which suffices to be called a sweeping pacification. Yet within the borders, dismissed soldiers and fugitives from other provinces often lurk and watch for opportunities in their midst, so bandits certainly continue to proliferate. As for other matters: the foreigners at Macao (Aoyi) have established settlements, secretly taking on the aspect of an enemy; pearl traffickers link their masts and openly engage in plundering; although the Li and Qi peoples of Qiongzhou and Yazhou are differentiated into tame and wild [or: are of a distinct race], the proposal for intersecting cross-roads through their territory has not yet been carried out, and those who prepare ahead ("mulberry roots") worry about them; although the Yao and Lang peoples of Luopang have been suppressed and pacified, the wicked remnants who escaped the blade have not yet been annihilated, and those who take precautions ("rag-stuffing for leaks") remain on guard against them. I fear there will never be a day when Guangdong can lay down its arms. Now, Guangdong has employed troops for years. It has fleeced the common people in the villages to fill the military ranks, to the point of levying taxes even on chickens…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
豚民財詘矣議兵則民無以堪去兵則
盜無由息今其計將安出歟抑别有調
停均節之術可以禦夷弭盜而亦不重
為民病者歟諸士為桑梓慨中必有上
策願悉以對
punctuated: 豚，民財詘矣。議兵則民無以堪，去兵則盜無由息，今其計將安出歟？抑别有調停均節之術，可以禦夷弭盜，而亦不重為民病者歟？諸士為桑梓慨，中必有上策，願悉以對。
translation_en: …pigs, and the people's wealth has been exhausted. If we deliberate on maintaining troops, the people cannot bear the burden; if we disband the troops, there will be no way to quell the bandits. From where, then, shall a plan be devised today? Or is there some other method of accommodation and balanced regulation that can both defend against the foreign barbarians and suppress the bandits without imposing a heavy affliction upon the people? You gentlemen, feeling deeply for your native land, must hold superior strategies in your hearts; I hope you will set them forth in full in your replies.

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人七十五名
第一名吳國光新安縣學生易
第二名黃淳博羅縣學增廣生詩
第三名黃希奭潮州府學生書
第四名劉堯佐廣州府學生春秋
第五名蒙而鎡三水縣學附學生禮記
第六名牛大緯瓊州府學生詩
第七名陳建中廣州府學附學生易
===
第八名歐陽勁從化縣學生詩
第九名潘湛廣州府學生易
第十名甘守正南海縣學附學生易

第十五名梁為熹順德縣學增廣生易
第十六名陳紹虞惠州府學生書
punctuated:

第八名，歐陽勁，從化縣學生，《詩》。
第九名，潘湛，廣州府學生，《易》。
第十名，甘守正，南海縣學附學生，《易》。
第十一名，鄺堯齡，南海縣學生，《易》。
第十二名，陳見龍，潮陽縣學附學生，《詩》。
第十三名，何維翰，順德縣儒士，《易》。
第十四名，何兆湖，廣州府學增廣生，《禮記》。
第十五名，梁為熹，順德縣學增廣生，《易》。

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
衞公孫朝問於子貢曰仲尼焉學子貢曰
文武之道未墜於地在人賢者識其大
者不賢者識其小者莫不有文武之道
焉夫子焉不學而亦何常師之有
吳國光
同考試官教諭侯批體裁純正思致精確發
夫子何常師處透徹可式
===
同考試官學正趙批聖學師道道無不在則
師亦無常是作發揮精徹獨得本旨宜錄以式
考試官訓導唐批平正通達
考試官教諭鄭批雋雅
大夫究聖人之學而賢者明其無專學焉夫聖
道恒寄于人也無人非道則無人非學矣孰謂
仲尼有常師哉且夫帝王之道備于文武文武
之道集于仲尼則謂仲尼學文武可也謂其師
文武亦可也何公孫朝以仲尼焉學問焉將謂
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「衞公孫朝問於子貢曰：『仲尼焉學？』子貢曰：『文、武之道，未墜於地，在人。賢者識其大者，不賢者識其小者，莫不有文、武之道焉。夫子焉不學？而亦何常師之有？』」
吳國光
同考試官教諭侯批：體裁純正，思致精確，發「夫子何常師」處透徹，可式。
同考試官學正趙批：聖學師道，道無不在，則師亦無常。是作發揮精徹，獨得本旨，宜錄以式。
考試官訓導唐批：平正通達。
考試官教諭鄭批：雋雅。
大夫究聖人之學，而賢者明其無專學焉。夫聖道恒寄于人也，無人非道，則無人非學矣，孰謂仲尼有常師哉？且夫帝王之道備于文、武，文、武之道集于仲尼，則謂仲尼學文、武可也，謂其師文、武亦可也。何公孫朝以「仲尼焉學」問焉？將謂…
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
"Gongsun Chao of Wei asked Zigong, 'From whom did Zhongni [Confucius] learn?' Zigong said, 'The Way of Kings Wen and Wu has not fallen to the ground; it lives on in people. The worthy remember its greater aspects, and the unworthy remember its smaller aspects. None lacks the Way of Wen and Wu. From whom, then, did the Master not learn? And yet what regular teacher did he have?'" [Analects 19.22]
Wu Guoguang 吳國光
Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies (jiaoyu) Hou 侯: The literary form is pure and upright, and the train of thought is precise and accurate. Its exposition of the passage "what regular teacher did the Master have" is penetrating and worthy of serving as a model.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Zhao 趙: Sage learning takes the Way as its teacher; since the Way is omnipresent, the teacher is likewise not fixed. This essay develops the theme with penetrating precision and uniquely grasps the fundamental purport; it ought to be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Assistant Director of Studies (xundao) Tang 唐: Balanced, proper, and lucid.
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies (jiaoyu) Zheng 鄭:Incisive and elegant.
A grand officer inquired into the learning of the Sage, and a worthy made clear that his learning had no single exclusive source. Now, the Way of the Sages constantly resides in people. Since there is no person without the Way, there is no person from whom one cannot learn; who, then, could say that Zhongni had a regular teacher? Moreover, the Way of the sovereign emperors and kings was brought to completion in Kings Wen and Wu, and the Way of Wen and Wu was synthesized in Zhongni. Thus, one may rightly say that Zhongni learned from Wen and Wu, and one may also say that he took Wen and Wu as his teachers. Why, then, did Gongsun Chao ask, "From whom did Zhongni learn?" Was he about to say…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其有常學乎亦將謂其有常師乎子貢迺告之
曰子疑夫子之焉學哉亦未知其得統于文武
耳蓋文武生而道在文武文武往而道在後人
道有大者人之賢者則識之謨烈之重光固奕
世之紹述也而賢者有斯道焉是道在賢者而
未墜矣道有小者人之不賢者則識之經制之
緒餘固後人之誦法也而不賢者有斯道焉是
道在不賢而未墜矣吾夫子于賢者學之學道
之大也而又不遺其小則賢其師而不專于賢
===
也于不賢者學之學道之小也而又盡其大則
不賢其師而不專于不賢也道垂啓佑恒得人
以衍其盛而合大小皆聖學之資學切憲章每
因人以繼其傳而隨賢否皆得師之益夫子焉
不學也焉不師也而亦何常之有哉至是而文
武之道在人者又在夫子未墜于地者將昭垂
于萬世也已公孫朝其知之雖然仲尼非徒學
文武也學文武之道將以行之也是故東周之
思與人存政舉之論每惓惓焉其心誠欲使成
punctuated: 其有常學乎？亦將謂其有常師乎？子貢迺告之曰：「子疑夫子之焉學哉？亦未知其得統于文武耳。」蓋文武生而道在文武，文武往而道在後人。道有大者，人之賢者則識之。謨烈之重光，固奕世之紹述也，而賢者有斯道焉，是道在賢者而未墜矣。道有小者，人之不賢者則識之。經制之緒餘，固後人之誦法也，而不賢者有斯道焉，是道在不賢而未墜矣。吾夫子于賢者學之，學道之大也，而又不遺其小，則賢其師而不專于賢也；于不賢者學之，學道之小也，而又盡其大，則不賢其師而不專于不賢也。道垂啓佑，恒得人以衍其盛，而合大小皆聖學之資；學切憲章，每因人以繼其傳，而隨賢否皆得師之益。夫子焉不學也，焉不師也，而亦何常之有哉？至是而文武之道在人者，又在夫子；未墜于地者，將昭垂于萬世也已。公孫朝其知之！雖然，仲尼非徒學文武也，學文武之道將以行之也。是故東周之思，與「人存政舉」之論，每惓惓焉，其心誠欲使成
translation_en: …that he had a fixed subject of study, or that he had a regular teacher? Zigong 子貢 then told him: "Do you wonder from whom the Master learned? You simply do not realize that he received the succession from King Wen 文 and King Wu 武." Indeed, while Wen and Wu were alive, the Way resided in Wen and Wu; once Wen and Wu passed away, the Way resided in later generations. In the Way there is that which is great, and men of worth remember it. The renewed splendor of their counsels and achievements was surely transmitted across successive generations, and since men of worth possessed this Way, the Way resided in the worthy and had not yet fallen to the ground. In the Way there is that which is small, and those who are not of great worth remember it. The remnants of their institutions and regulations were surely recited and modeled upon by later men, and since those not of great worth possessed this Way, the Way resided in the unworthy and had not yet fallen to the ground. When our Master learned from men of worth, he learned the great aspects of the Way, yet he did not neglect the small; thus the worthy were his teachers, though he did not restrict himself solely to the worthy. When he learned from those not of great worth, he learned the small aspects of the Way, yet he also exhausted the great; thus the unworthy were his teachers, though he did not restrict himself solely to the unworthy. Passed down to enlighten and aid posterity, the Way always finds men to extend its flourishing, so that great and small together serve as resources for sage learning; earnest in modeling himself on the ancient kings, his learning always relied on people to continue the transmission, so that whether worthy or not, all yielded the benefit of a teacher. Where did the Master not learn, and whom did he not take as a teacher? What regular teacher could he have had? At that point, the Way of Wen and Wu that had resided in others came to reside in the Master, and that which had not fallen to the ground would shine forth for ten thousand generations. May Gongsun Chao 公孫朝 understand this! Even so, Zhongni 仲尼 did not merely study Wen and Wu; he studied the Way of Wen and Wu in order to put it into practice. Therefore, in his thoughts of making an Eastern Zhou and in his discourse on how "when the right men are present, government flourishes," he was ever earnestly devoted, for in his heart he truly wished to cause…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
棣之詩爲宜家而發也言妻子之合而有鼓瑟
琴之和言兄弟之翕而有樂且耽之美室家之
宜妻帑之樂胥此矣是詩也特妻子兄弟之詠
而未及於父母也乃夫子則謂其父母之可順
焉何哉蓋妻子兄弟之身未始不與父母相聯
屬則父母之心亦未始不與妻子兄弟相流通
者也玆惟道隆于家而一家之恩義旣交孚而
罔間則心通于親而一念之豫順自浹洽而無
違好合妻子之心也亦父母之心也而和於妻
===
子者不可必其和於父母乎允若之化固自其
刑于者基之矣旣翕兄弟之願也亦父母之願
也而宜於兄弟者不可必其宜於父母乎底豫
之風固自其友于者始之矣然則詩人所詠其
㫖深哉吁君子觀道於妻子兄弟而思順親之
化又觀道於父母而思聚順之原則道之行遠
自邇登高自卑也此其一徵矣乎雖然宜家之
驗非止順親已也推而極之雖天下之順亦不
外此蓋化行自近而正家固正天下之本也甞
punctuated: 棣》之詩，爲宜家而發也。言妻子之合，而有「鼓瑟琴」之和；言兄弟之翕，而有「樂且耽」之美。「室家之宜」、「妻帑之樂」，胥此矣。是詩也，特妻子兄弟之詠，而未及於父母也。乃夫子則謂其父母之可順焉，何哉？蓋妻子兄弟之身，未始不與父母相聯屬；則父母之心，亦未始不與妻子兄弟相流通者也。玆惟道隆于家，而一家之恩義旣交孚而罔間；則心通于親，而一念之豫順自浹洽而無違。好合，妻子之心也，亦父母之心也；而和於妻子者，不可必其和於父母乎？允若之化，固自其刑于者基之矣。旣翕，兄弟之願也，亦父母之願也；而宜於兄弟者，不可必其宜於父母乎？底豫之風，固自其友于者始之矣。然則詩人所詠，其㫖深哉！吁！君子觀道於妻子兄弟，而思順親之化；又觀道於父母，而思聚順之原。則道之「行遠自邇，登高自卑」也，此其一徵矣乎！雖然，宜家之驗，非止順親已也；推而極之，雖天下之順，亦不外此。蓋化行自近，而正家固正天下之本也。甞
translation_en: …The ode ["Changdi" ("The Cherry Tree") in the Book of Odes] was composed to express bringing harmony to the family. It speaks of loving union with wife and children, having the harmony of "strumming zithers and lutes"; it speaks of the concord of brothers, having the beauty of "rejoicing and delighting." "Ordering well one's household" and "giving joy to wife and children" all lie herein. This ode is merely a song about wife, children, and brothers, without yet mentioning parents. Why, then, did the Master say of it that parents will thereby be in accord and at ease? It is because the persons of wife, children, and brothers have never failed to be bound together with the parents; thus, the hearts of the parents have likewise never failed to flow in mutual communion with wife, children, and brothers. Here, only when the Way flourishes within the family, and the affection and righteousness of the whole household are already mutually trusted without rift, will the heart communicate with the parents, and every thought of joyful accord will naturally be pervasive and without disharmony. Loving union is the heart's desire of wife and children, and it is also the heart's desire of parents; when one is harmonious with wife and children, can one not be assured of being harmonious with parents? The transformation of sincere compliance is indeed founded upon setting an example for one's wife. Concord is the wish of brothers, and it is also the wish of parents; when one is on good terms with one's brothers, can one not be assured of being on good terms with parents? The custom of bringing parents to delight indeed begins with brotherly affection. If this is so, then how profound is the purport of what the poet sang! Ah! When the gentleman observes the Way in wife, children, and brothers, and contemplates the transformation that brings accord to parents; and when he further observes the Way in parents, and contemplates the source of gathered harmony—is this not one proof that the Way "in traveling far, starts from the near; in ascending high, starts from the low"? Even so, the efficacy of regulating the family does not stop merely at bringing accord to parents; if extended to its utmost, even the accord of the whole empire does not lie outside this. For moral transformation proceeds from what is near, and rectifying the family is truly the root of rectifying the empire. Once, when…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
讀詩至文王之化御于家邦而必本諸刑于其
義不亦深切著明矣乎有家國天下之責者當
自得之
士之仕也猶農夫之耕也農夫豈為出疆
舍其耒耜哉
陳見龍
同考試官教諭李批發揮載質意親切且體
格醇正思致俊拔佳士也取之
同考試官教諭梁批是題口氣最難體貼而
平正冠冕卓爾大雅獨見此作取之
考試官訓導唐批典雅純粹
考試官教諭鄭批典確
===
士必載質而出例之農可知也夫士必仕載質
所以仕也不然是農夫而舍耒耜矣可乎哉孟
子例言以曉周霄者意曰君子之在天下謂道
不可以不行故身在必出謂身不容以苟就故
進必以禮子疑士之載質也亦即農夫觀之乎
蓋士謀道者也以道為志則得之不忍私其身
punctuated:
讀《詩》至文王之化「御于家邦」，而必本諸「刑于」，其義不亦深切著明矣乎？有家國天下之責者，當自得之。

「士之仕也，猶農夫之耕也；農夫豈為出疆舍其耒耜哉？」
陳見龍
同考試官教諭李批：發揮「載質」意親切，且體格醇正，思致俊拔，佳士也，取之。
同考試官教諭梁批：是題口氣最難體貼，而平正冠冕，卓爾大雅，獨見此作，取之。
考試官訓導唐批：典雅純粹。
考試官教諭鄭批：典確。

士必載質而出，例之農可知也。夫士必仕，載質所以仕也；不然，是農夫而舍耒耜矣，可乎哉？孟子例言以曉周霄者，意曰：「君子之在天下，謂道不可以不行，故身在必出；謂身不容以苟就，故進必以禮。子疑士之載質也，亦即農夫觀之乎？蓋士，謀道者也。以道為志，則得之不忍私其身，
translation_en:
… reading the Book of Odes (Shi) up to how King Wen's moral transformation "governed family and state," and seeing that it necessarily took "setting an example for his wife" as its root, is not its meaning deep, incisive, and brilliantly clear? Those who bear responsibility for family, state, and All under Heaven ought to grasp this for themselves.

"A scholar's taking office is like a farmer's plowing; does a farmer abandon his plowshare and handle just because he crosses the frontier?" [Mencius 3B.3]
By Chen Jianlong 陳見龍.
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Li's comment: He develops the meaning of "carrying ceremonial gifts" intimately and incisively; moreover, the style and structure are pure and upright, and the train of thought is outstanding and elevated. A fine scholar—select it!
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Liang's comment: The rhetorical tone of this topic is most difficult to capture empathetically, yet an essay that is balanced, upright, dignified, and surpassingly refined in high elegance is seen uniquely in this composition—select it!
Examiner and Assistant Director of Studies Tang's comment: Classically elegant and unadulterated.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng's comment: Classically grounded and precise.

That a scholar necessarily carries ceremonial gifts when going abroad can be understood by comparing him to a farmer. Now, a scholar must take office, and carrying ceremonial gifts is the means by which he takes office; otherwise, he would be a farmer who abandons his plowshare and handle—how could that be permissible? When Mencius spoke by way of analogy to enlighten Zhou Xiao 周霄, his meaning was as follows: "When the gentleman is in the world, he holds that the Way cannot go unpracticed, and therefore, as long as he is alive, he must go forth; he holds that his person cannot be compromised by casually accepting a post, and therefore his advancement must be in accordance with ritual propriety. You doubt a scholar's carrying ceremonial gifts; why not examine it by looking at the farmer? For the scholar is one who plans for the Way. Taking the Way as his aspiration, once he attains it he cannot bear to keep his person to himself, …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而皇皇然思以應廟廊之求者其心也固無論
其出疆與否而皆然也猶之農夫謀食者也以
食爲念則求之無敢愛其力而汲汲然思以盡
畒畝之務者其心也亦無論其出疆與否而皆
然也然士欲仕而仕之禮質是已農欲耕而耕
之具耒耜是已使農之耒耜可以出疆舍則士
之質亦可以無載也孰知農夫之出既不擇地
而耕則耒耜之用豈爲出疆而舍百畝之不易
彼誠憂之則凡所以爲明農計者必有身出而
===
器與之俱矣况士將委質人國者而可一日廢
先資之信哉百穀之未播彼誠念之則凡所以
爲力穡謀者必有身往而器與之偕矣况士將
傳質爲臣者而可一日廢見君之禮哉蓋良農
能耕不能使耕之舍乎耒耜彼舍焉者不欲耕
者也非農之常也君子能仕不能使仕之不載
乎質彼不載焉者不欲仕者也非士之常也知
乎此而君子之載質可無疑矣噫孟氏之梁之
齊出疆者數矣而卒不合豈獨無質哉非堯舜
punctuated: 而皇皇然思以應廟廊之求者，其心也，固無論其出疆與否而皆然也。猶之農夫，謀食者也。以食爲念，則求之無敢愛其力，而汲汲然思以盡畒畝之務者，其心也，亦無論其出疆與否而皆然也。然士欲仕，而仕之禮，質是已；農欲耕，而耕之具，耒耜是已。使農之耒耜可以出疆舍，則士之質亦可以無載也。孰知農夫之出，既不擇地而耕，則耒耜之用，豈爲出疆而舍？百畝之不易，彼誠憂之，則凡所以爲明農計者，必有身出而器與之俱矣。况士將委質人國者，而可一日廢先資之信哉？百穀之未播，彼誠念之，則凡所以爲力穡謀者，必有身往而器與之偕矣。况士將傳質爲臣者，而可一日廢見君之禮哉？蓋良農能耕，不能使耕之舍乎耒耜，彼舍焉者，不欲耕者也，非農之常也。君子能仕，不能使仕之不載乎質，彼不載焉者，不欲仕者也，非士之常也。知乎此，而君子之載質可無疑矣。噫！孟氏之梁、之齊，出疆者數矣，而卒不合，豈獨無質哉？非堯、舜
translation_en: …and anxiously seeks to answer the call of the court—such is his heart, and it is certainly so regardless of whether he crosses the border or not. It is just like the farmer, who is one that plans for food. Taking food as his concern, in seeking it he does not dare spare his strength, and eagerly seeks to fulfill the duties of the fields—such is his heart, and it too is so regardless of whether he crosses the border or not. Now, the scholar wishes to serve in office, and the ritual of serving is the introductory gift (zhi); the farmer wishes to plow, and the implements of plowing are the plowhandle and plowshare (leisi). If the farmer's plowhandle and plowshare could be left behind upon crossing a border, then the scholar's introductory gift could likewise go uncarried. Who does not know that since a farmer, upon going out, does not pick and choose the land before plowing, how could the use of his plowhandle and plowshare be abandoned merely because he crosses a border? If he truly worries that the hundred mu of land are not properly cultivated, then in all his plans for husbandry, whenever he goes forth in person, his tools must surely go with him. How much more so for a scholar who is about to pledge his introductory gift to another state—could he for a single day dispense with the token of good faith presented in advance? If the farmer truly bears in mind that the hundred grains are not yet sown, then in all his counsels for diligent farming, whenever he goes forth in person, his tools must surely accompany him. How much more so for a scholar who is about to pass in his introductory gift to become a minister—could he for a single day dispense with the ritual for having an audience with a ruler? Indeed, a good farmer is able to plow, but cannot make plowing dispense with the plowhandle and plowshare; one who leaves them behind is someone who does not wish to plow, which is not the constant way of the farmer. A gentleman is able to serve in office, but cannot make serving dispense with carrying an introductory gift; one who does not carry it is someone who does not wish to serve, which is not the constant way of the scholar. Once one understands this, there need be no doubt about the gentleman's carrying an introductory gift. Alas! Mencius went to Liang and went to Qi, crossing borders several times, yet in the end he did not find a match—was it because he alone lacked an introductory gift? Anything other than the way of Yao and Shun…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之道不陳非仁義之猷不言是孟氏之質也吾
能載質以待用而不能必人之我用用不用人
也孟氏則俟之而已胡肯以輕售也噫是又孔
氏家法也
易
君子黃中通理正位居體
吳國光
同考試官學正趙批場中發中順類多支蔓
子能刋落陳言直攄心蘊深于易者錄之
===
同考試官教諭李批剀調追雅不厭咀嚼
考試官訓導唐批潔淨
考試官教諭鄭批純正
文言著君子中順之德所以釋黃裳之義也夫
黃中而通理中也正位而居體順也合而觀之
黃裳之義明矣甞謂人君之所貴者德而君德
之所貴者則有要也六五之所以取象于黃裳
者何哉吾有以觀其深矣彼人君以一人而建
極于上其德尚中自夫或失則偏非中也非可
punctuated:
之道不陳，非仁義之猷不言，是孟氏之質也。吾能載質以待用，而不能必人之我用；用不用，人也，孟氏則俟之而已，胡肯以輕售也？噫！是又孔氏家法也。

《易》
「君子黃中通理，正位居體。」
吳國光
同考試官學正趙批：場中發中順，類多支蔓。子能刋落陳言，直攄心蘊，深于《易》者。錄之。
同考試官教諭李批：剀調追雅，不厭咀嚼。
考試官訓導唐批：潔淨。
考試官教諭鄭批：純正。

《文言》著君子中順之德，所以釋「黃裳」之義也。夫黃中而通理，中也；正位而居體，順也。合而觀之，「黃裳」之義明矣。甞謂人君之所貴者德，而君德之所貴者則有要也。六五之所以取象于「黃裳」者何哉？吾有以觀其深矣。彼人君以一人而建極于上，其德尚中。自夫或失則偏，非中也，非可
translation_en:
… the Way [of Yao and Shun], he would not set it forth; if it was not the plan of benevolence and righteousness, he would not speak of it—this was Mencius's introductory gift. I can carry my introductory gift and await employment, yet I cannot guarantee that others will employ me. Whether I am employed or not depends on others; Mencius simply waited for it—how would he be willing to sell himself lightly? Alas! This too was the family tradition of Confucius.

Book of Changes (Yi)
"The superior man is yellow and central, penetrating the principles; he is in the correct position and abides in the body."
Wu Guoguang 吳國光
Comment by Associate Examiner Department Director of Schools Zhao 趙: In the examination hall, those who expounded upon centrality and docility were mostly diffuse andrambling. You were able to pare away worn-out clichés and directly express the inner depths of the mind—one who is profound in the Book of Changes. Recorded.
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Schools Li 李: Incisive and harmonious, pursuing elegance; one never tires of savoring it.
Comment by Examiner Assistant Director of Schools Tang 唐: Pure and clean.
Comment by Examiner County Director of Schools Zheng 鄭: Pure and correct.

The "Words of the Text" (Wenyan) manifests the superior man's virtue of centrality and docility, thereby explaining the meaning of the "yellow lower garment." Now, to be yellow inside and penetrate the principles is centrality; to be in the correct position and abide in the body is docility. Viewed together, the meaning of the "yellow lower garment" becomes clear. I have held that what a ruler values is virtue, and what is valued in a ruler's virtue has its essentials. Why is it that the Six in the Fifth place takes its image from the "yellow lower garment"? I have been able to observe its profundity. title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以語黃也惟君子則精一之功以純而德之在
內者立天下之大中焉語中之統體則萬理貫
徹而不遺何若是其通也語中之散殊則脉絡
分明而不亂何若是其理也合之大而析之精
而天然自有之妙會于君子之心矣是故以中
德而象於黃也謂其色之中也人君以一人而
正位于上其德尚順自夫或失則戾非順也非
可以語裳也惟君子則謙遜之衷恒存而位之
所居者布天下之大順焉貴為天子而虛其心
===
以禮天下之士待臣之體則然也尊為元后而
抑其心以下天下之人待民之體則然也位愈
高而德愈下而柔嘉巽順之懿達于君子之身
矣是故以順德而象于裳也謂其飾之下也要
之中存于內立其體也而實為順之基順見于
外達其用也而實為中之驗觀此而黃裳之義
寧有餘蘊哉愚甞仰稽于古譚治道之盛者莫
過于堯舜君德之盛亦莫過于堯舜也二典所
稱曰允執厥中曰溫恭克讓夫非中順主哉而
punctuated: 以語黃也。惟君子則精一之功以純，而德之在內者，立天下之大中焉。語中之統體，則萬理貫徹而不遺，何若是其通也？語中之散殊，則脉絡分明而不亂，何若是其理也？合之大而析之精，而天然自有之妙，會于君子之心矣。是故以中德而象於黃也，謂其色之中也。人君以一人而正位于上，其德尚順。自夫或失則戾，非順也，非可以語裳也。惟君子則謙遜之衷恒存，而位之所居者，布天下之大順焉。貴為天子，而虛其心以禮天下之士，待臣之體則然也；尊為元后，而抑其心以下天下之人，待民之體則然也。位愈高而德愈下，而柔嘉巽順之懿，達于君子之身矣。是故以順德而象于裳也，謂其飾之下也。要之，中存于內，立其體也，而實為順之基；順見于外，達其用也，而實為中之驗。觀此，而黃裳之義寧有餘蘊哉？愚甞仰稽于古，譚治道之盛者，莫過于堯、舜，君德之盛，亦莫過于堯、舜也。二典所稱，曰「允執厥中」，曰「溫恭克讓」，夫非中順主哉？而
translation_en:
… speak of “yellow.” Only in the noble man is the effort of refinement and single-mindedness made pure, so that the virtue residing within establishes the great centrality of all under heaven. Speaking of centrality in its unified totality, the myriad principles penetrate throughout without omission—how is it so comprehending? Speaking of centrality in its dispersed particulars, its veins and threads are distinct and unconfused—how is it so well-ordered? Vast when combined and subtle when analyzed, its naturally inherent marvel converges in the mind of the noble man. Therefore, central virtue is symbolized by yellow, referring to the centrality of that color.

When a ruler, as one man, occupies the correct position above, his virtue prizes compliance. Once he errs, he becomes perverse; that is not compliance, and one cannot speak of the “lower garment.” Only in the noble man is an inner heart of humility and deference constantly preserved, so that the position he occupies spreads great compliance throughout all under heaven. Though noble as the Son of Heaven, he empties his mind to treat the scholars of the world with ritual courtesy—such is the proper form for treating ministers. Though exalted as the sovereign ruler, he restrains his mind to humble himself before the people of the world—such is the proper form for treating the people. The higher his position, the lowlier his virtue, and the excellence of gentle goodness and humble compliance is realized in the person of the noble man. Therefore, compliant virtue is symbolized by the lower garment, referring to the lowliness of that attire.

In sum, centrality abides within to establish the substance, and truly serves as the foundation of compliance; compliance is manifest without to extend the function, and truly serves as the verification of centrality. Looking at it this way, how could there be any remaining hidden meaning in the significance of the “yellow lower garment”?

I have looked up to examine antiquity: those who discuss the flourishing of the way of governance find none surpassing Yao and Shun, and in the flourishing of ruler’s virtue, too, none surpasses Yao and Shun. What the two Canons praise—saying “sincerely hold fast the Mean,” and saying “mild, reverent, and able to yield”—were they not masters of centrality and compliance? And when one …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
窺其原則兢兢業業爲之也然則欲全中順之
德可無主敬之心乎故曰敬者聖學之所以成
始而成終也
言行君子之樞機樞機之發榮辱之主也
陳建中
同考試官敎諭李批樞機二字講多未融是
篇精暢古雅不羣經義之佳者
考試官訓導唐批精緻
考試官敎諭鄭批瑩潤
===
大傳喻言行之切於人而明其所係之重焉夫
善否不同而榮辱因之是所係固甚重也君子
於言行其可苟焉而已哉大傳什中孚九二爻
義如此今夫中孚之理妙於感通而感通之要
存乎言行人之忽於言行而不加擬議之功者
亦未審其所係之何如耳彼樞運而戶斯闢機
動而矢斯隨言天下之至速者莫踰於此矣今
言出乎身卽加乎民觸則必應若有所轉移於
其間是言焉一樞機也行發乎邇卽見乎遠感
punctuated:
窺其原則兢兢業業爲之也。然則欲全中順之德，可無主敬之心乎？故曰：「敬者，聖學之所以成始而成終也。」

「言行，君子之樞機；樞機之發，榮辱之主也。」
陳建中
同考試官敎諭李批：樞機二字，講多未融，是篇精暢古雅不羣，經義之佳者。
考試官訓導唐批：精緻。
考試官敎諭鄭批：瑩潤。

大傳喻言行之切於人，而明其所係之重焉。夫善否不同而榮辱因之，是所係固甚重也，君子於言行，其可苟焉而已哉？大傳什《中孚》九二爻義如此。今夫中孚之理，妙於感通，而感通之要，存乎言行。人之忽於言行，而不加擬議之功者，亦未審其所係之何如耳。彼樞運而戶斯闢，機動而矢斯隨，言天下之至速者，莫踰於此矣。今言出乎身，卽加乎民，觸則必應，若有所轉移於其間，是言焉一樞機也；行發乎邇，卽見乎遠，感
translation_en:
…if one peers into their source, it is done through cautiousness and diligence. This being so, if one wishes to perfect the virtues of centrality and compliance, how could one lack a mind that holds fast to reverence? Therefore it is said: "Reverence is that whereby the learning of the sages completes both beginning and end."

"Words and deeds are the pivot and trigger of the superior man; the release of the pivot and trigger is the master of glory and disgrace."
By Chen Jianzhong 陳建中.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li: In explaining the two characters "pivot and trigger" (shuji), most candidates fail to achieve a thorough synthesis. This essay is refined, fluent, classically elegant, and extraordinary—an excellent piece among the Classics essays.
Comment by Examiner Assistant Instructor Tang: Refined and meticulous.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zheng: Lustrous and polished.

The Great Commentary (Dazhuan) uses a metaphor to show how intimately words and deeds concern a person, and clarifies the gravity of what depends on them. Now, because good and bad differ, glory and disgrace follow accordingly; what depends on them is indeed most weighty. How could the superior man be merely careless in his words and deeds? Such is the Great Commentary's explanation [?] of the meaning of the second line (Nine in the Second Place) of the hexagram Inner Trust (Zhongfu 中孚). Now, the principle of Inner Trust has its subtlety in sympathetic resonance and communication, and the essential point of sympathetic resonance and communication lies in words and deeds. When people neglect their words and deeds and do not apply the effort of deliberation and discussion to them, it is simply because they have not examined what depends upon them. When that pivot turns, the door thereupon opens; when the trigger moves, the arrow thereupon follows—speaking of the swiftest things in the world, nothing surpasses these. Now, when words go forth from one's person, they immediately affect the people; where they touch, there is surely a response, as though something were shifting them from within—thus words are a pivot and trigger. When deeds are initiated near at hand, they immediately become visible afar; where they stir…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則必孚若有所斡旋於其內是行焉一樞機也
樞機之發所係豈其微哉自其應之於千里之
外也言而民信行而民悅何榮也顧榮非自榮
而樞機之善實爲榮之主焉善爲主則榮爲應
人情莫不欲榮也而孰知主是榮者之有所在
乎自其違之於千里之外也令之而不從推之
而不協何辱也顧辱非自辱而樞機之不善實
爲辱之主焉不善爲主則辱爲應人情莫不惡
辱也而孰知主是辱者之有所存乎夫樞機爲
===
榮之主是榮固自已求之也樞機爲辱之主是
辱亦自已求之也觀其所主而擬議以致其慎
者信乎其不容緩矣雖然慎之之功非可以襲
取焉也古之君子豫養於暗室屋漏之中不動
而敬不言而信故孚誠所積而潛通默喻捷於
響桴若養之不豫直取一言一動而矯飾之乃
曰吾將如是而化邦如是而格豚魚也亦繆於
中孚之旨矣
書
punctuated:
則必孚，若有所斡旋於其內，是行焉一樞機也。樞機之發，所係豈其微哉！自其應之於千里之外也，言而民信，行而民悅，何榮也！顧榮非自榮，而樞機之善實爲榮之主焉。善爲主，則榮爲應；人情莫不欲榮也，而孰知主是榮者之有所在乎？自其違之於千里之外也，令之而不從，推之而不協，何辱也！顧辱非自辱，而樞機之不善實爲辱之主焉。不善爲主，則辱爲應；人情莫不惡辱也，而孰知主是辱者之有所存乎？夫樞機爲榮之主，是榮固自已求之也；樞機爲辱之主，是辱亦自已求之也。觀其所主，而擬議以致其慎者，信乎其不容緩矣。雖然，慎之之功，非可以襲取焉也。古之君子，豫養於暗室屋漏之中，不動而敬，不言而信，故孚誠所積，而潛通默喻，捷於響桴。若養之不豫，直取一言一動而矯飾之，乃曰：「吾將如是而化邦，如是而格豚魚也。」亦繆於中孚之旨矣。
書
translation_en:
… then it will certainly inspire trust, as if something were turning and operating within it; thus action is a pivot and trigger. When the pivot and trigger are set in motion, how could what depends upon them be slight! From the fact that they meet with response a thousand miles away—when one speaks, the people believe; when one acts, the people rejoice—what honor that is! Yet honor does not come of itself; the goodness of the pivot and trigger is truly the master of honor. When goodness is the master, honor is the response. In human feeling there is no one who does not desire honor, yet who realizes that what masters this honor has a place where it resides? From the fact that they meet with opposition a thousand miles away—when one commands them, they do not obey; when one extends policies to them, they do not harmonize—what disgrace that is! Yet disgrace does not come of itself; the lack of goodness in the pivot and trigger is truly the master of disgrace. When lack of goodness is the master, disgrace is the response. In human feeling there is no one who does not detest disgrace, yet who realizes that what masters this disgrace has a place where it abides? Now, since the pivot and trigger are the master of honor, this honor is surely sought by oneself; since the pivot and trigger are the master of disgrace, this disgrace is likewise sought by oneself. Observing what they master, and deliberating and discussing in order to exercise the utmost caution—truly this brooks no delay! Even so, the effort of exercising caution cannot be seized through mere outward imitation. The noble men of antiquity cultivated themselves beforehand in the privacy of the dark chamber and the northwest corner of the house; without moving, they were reverent, and without speaking, they were trustworthy. Therefore, through the accumulation of sincere truthfulness, their unseen communion and silent understanding were swifter than an echo or the stroke of a drumstick. If one does not cultivate oneself beforehand, but merely takes each word and each action and artificially adorns them, saying, "By doing thus I shall transform the state, and by doing thus I shall move even pigs and fishes," this too goes against the meaning of the "Inner Truth" (Zhongfu) hexagram.
