理
御寓以來蓋三論民秀於鄉矣而
督有司
punctuated: 毀質，雕鏤亂眞，師錫鰓鰓焉是懼。乃竊持三術，用探厥蘊：其沉涵道眞、厭飫理奧者，聖學昭也；博大宏衍、周詳通敏者，政體具也；幹以正直、澤之忠厚者，節槩正也。此師錫之所采以告成事、以塞責也。鹿鳴旣歌，多士畢集，乃進而告之曰：「休！爾多士，其尚知聖天子掄才至意乎？天子神聖，嘉與海內賢雋共臻至理。御寓以來，蓋三論民秀於鄉矣，而督有司
translation_en:
…mar the substance, and ornate carving confounds the genuine; I, Shixi, was anxiously fearful of this. I therefore ventured to uphold three criteria with which to fathom their inner depth: where the writing is steeped in the truth of the Way and saturated with the profundities of principle, the sage learning is made manifest; where it is broad, expansive, thorough, and perceptive, the essentials of governance are complete; where its backbone is uprightness and its luster is loyalty and generosity, moral integrity is sound. Such are those whom I, Shixi, have selected in order to report the completion of this task and fulfill my responsibility.

Once the "Luming" ode had been sung and the many scholars had all assembled, I stepped forward and addressed them, saying: "Splendid! You many scholars, do you truly understand the Sacred Son of Heaven's utmost intention in selecting talent? The Son of Heaven is divinely sage and delights in joining with the worthy and eminent throughout the realm to attain ultimate governance together. Since ascending the throne to rule the empire, He has thrice selected the finest of the people in the provinces, while His imperial decrees supervising the authorities…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詔旨視昔有加上體
祖宗心下以端多士之習默焉鼓
舞將用之也爾多士其何以
稱
上意乎夫士窮居草茅坐誦書史
誠願得一見
天子披忠愫或受
===
命爲吏舉平生稍施行之乃至有
顛越所挾持捐若弁髦弗遑
顧學名見道而以文姦才稱
練達而以濟慾事務苛細而
以沽名則〔師錫〕向之三術無
乃三懼乎
聖天子在上雖殊方偏國猶輸忠
punctuated: 詔旨視昔有加，上體祖宗心，下以端多士之習，默焉鼓舞，將用之也。爾多士其何以稱上意乎？夫士窮居草茅，坐誦書史，誠願得一見天子，披忠愫，或受命爲吏，舉平生稍施行之。乃至有顛越所挾持，捐若弁髦，弗遑顧。學名見道，而以文姦；才稱練達，而以濟慾；事務苛細，而以沽名。則〔師錫〕向之三術，無乃三懼乎？聖天子在上，雖殊方偏國，猶輸忠
translation_en:
… imperial edicts have become even more rigorous than in the past—above, embodying the intentions of the dynastic ancestors, and below, rectifying the habits of the many scholars—silently inspiring and encouraging them, as He prepares to employ them. How, then, will you scholars live up to His Majesty's intentions?

When a scholar lives in obscurity among the thatched huts, sitting and reciting the classics and histories, he truly wishes to gain an audience with the Son of Heaven to pour out his loyal devotion, or to receive a commission as an official and put into practice a measure of what he has learned throughout his life. Yet it comes to pass that some overturn the principles they once upheld, casting them aside like a boyhood cap without a second thought. Their learning goes by the name of perceiving the Way, yet is used to gloss over wickedness; their talent is praised as seasoned and capable, yet is used to indulge desires; their handling of affairs is overly harsh and petty, yet is used to fish for fame. Then are not the three paths that I, 〔Shi Xi〕, spoke of earlier in fact three things to be feared?

With the Sage Son of Heaven reigning above, even distant quarters and remote states offer their loyal …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
款歸命
闕下奉
政令惟謹而况多士漸摩
聖澤視齊民不啻百倍視慕化來
者不啻千倍一朝際風雲躡
文陛而立以自附於當世名賢
長者後忍令先資𨺚之一至
===
此哉先民有言上不負天子
下不負所學爾多士習聞之
矣乃稱其不負者何在師錫
不敏竊謂不負其心而已何
者忠信之性固多士所素植
也誠堅忠信之素衷奉不負
之成訓以仰副
punctuated: 款，歸命闕下，奉政令惟謹。而况多士漸摩聖澤，視齊民不啻百倍，視慕化來者不啻千倍；一朝際風雲、躡文陛而立，以自附於當世名賢長者後，忍令先資𨺚之，一至此哉！先民有言：「上不負天子，下不負所學。」爾多士習聞之矣，乃稱其不負者何在？師錫不敏，竊謂不負其心而已。何者？忠信之性，固多士所素植也。誠堅忠信之素衷，奉不負之成訓，以仰副
translation_en: …sincerity, submit their allegiance before the palace gates, and obey the government's decrees with utmost reverence. How much more so for these many scholars, who have been steeped in the imperial grace—more than a hundredfold compared to the common people, and more than a thousandfold compared to those who come drawn by civilizing influence! Once they meet with propitious fortune, ascend the ornate steps of the court, and take their stand to rank themselves behind the eminent worthies and elders of the age, how could they bear to let the writings by which they first commended themselves fall into ruin [?] to such a degree as this? A predecessor had a saying: "Above, do not fail the Son of Heaven; below, do not fail what you have learned." All you scholars have long been familiar with hearing this; yet wherein lies that which matches "not failing"? Unworthy as I, Shixi, am, I venture to say that it is simply a matter of not failing one's own mind. Why is this? Because a nature of loyalty and trustworthiness is indeed what these many scholars have long cultivated. If they truly hold firm to their habitual disposition of loyalty and trustworthiness, and uphold the established precept of "not failing," so as to reverently fulfill…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上側席
盛心而
聖祖設科不爲希寵藉手則豈特
多士之休而主司聲榮亦與
斯錄俱矣勗乎哉
浙江湖州府儒學訓導□□師
錫謹序
punctuated:
皇上側席盛心，而聖祖設科不爲希寵藉手，則豈特多士之休，而主司聲榮亦與斯錄俱矣！勗乎哉！
浙江湖州府儒學訓導□□師錫謹序。
translation_en:
… the Emperor’s earnest desire in eagerly awaiting worthy talents, and so that the Sacred Ancestor’s establishment of the examination system does not serve merely as a stepping stone for seeking favor—then not only will this be to the glory of you many scholars, but the reputation and honor of the examiners will also endure together with this record! Be diligent!

Respectfully written as a postface by […][…] Shixi, Assistant Instructor of the Confucian School of Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
萬曆己卯秋八月天下士復
□□惟廣東則巡按監察
□臨之恪奉
□
□□鶴之屆
□□四方至
□□□及訓導唐師
試學正趙之垣敎諭
侯必恭梁學奎李一元林祭
明訓導劉世節應一唯同考
試而提調則右布政使錢藻
左參議漆彬監試則按察使
莊國禎副使趙志皐一切內
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序
萬曆己卯秋八月，天下士復□□，惟廣東則巡按監察□臨之。恪奉□□□鶴之屆，□□四方至□□□，及訓導唐師、試學正趙之垣、敎諭侯必恭、梁學奎、李一元、林祭明、訓導劉世節、應一唯同考試。而提調則右布政使錢藻、左參議漆彬；監試則按察使莊國禎、副使趙志皐。一切內
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the jimao year of the Wanli reign (1579), the scholars of the empire once again [assembled for the triennial examinations?]. In Guangdong, the Regional Inspector, Investigating [Censor] [?], served as Supervising Official. Reverently upholding [the imperial mandate?], at the arrival of […] He [?], [the examiners…] arrived from the four quarters […], together with Assistant Instructor Tang Shi 唐師; Probationary Subprefectural/Departmental Director of Studies Zhao Zhiyuan 趙之垣; District Directors of Studies Hou Bigong 侯必恭, Liang Xuekui 梁學奎, Li Yiyuan 李一元, and Lin Jiming 林祭明 [?]; and Assistant Instructors Liu Shijie 劉世節 and Ying Yiwei 應一唯, who served as Associate Examiners. As for the Proctors, they were Right Administration Commissioner Qian Zao 錢藻 and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Qi Bin 漆彬; as for the Monitoring Examiners, they were Surveillance Commissioner Zhuang Guozhen 莊國禎 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhao Zhigao 趙志皐. All the inner…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
外百執事庀僚分寄咸充其
選旣復羣百執事齋籲而盟
惟公惟慎期綜材實而収之
以不虛
簡任至意越日進提學副使應鋐
□提學副使舒大猷所遴
□□□□奇試之三而
===
功令率循無爲文具文學校閱
不令旁干則御史尤諄諄焉
于是遵
制拔其雋七十五人幷彙其文之
如式者以
獻錄成御史顧曰休宜序諸首日
休不佞猥以職事獲與掄材
punctuated: 外百執事，庀僚分寄，咸充其選。旣，復羣百執事齋籲而盟，惟公惟慎，期綜材實而収之，以不虛簡任至意。越日，進提學副使應鋐、□提學副使舒大猷所遴□□□□奇，試之三，而功令率循，無爲文具；文學校閱，不令旁干，則御史尤諄諄焉。于是遵制拔其雋七十五人，幷彙其文之如式者以獻。錄成，御史顧曰：「休宜序諸首。」日休不佞，猥以職事獲與掄材
translation_en: …and outer functionaries, who were assembled to share the responsibilities, all admirably fulfilled their selection. Afterward, the various functionaries were gathered to fast, offer prayers, and swear an oath to act solely with impartiality and caution, aiming to assess true talent and select them so as not to fail the utmost intent of the imperial appointment. Days later, the [thousands of] outstanding candidates [?] selected by Education-intendant Vice Commissioner Ying Hong 應鋐 and [former?] Education-intendant Vice Commissioner Shu Dayou 舒大猷 were admitted and tested in three sessions. That the regulations were strictly followed without becoming mere formalities, and that the literary evaluation and grading were kept free from outside interference, were matters upon which the Censor was especially earnest and insistent. Thereupon, in compliance with the imperial system, seventy-five of the most outstanding talents were selected, and their essays that conformed to the prescribed standards were compiled to be presented to the throne. When the record was completed, the Censor looked to me and said, "You, [Ri]xiu, ought to write the preface at its head." Incompetent as I, Rixiu 日休, am, having had the undeserved fortune by virtue of my official duties to participate in the grand…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之盛敢不唯唯蓋自周制天
子命侯國建學造士士之有
造而秀者鄕論之第升之天
子銓敘材品而祿爵之當其
時上弘薪槱之道賓賢之典
罔或不虔士以賢見賓登之
論選罔或不適考信於王制
===
以跡其盛則聖世人文可遡
而窺也
明興準周甄士三載賓賢方之為
烈肆東粤士競爽稱文繇其
文評隲其材豈不贇贇然秀
哉夫士挾材不難際時難際
時不難遇君難懿我
punctuated: 之盛，敢不唯唯？蓋自周制，天子命侯國建學造士，士之有造而秀者，鄕論之，第升之天子，銓敘材品而祿爵之。當其時，上弘薪槱之道，賓賢之典罔或不虔；士以賢見賓，登之論選，罔或不適。考信於《王制》，以跡其盛，則聖世人文，可遡而窺也。明興，準周甄士，三載賓賢，方之為烈。肆東粤士競爽稱文，繇其文評隲其材，豈不贇贇然秀哉？夫士挾材不難，際時難；際時不難，遇君難。懿我
translation_en:
… of this grand occasion; how could I dare not respectfully comply? Indeed, since the system of the Zhou dynasty, the Son of Heaven commanded the feudal states to establish schools to cultivate scholars. Those scholars who were accomplished and outstanding were evaluated by their local communities and promoted in sequence to the Son of Heaven, who assessed and ranked their talents and qualities, and bestowed emoluments and titles of nobility upon them. At that time, the ruler above broadened the way of gathering and nurturing talent, and in the ceremony of feasting the worthy as guests, there was nothing that was not reverent; scholars, being received as guests for their worthiness and elevated through evaluation and selection, never failed to be well-suited. If one verifies this in the "Royal Regulations" (Wangzhi) to trace its flourishing, the cultural refinement of that sagely age can be traced back and glimpsed.

When the Ming arose, it modeled itself on the Zhou in selecting scholars; feasting the worthy every three years, its glory even surpasses that of the past. Thus the scholars of eastern Guangdong vie in brilliance and are renowned for their literary writings. Judging and evaluating their talents through their writings, are they not splendidly refined and outstanding? Now, for a scholar to possess talent is not difficult, but to meet with the right era is difficult; to meet with the right era is not difficult, but to encounter the right sovereign is difficult. Admirable is our …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上睿喆秉籙
經幃不輟
御幸學右文廣厲多士斂琱還樸
無言逖邇菁英躍於聽覩藻
采新於風問夫孰不願爲材
曩東粤梀兵土無寧業
詔趣文武大吏不崇朝而清之卽
===
今文治同風要以轉呻鞏而
絃誦寔惟粤士不無幸者是
以日休從鎖院後繙據多士
所爲文大都淹六籍漱衆流
指事陳政不卑卑吐華此非
帝德焜燿宜不及此夫士偃蓬蒿
抱藝媒合惟恐不得當有司
punctuated: 皇上睿喆秉籙，經幃不輟，御幸學右文，廣厲多士，斂琱還樸，無言逖邇。菁英躍於聽覩，藻采新於風問，夫孰不願爲材？曩東粤梀兵，土無寧業，詔趣文武大吏，不崇朝而清之。卽今文治同風，要以轉呻鞏而絃誦，寔惟粤士不無幸者。是以日休從鎖院後，繙據多士所爲文，大都淹六籍、漱衆流，指事陳政，不卑卑吐華，此非帝德焜燿，宜不及此。夫士偃蓬蒿，抱藝媒合，惟恐不得當有司。
translation_en: …His Majesty, in his sagely wisdom, holds the imperial mandate. He is unceasing at the Classic Mat, personally visits the Imperial University to promote literary culture, and broadly encourages the multitude of scholars, restraining ornate carving to return to simplicity, without needing words to reach far and near. The finest talents leap forth at what they hear and see, and literary brilliance is renewed at the tidings; who, then, would not wish to become a man of talent? Formerly, when eastern Guangdong suffered from warfare [? 梀兵, likely for 困兵 or 練兵] and the land had no peaceful livelihood, an imperial edict urged the senior civil and military officials, and before the morning was out they pacified it. Now, civil governance unifies customs, essentially transforming groans of distress [? 呻鞏, likely for 呻吟] into the strumming of strings and chanting of texts; truly, the scholars of Guangdong are not without good fortune. Therefore, after entering the locked examination compound, I, Rixiu, leafed through and examined the essays composed by the many scholars. For the most part, they are steeped in the Six Classics and rinse their mouths in the myriad schools of thought; in pointing to affairs and setting forth governance, they do not merely spit out petty flowery phrases. Were it not for the radiant splendor of the Emperor's virtue, they surely could not have reached this level. Now, when scholars lie hidden amid the wormwood and mugwort, embracing their arts to seek advancement, their only fear is failing to suit the authorities…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有司業以士進矣吹一映以
快里耳折楊皇華則噤無與
和績緝緒言以詭世資竟之
實不揜名履不循素至令主
司懍懍懷懼則何以稱哉先
是言官
上正文體五事又毖重試務而顓
===
===
之監臨委寄內簾以湛衡鑑
皇上嘉與元輔疏
聞輒下禮卿條便宜
頒之郡國搜羅雋彥誠急之也鄕
始論士即注
聖衷如此士灑心以應
明德趣安所决哉在昔文治初闢
punctuated: 有司業以士進矣，吹一映以快里耳，《折楊》、《皇華》則噤無與和；績緝緒言以詭世資，竟之實不揜名，履不循素，至令主司懍懍懷懼，則何以稱哉？先是，言官上正文體五事，又毖重試務，而顓之監臨，委寄內簾，以湛衡鑑。皇上嘉與元輔疏聞，輒下禮卿條便宜，頒之郡國，搜羅雋彥，誠急之也。鄕始論士，即注聖衷如此，士灑心以應明德，趣安所决哉？在昔文治初闢，
translation_en: Once the authorities have advanced these scholars, if they merely blow a single breath of sound to delight rustic ears while falling silent and unable to join in harmony with tunes beyond "Zheyang" and "Huanghua" [?]; or if they piece together leftover words to deceitfully gain worldly status, so that in the end their reality does not match their reputation and their conduct does not follow their former principles—to the point of making the chief examiners tremble with dread—then how can they be worthy of their title? Earlier, speaking officials submitted five matters on rectifying literary style, and further urged caution and gravity in examination affairs, placing dedicated authority in the Supervising Official and entrusting the inner examination compound to clarify the balance and mirror of evaluation. His Majesty praised this, and when the Senior Grand Secretary reported it in a memorial, He immediately ordered the Minister of Rites to itemize appropriate measures and promulgate them to the prefectures and principalities. In searching out and gathering outstanding talents, He is truly urgent! When at the very beginning of evaluating scholars at the provincial level, His Sacred Mind pays such close attention as this, as scholars cleanse their hearts to respond to His illustrious virtue, in what direction should their aspirations be resolved? In the past, when cultural governance was first opened in this region, …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
區冊趙德才能不逾中人猶
然附青雲以有聲此一時也
非馳騖勤思抗蹟嵬伐則不
足以軼前徽照後禩何者
主上明聖則當意之難遘會
熈明則表見未易也吾聞廉吏綰
綬而鍾乳復賢守剖符而明
===
珠還彼守長耳至於山靈告
祥淵光生媚矧我
皇上儼然以
純德臨照之而
嘉禮慶成關雎歌洽則羔羊在位
兔罝在野其應不爽多士資
適逢世當令蚌胎讓采乳穴
punctuated: 區冊、趙德才能不逾中人，猶然附青雲以有聲。此一時也，非馳騖勤思、抗蹟嵬伐，則不足以軼前徽、照後禩。何者？主上明聖，則當意之難；遘會熈明，則表見未易也。吾聞廉吏綰綬而鍾乳復，賢守剖符而明珠還。彼守長耳，至於山靈告祥、淵光生媚，矧我皇上儼然以純德臨照之，而嘉禮慶成、《關雎》歌洽，則《羔羊》在位、《兔罝》在野，其應不爽。多士資適逢世，當令蚌胎讓采、乳穴…
translation_en: … Ou Ce 區冊 and Zhao De 趙德 possessed talents no greater than those of ordinary men, yet by attaching themselves to high-ranking patrons they achieved renown. That was one era; today, unless one strives earnestly and thinks diligently, elevating one's conduct to lofty achievements, it will not be enough to surpass the fine examples of the past and shine upon future generations. Why is this? Because when the Sovereign above is enlightened and sagely, it is difficult to meet his expectations; and when one encounters an era of radiant splendor, it is not easy to distinguish oneself. I have heard that when an incorrupt official tied on his seal-ribbon, the stalactite milk returned to the caves, and when a worthy Grand Protector split the tally of office, the bright pearls came back to the waters. Those were mere commandery chiefs, yet the mountain spirits announced auspicious signs and the gleaming depths grew radiant with charm. How much more so when our August Emperor solemnly shines upon the realm with his pure virtue, and when the auspicious wedding rites have been felicitously completed and the song of "Guanju" 關雎 resounds in harmony! Then officials like those of "Gaoyang" 羔羊 will occupy their posts and worthies like those of "Tuju" 兔罝 will be found in the countryside—such responses never fail. You many scholars, whose talents happen to meet with this opportune age, should make the pearl-oyster's womb yield in brilliance and the stalactite caverns…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
遜珍其所自效宜何如者言
蘄成信不弁髦其先資事蘄
當功不虛恢於注厝宣猶展
采直與素絲一節公侯匹體
詎兎罝野人下哉惟多士決
策焉異時抽
天府賢書論讚其盛如所爲追頌
===
王制者必在
今日矣是舉也先總督兩廣軍
務都察院右都御史今陞南
京兵部尚書凌雲翼今總督
兩廣軍務兵部右侍郎劉堯
誨後先節鎮揆武宣文提督
南贛汀韶軍務都察院右僉
punctuated:
遜珍，其所自效宜何如者？言蘄成信，不弁髦其先資；事蘄當功，不虛恢於注厝。宣猶展采，直與素絲一節、公侯匹體，詎兎罝野人下哉？惟多士決策焉。異時抽天府賢書，論讚其盛，如所爲追頌王制者，必在今日矣。
是舉也，先總督兩廣軍務、都察院右都御史，今陞南京兵部尚書凌雲翼，今總督兩廣軍務、兵部右侍郎劉堯誨，後先節鎮，揆武宣文；提督南贛汀韶軍務、都察院右僉
translation_en:
…yield their treasures—then how ought they to devote themselves in service? In their words, they should strive to establish trustworthiness, not casting aside like a worn-out cap the writings by which they first commended themselves; in their deeds, they should strive for fitting achievement, not indulging in empty boastfulness in the measures they enact. Unfolding their counsels and displaying their accomplishments, they will directly match the integrity celebrated in "White Silk" (Susi) and stand as counterparts to the dukes and marquises—how could they fall short of the rustic men of "The Rabbit Snare" (Tuju)? Let the many scholars resolve upon their course! In days to come, when the registers of the worthy in the Imperial Treasury are drawn forth and their flourishing glory is lauded and appraised, that which will be celebrated in retrospect as the Royal Regulations (Wangzhi) shall surely lie in what is begun today.

In this undertaking, the former Supreme Commander of Military Affairs of Liangguang and Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, now promoted to Nanjing Minister of War, Ling Yunyi 凌雲翼, and the current Supreme Commander of Military Affairs of Liangguang and Right Vice Minister of War, Liu Yaohui 劉堯誨, have successively held the regional command, regulating military affairs and propagating civil culture; the Grand Coordinator and Military Superintendent of Nan'gan, Tingzhou, and Shaozhou, Right Assistant…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
都御史蒙詔風猷表士而右
參政劉經緯徐時可張明正
右參議王來賢副使劉世賞
張堯年僉事馬千乘熊惟學
侯應爵右都督總兵官張元
勳副總兵陳璘侯繼高參將
楊瑄夏尚忠季金顧宗文遊
===
擊金丹韓沛朱文達葉歡署
都指揮僉事祖萬松咸防範
惟周先期入
賀則左參政孫光祖僉事劉倬
署都指揮僉事成大儒遷秩
則左布政使今陞順天府府
尹施堯臣與聞
punctuated: 都御史蒙詔，風猷表士。而右參政劉經緯、徐時可、張明正，右參議王來賢，副使劉世賞、張堯年，僉事馬千乘、熊惟學、侯應爵，右都督總兵官張元勳，副總兵陳璘、侯繼高，參將楊瑄、夏尚忠、季金、顧宗文，遊擊金丹、韓沛、朱文達、葉歡，署都指揮僉事祖萬松，咸防範惟周。先期入賀，則左參政孫光祖、僉事劉倬、署都指揮僉事成大儒；遷秩，則左布政使今陞順天府府尹施堯臣：與聞
translation_en: … Censor-in-Chief Meng Zhao 蒙詔 has set a moral example for the scholars through his conduct and plans. Meanwhile, Right Administration Vice Commissioners Liu Jingwei 劉經緯, Xu Shike 徐時可, and Zhang Mingzheng 張明正; Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Wang Laixian 王來賢; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Liu Shishang 劉世賞 and Zhang Yaonian 張堯年; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Ma Qiancheng 馬千乘, Xiong Weixue 熊惟學, and Hou Yingjue 侯應爵; Right Commissioner-in-Chief and Regional Commander Zhang Yuanxun 張元勳; Regional Vice Commanders Chen Lin 陳璘 and Hou Jigao 侯繼高; Assistant Regional Commanders Yang Xuan 楊瑄, Xia Shangzhong 夏尚忠, Ji Jin 季金, and Gu Zongwen 顧宗文; Mobile Corps Commanders Jin Dan 金丹, Han Pei 韓沛, Zhu Wenda 朱文達, and Ye Huan 葉歡; and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Zu Wansong 祖萬松 all maintained thorough security precautions. Those who departed ahead of time to present congratulations at court—namely Left Administration Vice Commissioner Sun Guangzu 孫光祖, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Liu Zhuo 劉倬, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Cheng Daru 成大儒—and he who was promoted to another post, namely Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Shi Yaochen 施堯臣, now promoted to Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture 順天府, all participated in…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
衞公孫朝問於子貢曰仲尼焉學子貢曰
文武之道未墜於地在人賢者識其大
者不賢者識其小者莫不有文武之道
焉夫子焉不學而亦何常師之有
詩曰妻子好合如鼓瑟琴兄弟旣翕和樂
且耽宜爾室家樂爾妻帑子曰父母其
順矣乎
===
士之仕也猶農夫之耕也農夫豈爲出疆
舍其耒耜哉
易
君子黃中通理正位居體
利貞乁於其道也
言行君子之樞機樞機之發榮辱之主也
六爻相雜唯其時物也其初難知其上易
知本末也初辭擬之卒成之終若夫雜
物撰德辨是與非則非其中爻不備
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
衞公孫朝問於子貢曰：「仲尼焉學？」子貢曰：「文、武之道，未墜於地，在人。賢者識其大者，不賢者識其小者，莫不有文、武之道焉。夫子焉不學？而亦何常師之有！」
《詩》曰：「妻子好合，如鼓瑟琴。兄弟旣翕，和樂且耽。宜爾室家，樂爾妻帑。」子曰：「父母其順矣乎！」
士之仕也，猶農夫之耕也；農夫豈爲出疆舍其耒耜哉？

易
君子黃中通理，正位居體。
利貞，乁於其道也。
言行，君子之樞機。樞機之發，榮辱之主也。
六爻相雜，唯其時物也。其初難知，其上易知，本末也。初辭擬之，卒成之終。若夫雜物撰德，辨是與非，則非其中爻不備。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Gongsun Chao of Wei asked Zigong, "From whom did Zhongni [Confucius] learn?" Zigong replied, "The Way of King Wen and King Wu has not yet fallen to the ground; it persists among people. Those who are worthy remember its greater principles, and those who are not worthy remember its smaller details. None lack something of the Way of Wen and Wu. Where could our Master not learn? And yet why would he have any single constant teacher?"

The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: "Loving union with wife and children is like the strumming of zithers and lutes; when brothers are in harmony, there is peace, joy, and deep delight; thus order well your household, and bring joy to your wife and children." The Master said, "How at ease the parents will be!"

"A scholar's taking office is like a farmer's plowing; does a farmer ever abandon his plowshares just because he crosses the border out of a state?"

Book of Changes (Yijing)

"The noble man, with yellow [central] moderation,comprehends principle; holding the correct position, he abides in the main body."

"'Advantageous to be firm and correct': this means enduring long in its Way."

"Words and deeds are the hinge and trigger of the noble man. The release of the hinge and trigger is the master of glory and disgrace."

"The six lines are intermingled with one another simply according to their timely things. The first line is difficult to know, and the top line is easy to know, for they are the root and the branch. The words for the first line deliberate upon it, and at the end they bring it to completion. As for intermingling things and composing virtues, and distinguishing right from wrong, without the middle lines it would not be complete."

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書
稽于衆舍己從人不虐無告不廢困窮
伊洛瀍澗既入于河
自殷王中宗及高宗及祖甲及我周文王
茲四人迪哲
則亦有熊羆之士不二心之臣保乂王家
詩
春日載陽有鳴倉庚
樂只君子天子葵之
===
雝雝在宮肅肅在廟不顯亦臨無射亦保
四海來假來假祁祁景員維河殷受命咸
宜百祿是何
春秋
鄭人伐衛〔隱公二年〕
齊師宋師曹師次于聶北救邢 夏六月
邢遷于夷儀齊師宋師曹師城邢〔俱僖〕
〔公元年〕
衛人救陳〔宣公十有二年〕會于蕭魚〔襄公〕
punctuated:
《書》：
「稽于衆，舍己從人，不虐無告，不廢困窮。」
「伊、洛、瀍、澗，既入于河。」
「自殷王中宗，及高宗，及祖甲，及我周文王，茲四人迪哲。」
「則亦有熊羆之士，不二心之臣，保乂王家。」

《詩》：
「春日載陽，有鳴倉庚。」
「樂只君子，天子葵之。」
「雝雝在宮，肅肅在廟。不顯亦臨，無射亦保。」
「四海來假，來假祁祁。景員維河，殷受命咸宜，百祿是何。」

《春秋》：
「鄭人伐衛。」〔隱公二年〕
「齊師、宋師、曹師次于聶北，救邢。夏，六月，邢遷于夷儀。齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。」〔俱僖公元年〕
「衛人救陳。」〔宣公十有二年〕「會于蕭魚。」〔襄公…
translation_en:
Book of Documents (Shu):
"He consulted the multitude, giving up his own view to follow others; he did not oppress the helpless, nor did he neglect the straitened and poor."
"The Yi, Luo, Chan, and Jian rivers were conducted into the Yellow River."
"From the Yin king Zhongzong, down to Gaozong and Zujia, and to our Zhou King Wen—these four men walked in wisdom."
"Have likewise warriors fierce as bears and grizzlies, and ministers of undivided heart, who help to protect and govern the royal house."

Book of Odes (Shi):
"In the spring days the warmth begins, and the oriole is singing."
"Happy be the lord! The Son of Heaven measures his merits."
"Full of harmony was he in the palace; full of reverence in the ancestral temple. Unseen, he still felt under inspection; unwearyingly, he preserved his virtue."
"Those within the four seas come to our sacrifices; they come in multitudes. The great border is the Yellow River. Rightly did Yin receive the mandate; all the hundred blessings does it bear."

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
賜輔臣九卿講官正字官各一幅謝表〔萬曆二年〕
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
攬納稅糧
禁止迎送
私賣軍器
詐為瑞應
第叁塲
===
策〔五道〕
問君心唯在所養而培養之功必于學焉
伊昔喆王典學首稱殷高宗說命所陳
其辭可指而述歟厥後代有英辟或石
渠講經或臨雍拜老或弘文置館或崇
政說書其學亦有得于說命之要歟我
太祖高皇帝
聖神御極
萬幾暇卽與侍臣講論經史
punctuated:
賜輔臣、九卿、講官、正字官各一幅謝表〔萬曆二年〕。

判語〔五條〕：
官吏給由。
攬納稅糧。
禁止迎送。
私賣軍器。
詐為瑞應。

第叁塲
策〔五道〕

問：君心唯在所養，而培養之功必于學焉。伊昔喆王典學，首稱殷高宗，《說命》所陳，其辭可指而述歟？厥後代有英辟，或石渠講經，或臨雍拜老，或弘文置館，或崇政說書，其學亦有得于《說命》之要歟？我太祖高皇帝聖神御極，萬幾暇卽與侍臣講論經史，
translation_en:
…bestowing one scroll each upon the Grand Secretaries, the Nine Ministers, the Lecturers-in-Waiting, and the Proofreaders: a Memorial of Thanks (2nd year of the Wanli era [1574]).

Legal Judgments (five items):
Issuing Certificates of Service for Officials and Subofficial Functionaries.
Monopolizing the Payment of Tax Grain.
Prohibiting the Welcoming and Escorting of Officials.
Illicitly Selling Military Weapons.
Fabricating Auspicious Omens.

Third Session
Policy Questions (five items)

Question: The ruler's mind depends solely on how it is nourished, and the work of nurturing it necessarily lies in learning. Among the wise kings of antiquity who devoted themselves to learning, foremost praise is given to Gaozong of Yin; as for what is set forth in the "Charge to Yue" (Yue ming), can its words be pointed out and recounted? In subsequent ages there were enlightened monarchs who variously expounded the Classics in the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiqu ge), visited the Imperial University (Biyong) to pay respects to the aged, established the Institute for the Advancement of Literature (Hongwen guan), or lectured on texts in the Hall of Venerating Governance (Chongzheng dian); did their learning also grasp the essentials of the "Charge to Yue"? When Our Taizu, the Emperor Gao, sagely and divinely ascended the throne, in his leisure from a myriad affairs of state he immediately discussed the Classics and Histories with his attending officials;…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承並崇
聖學其大要可得聞歟我
皇上
睿質天授
學問夙成而
經筵日講猶勤勤焉
詔麻闡繹直超殷宗上之一時講讀諸臣所納
誨必取衷于典學之撰矣夫
帝王之學與韋布不同其大本大原固有在也
===
攷之
會典所載進講後凡五府軍政六部要務詹
事等官皆得以次敷陳
今日可復行否耶宋儒在經筵有反覆開導
覬有啓悟者有講色莊嚴繼以諷諫者
今能有進於是乎諸士懷忠藎之忱素
矣願詳著于篇以為
聖學緝熙之助
問學術事功非二物也世之言學術者必
punctuated:
列聖相承，並崇聖學，其大要可得聞歟？我皇上睿質天授，學問夙成，而經筵日講猶勤勤焉。詔麻闡繹，直超殷宗上之。一時講讀諸臣所納誨，必取衷于典學之撰矣。夫帝王之學與韋布不同，其大本大原固有在也。攷之《會典》所載，進講後，凡五府軍政、六部要務、詹事等官皆得以次敷陳，今日可復行否耶？宋儒在經筵，有反覆開導、覬有啓悟者，有講色莊嚴、繼以諷諫者，今能有進於是乎？諸士懷忠藎之忱素矣，願詳著于篇，以為聖學緝熙之助。
問：學術、事功非二物也。世之言學術者，必
translation_en:
… The successive Sacred Emperors followed one after another, all revering sage learning; may we hear of its main essentials? Our reigning Emperor is endowed by Heaven with a perspicacious nature and his learning was accomplished early on, yet he remains ever diligent at the Classics Colloquium and the daily lectures. His edicts and proclamations expound and unfold meanings, directly surpassing Yin Gaozong and rising above him. The admonitions presented by the various lecturing and reading officials of the age must surely draw their guiding principles from works on constant dedication to learning. Now, the learning of emperors and kings differs from that of commoners in plain cloth; its great foundation and great source certainly have where they reside. Examining what is recorded in the Collected Statutes (Huidian), after the lectures were presented, all military administration of the Five Chief Military Commissions, important affairs of the Six Ministries, and officials of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent (Zhanshi) and others were permitted to set forth their views in turn; can this be restored and practiced today or not? When Song-dynasty Confucians attended the Classics Colloquium, some repeatedly guided and instructed in hopes of inspiring enlightenment, while others lectured with a solemn countenance and followed up with tactful remonstrance; today, can we go even further than this? You gentlemen have long cherished sentiments of loyal devotion; I hope you will set them forth in detail in your essays, to serve as an aid to the radiant and continuous progress of the Imperial learning.

Question: Scholarly learning and practical achievement are not two separate things. When people of the world speak of scholarly learning, they invariably…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
稱孔孟言事功者必曰伊周若岐而二
之何歟假令數聖賢者生同其時其所
建立發明亦有相符合者歟漢唐以來
有潜心大業罷黜百家者有攘斥異端
推尊孟氏者不謂非學術也而世儒何
每有訾言有運籌決勝佐成帝業者有
潜授豪賢卒正主器者不謂非事功也
而尚論者何猶有遺議歟若夫濂洛關
閩之學慶曆熈寧諸君子之勳班班史
===
冊稱盛矣視前數子者孰優其於孔孟
伊周之軌亦庶幾否耶然樹立俊偉者
不以理學稱而多所發明得理學之傳
者乃用之不果究焉豈所學不適於用
而用者無待於學歟諸生誦法孔孟亦
志伊周矣推學術以建事功此其時也
願質言之無隱
問吏數易置則民不安兩漢之盛也牧守
長子孫焉是非其效驗較著者歟我
punctuated:
稱孔、孟，言事功者必曰伊、周，若岐而二之，何歟？假令數聖賢者生同其時，其所建立、發明，亦有相符合者歟？漢、唐以來，有潜心大業、罷黜百家者，有攘斥異端、推尊孟氏者，不謂非學術也，而世儒何每有訾言？有運籌決勝、佐成帝業者，有潜授豪賢、卒正主器者，不謂非事功也，而尚論者何猶有遺議歟？若夫濂、洛、關、閩之學，慶曆、熈寧諸君子之勳，班班史冊，稱盛矣。視前數子者孰優？其於孔、孟、伊、周之軌，亦庶幾否耶？然樹立俊偉者不以理學稱，而多所發明、得理學之傳者，乃用之不果究焉。豈所學不適於用，而用者無待於學歟？諸生誦法孔、孟，亦志伊、周矣。推學術以建事功，此其時也。願質言之，無隱。

問：吏數易置則民不安。兩漢之盛也，牧守長子孫焉，是非其效驗較著者歟？我
translation_en:
…praise Confucius and Mencius, while those who speak of practical achievements necessarily speak of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, as though dividing them into two separate things—why is this? Suppose these several sages and worthies had lived at the same time: would what they established in action and elucidated in thought have been mutually consistent? Since the Han and Tang dynasties, there was one who immersed his mind in the great enterprise and dismissed the hundred schools [Dong Zhongshu], and one who repelled heterodoxies and exalted Mencius [Han Yu]; one cannot say this was not scholarship, yet why do scholars of the world constantly find fault with them? There was one who devised strategies to determine victory and assisted in accomplishing the imperial enterprise [Zhang Liang], and one who secretly mentored heroic worthies and ultimately restored the rightful heir to the throne [Di Renjie]; one cannot say these were not practical achievements, yet why do those who evaluate historical figures still leave lingering criticisms of them? As for the learning of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min [Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi], and the meritorious deeds of the noble men of the Qingli (1041–1048) and Xining (1068–1077) eras, they are clearly recorded in the historical annals and praised as flourishing. Compared to the several masters mentioned earlier, which are superior? And do they come close to the path of Confucius, Mencius, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou, or not? Yet those who established magnificent achievements were not renowned for Neo-Confucian principle-learning (lixue), while those who elucidated much and obtained the transmission of principle-learning were employed without their potential being fully realized. Could it be that what is learned is unsuited for practical application, and that practical application has no need to rely on learning? You students recite and model yourselves on Confucius and Mencius, and also aspire to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. Extending scholarly learning to establish practical achievements—this is the time for it. I wish you to speak plainly and hold nothing back.

Question: When officials are frequently replaced, the people are unsettled. During the flourishing of the Western and Eastern Han dynasties, regional governors and grand administrators raised children and grandchildren in their posts—is this not a clearly manifest proof of its effectiveness? When our…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上御寓之初首用輔臣議久任責成不驟遷
以奪其成效一時吏稱民安臻上理矣
而或者謂久任便民不便吏然歟夫置
吏爲民民誠便不便吏何傷顧使吏多
滯歎人懷厭心不有以鼓舞振作之亦
奚以厲世而磨鈍也乃其道安在歟先
正有言久任之法與超遷相表裏其說
可得聞歟
祖宗朝蓋兼用之矣其在
===
今日可踵而行之否也或又謂文法之拘勝
則顧慮多內外之勢懸則覬慕起斯二
患蓋自古已然玆欲使長民之吏皆樂
於久任以殫脩厥職而不負責成則將
何策而可
問象緯禨祥之說推天徵人多所牽合然
蓋尚矣乃孔子作春秋紀災異而不言
事應何歟考之星官彗孛飛流皆變星
也說者謂孛而不已繼之以彗而晏子
punctuated:
皇上御寓之初，首用輔臣議，久任責成，不驟遷以奪其成效，一時吏稱民安，臻上理矣。而或者謂久任便民不便吏，然歟？夫置吏爲民，民誠便，不便吏何傷？顧使吏多滯歎，人懷厭心，不有以鼓舞振作之，亦奚以厲世而磨鈍也？乃其道安在歟？先正有言：「久任之法，與超遷相表裏。」其說可得聞歟？祖宗朝蓋兼用之矣，其在今日，可踵而行之否也？或又謂文法之拘勝則顧慮多，內外之勢懸則覬慕起，斯二患蓋自古已然。玆欲使長民之吏，皆樂於久任，以殫脩厥職，而不負責成，則將何策而可？
問：象緯禨祥之說，推天徵人，多所牽合，然蓋尚矣。乃孔子作《春秋》，紀災異而不言事應，何歟？考之星官，彗、孛、飛、流，皆變星也。說者謂孛而不已，繼之以彗；而晏子
translation_en:
… At the beginning of His Majesty's reign, he first adopted the counsel of his Grand Secretaries to keep officials in office for long tenures and hold them accountable for results, not transferring them abruptly so as to deprive them of their accomplishments. For a time, officials were competent and the people were at peace, attaining supreme governance. Yet some say that long tenure is convenient for the people but inconvenient for the officials; is this so? Now, officials are appointed for the sake of the people; if the people are truly convenienced, what harm is there if it is inconvenient for the officials? However, if officials are left with frequent sighs over stagnation and everyone harbors a sense of weariness, without something to inspire and rouse them, how can one encourage the world and sharpen the dull? Wherein, then, lies the way to do so? A former worthy had a saying: "The method of long tenure and that of exceptional promotion are complementary sides of the same coin." May we hear an explanation of this view? During the reigns of our Imperial Ancestors, both were indeed used together; at the present day, can we follow in their footsteps and put this into practice or not? Others also say that when the constraints of legalistic regulations prevail, anxieties and hesitations multiply; when the disparity in status between the inner court and outer provinces is great, ambitious coveting arises. These two ills have indeed existed since antiquity. Now, if we wish to make all officials who govern the people happy to serve long tenures, so as to exhaust their efforts in fulfilling their duties without failing the accountability demanded of them, what policy will suffice?

Question: The theories of celestial phenomena and portents of good and ill fortune, which deduce human affairs from heavenly signs, involve much forced correlation, yet they are of great antiquity. Why is it, then, that when Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), he recorded calamities and anomalies without speaking of their corresponding human events? Examining the astrological treatises, sweeping comets (hui), bushy comets (bo), flying stars (fei), and meteors (liu) are all anomalous stars. Commentators say that when a bushy comet does not cease, it is followed by a sweeping comet; yet Master Yan (Yanzi)…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則曰君不脩政孛星將出彗何懼焉則
孛又甚於彗矣然而建元元狩中有孛
于西北孛于東方者矣地節中有孛于
西方孛于參者矣永平建初中有孛于
天船孛于天市孛于紫宮者矣夫語中
興之業宜無二於四君者乃其變若此
而徵應不見豈史失其傳歟抑天道遠
而難言歟或四君者所以消弭之者有
道變不為災歟有言星變結和太上脩
===
德其次脩政其次脩救其次脩禳其亦
有當否我
皇上敬
天朝夕乾惕頃
書十二事
座右以備
觀省宜無容言者比以星變輒
警畏勵精
簡廷臣而科條之百司皇皇思過不暇雖知
punctuated: 則曰：「君不脩政，孛星將出，彗何懼焉？」則孛又甚於彗矣。然而建元、元狩中有孛于西北、孛于東方者矣；地節中有孛于西方、孛于參者矣；永平、建初中有孛于天船、孛于天市、孛于紫宮者矣。夫語中興之業，宜無二於四君者，乃其變若此，而徵應不見，豈史失其傳歟？抑天道遠而難言歟？或四君者所以消弭之者有道，變不為災歟？有言星變結和：太上脩德，其次脩政，其次脩救，其次脩禳。其亦有當否？我皇上敬天，朝夕乾惕，頃書十二事座右，以備觀省，宜無容言者。比以星變，輒警畏勵精，簡廷臣而科條之，百司皇皇，思過不暇。雖知
translation_en: … however, said: "If the ruler does not cultivate his governance, a bushy star (beixing) is about to appear; what is there to fear in a broom star (huixing)?" Thus a bushy star is even worse than a broom star. Yet during the Jianyuan (140–135 BCE) and Yuanshou (122–117 BCE) eras [of Emperor Wu of Han], there were bushy stars in the northwest and bushy stars in the east; during the Dijie era (69–66 BCE) [of Emperor Xuan of Han], there were bushy stars in the west and bushy stars in the constellation Shen (Orion); and during the Yongping (58–75 CE) and Jianchu (76–84 CE) eras [of Emperors Ming and Zhang of Han], there were bushy stars in the Tianshuan constellation, bushy stars in the Tianshi enclosure, and bushy stars in the Zigong (Purple Palace) enclosure. Now, when speaking of achievements in dynastic revival and flourishing, none should surpass these four rulers; yet their celestial anomalies were like this, while no corresponding portents or repercussions were seen. Could it be that the histories lost their transmission? Or that the Way of Heaven is distant and difficult to speak of? Or is it that these four rulers possessed the proper way to dispel and avert them, so that the anomalies did not turn into disasters? Someone has said regarding the resolution of harmony in response to stellar anomalies [?]: the highest course is to cultivate virtue, the next is to cultivate governance, the next is to cultivate relief measures, and the next is to cultivate exorcistic prayers. Is this view also appropriate or not? Our Augustus the Emperor reveres Heaven, remaining diligent and vigilant from morning to night. Recently He inscribed twelve matters beside His seat to prepare for His own observation and reflection, leaving nothing further that needs to be said. Lately, because of a stellar anomaly, He immediately grew alarmed and fearful, rousing His spirit to select court officials and subject them to itemized regulations, so that all the officials are anxious and fearful, having barely enough time to reflect upon their faults. Although we know that…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天心仁愛之至而臣子無已之心猶有所願效
者諸士計必畜於衷願詳言之吾將以
聞于
上
問語計安者非禦夷則弭盜夫夷狄非我
族類其有時為梗不足怪者盜吾人也
人情莫不樂生而獨試其身于盜毋亦
有以驅之者耶說者謂盜有源然耶東
粵阻山濱海地廣邊夷又其民呰窳偷
===
生多盜邇荷
聖天子神武當事者經略山海之間足稱蕩平
然境內汰兵異省亡命往往窺伺其間
盜固滋有也他則澳夷結落隱然敵形
珠販連檣公肆剽掠瓊崖黎岐雖別生
也然十字之議未行桑土者憂焉羅旁
徭浪雖戡定也然漏刃之孽未殲衣袽
者戒焉吾慮廣之銷兵無日也夫廣用
兵有年矣剝閭閻實行伍以至筭及雞
punctuated:
天心仁愛之至，而臣子無已之心猶有所願效者。諸士計必畜於衷，願詳言之，吾將以聞于上。

問：語計安者，非禦夷則弭盜。夫夷狄非我族類，其有時為梗，不足怪者；盜，吾人也。人情莫不樂生，而獨試其身于盜，毋亦有以驅之者耶？說者謂盜有源，然耶？東粵阻山濱海，地廣邊夷，又其民呰窳偷生，多盜。邇荷聖天子神武，當事者經略山海之間，足稱蕩平。然境內汰兵、異省亡命，往往窺伺其間，盜固滋有也。他則澳夷結落，隱然敵形；珠販連檣，公肆剽掠。瓊崖黎、岐，雖別生熟也，然十字之議未行，桑土者憂焉；羅旁徭、浪，雖戡定也，然漏刃之孽未殲，衣袽者戒焉。吾慮廣之銷兵無日也。夫廣用兵有年矣，剝閭閻，實行伍，以至筭及雞…
translation_en:
…the utmost benevolence of Heaven's mind, yet the unending devotion of ministers and subjects still has that which it wishes to offer. You gentlemen have surely harbored such plans in your hearts; I wish you to speak of them in detail, and I shall present them to the Emperor.

Question: Those who speak of plans for security talk either of defending against foreign peoples or of suppressing bandits. Now, foreign tribes are not of our kind, so that they sometimes cause obstruction is not to be wondered at; bandits, however, are our own people. In human sentiment there is no one who does not delight in life, yet if they alone risk their lives in banditry, is there not something that drives them to it? Commentators say that banditry has its source—is this so? Eastern Yue [Guangdong] is hemmed in by mountains and borders the sea, its territory is vast and adjoins foreign peoples, and moreover its people are shiftless and live from day to day, so there are many bandits. Recently, thanks to the divine martial prowess of the Sacred Son of Heaven, those in authority have managed campaigns between the mountains and the sea that may well be called a sweeping pacification. Yet within the borders, disbanded soldiers and fugitives from other provinces often spy out opportunities in our midst, and banditry indeed continues to proliferate. As for other matters: the foreigners of Aomen [Macau] have established settlements, covertly taking on the form of an enemy; illicit pearl traders link their masts and openly engage in plundering. Although the Li and Qi peoples of Qiongzhou and Yazhou [Hainan] are distinguished as "uncivilized" [sheng] and "[civilized]" [missing character], the proposal for bisecting cross-roads has not been carried out, and those who prepare before the rain ["mulberry roots"] worry over it; although the Yao and Lang peoples of Luopang have been pacified, the remnants who escaped the blade have not been wiped out, and those who guard against leaks ["caulking rags"] take warning from it. I fear there will never be a day when Guangdong can lay down its arms. Now, Guangdong has employed troops for years: fleecing the common folk to fill the military ranks, to the point that taxes are calculated even down to chickens…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
豚民財詘矣議兵則民無以堪去兵則
盜無由息今其計將安出歟抑別有調
停均節之術可以禦夷弭盜而亦不重
為民病者歟諸士為桑梓慨中必有上
策願悉以對
punctuated: 豚，民財詘矣。議兵，則民無以堪；去兵，則盜無由息。今其計將安出歟？抑別有調停均節之術，可以禦夷弭盜，而亦不重為民病者歟？諸士為桑梓慨，中必有上策，願悉以對。
translation_en: …and pigs; the people’s wealth has been exhausted. If we deliberate on maintaining troops, the people cannot bear the burden; if we disband the troops, there will be no means to quell the bandits. Today, from where shall a plan be devised? Or is there another method of balancing, adjusting, and regulating that can defend against the foreign barbarians and suppress the bandits without heavily afflicting the people? You gentlemen feel deep concern for your native land and must hold a superior strategy within your hearts; I wish for you to reply in full.

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
衞公孫朝問於子貢曰仲尼焉學子貢曰
文武之道未墜於地在人賢者識其大
者不賢者識其小者莫不有文武之道
焉夫子焉不學而亦何常師之有
吳國光
同考試官教諭侯批體裁純正思致精確發
夫子何常師處透徹可式
===
同考試官學正趙批聖學師道道無不在則
師亦無常是作發揮精徹獨得本旨宜錄以式
考試官訓導唐批平正通達
考試官教諭鄭批雋雅
大夫究聖人之學而賢者明其無專學焉夫聖
道恒寄于人也無人非道則無人非學矣孰謂
仲尼有常師哉且夫帝王之道備于文武文武
之道集于仲尼則謂仲尼學文武可也謂其師
文武亦可也何公孫朝以仲尼焉學問焉將謂
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「衞公孫朝問於子貢曰：『仲尼焉學？』子貢曰：『文、武之道，未墜於地，在人。賢者識其大者，不賢者識其小者，莫不有文、武之道焉。夫子焉不學？而亦何常師之有？』」

吳國光

同考試官教諭侯批：體裁純正，思致精確，發「夫子何常師」處透徹，可式。
同考試官學正趙批：聖學師道，道無不在，則師亦無常。是作發揮精徹，獨得本旨，宜錄以式。
考試官訓導唐批：平正通達。
考試官教諭鄭批：雋雅。

大夫究聖人之學，而賢者明其無專學焉。夫聖道恒寄于人也，無人非道，則無人非學矣，孰謂仲尼有常師哉？且夫帝王之道備于文、武，文、武之道集于仲尼，則謂仲尼學文、武可也，謂其師文、武亦可也。何公孫朝以「仲尼焉學」問焉？將謂
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"Gongsun Chao of Wei asked Zigong, 'From whom did Zhongni [Confucius] learn?' Zigong said, 'The Way of King Wen and King Wu has not yet fallen to the ground; it persists among people. Worthies remember its greater principles, and those who are not worthy remember its lesser principles; no one is without something of the Way of Wen and Wu. From whom, then, did our Master not learn? And yet what regular teacher did he have?'"

Wu Guoguang 吳國光

Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Hou's comment: The style is pure and upright, and the thought is precise and accurate. Its exposition of the passage "what regular teacher did our Master have" is thorough and penetrating, worthy of serving as a model.
Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Zhao's comment: The sage took the Way as his teacher; since the Way is omnipresent, his teachers were likewise not fixed. This essay develops the theme with refined thoroughness and uniquely grasps the essential meaning; it should be recorded as a model.
Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Tang's comment: Balanced, upright, and perspicacious.
Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Zheng's comment: Keen and elegant.

A grandee inquired into the learning of the sage, and a worthy made clear that his learning was not confined to a single source. Indeed, the Way of the sages is ever lodged in people; since there is no person without the Way, there is no person from whom one cannot learn—who then would say that Zhongni had a regular teacher? Moreover, the Way of the emperors and kings was brought to completion in King Wen and King Wu, and the Way of Wen and Wu was gathered together in Zhongni; thus to say that Zhongni learned from Wen and Wu is permissible, and to say that he took Wen and Wu as his teachers is also permissible. Why, then, did Gongsun Chao ask, "From whom did Zhongni learn?" Did he mean to say…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其有常學乎亦將謂其有常師乎子貢迺告之
曰子疑夫子之焉學哉亦未知其得統于文武
耳盖文武生而道在文武文武往而道在後人
道有大者人之賢者則識之謨烈之重光固奕
世之紹述也而賢者有斯道焉是道在賢者而
未墜矣道有小者人之不賢者則識之經制之
緒餘固後人之誦法也而不賢者有斯道焉是
道在不賢而未墜矣吾夫子于賢者學之學道
之大也而又不遺其小則賢其師而不專于賢
===
也于不賢者學之學道之小也而又盡其大則
不賢其師而不專于不賢也道垂啓佑恒得人
以衍其盛而合大小皆聖學之資學切憲章每
因人以繼其傳而隨賢否皆得師之益夫子焉
不學也焉不師也而亦何常之有哉至是而文
武之道在人者又在夫子未墜于地者將昭垂
于萬世也已公孫朝其知之雖然仲尼非徒學
文武也學文武之道將以行之也是故東周之
思與人存政舉之論每惓惓焉其心誠欲使咸
punctuated: 其有常學乎？亦將謂其有常師乎？子貢迺告之曰：子疑夫子之焉學哉？亦未知其得統于文武耳。盖文武生而道在文武，文武往而道在後人。道有大者，人之賢者則識之。謨烈之重光，固奕世之紹述也，而賢者有斯道焉，是道在賢者而未墜矣。道有小者，人之不賢者則識之。經制之緒餘，固後人之誦法也，而不賢者有斯道焉，是道在不賢而未墜矣。吾夫子于賢者學之，學道之大也，而又不遺其小，則賢其師而不專于賢也；于不賢者學之，學道之小也，而又盡其大，則不賢其師而不專于不賢也。道垂啓佑，恒得人以衍其盛，而合大小皆聖學之資；學切憲章，每因人以繼其傳，而隨賢否皆得師之益。夫子焉不學也？焉不師也？而亦何常之有哉？至是而文武之道在人者，又在夫子；未墜于地者，將昭垂于萬世也已。公孫朝其知之！雖然，仲尼非徒學文武也，學文武之道將以行之也。是故東周之思，與人存政舉之論，每惓惓焉，其心誠欲使咸
translation_en:
…that he had a fixed subject of study, or that he had a fixed teacher?

Zigong 子貢 thereupon told him: "Do you doubt from whom the Master learned? It is simply that you do not yet know that he received the line of transmission from King Wen 文王 and King Wu 武王. For when King Wen and King Wu were alive, the Way resided in King Wen and King Wu; once King Wen and King Wu passed away, the Way resided in people of later generations.

"In the Way there are major principles, and those among men who are worthy remember them. The renewed radiance of their counsels and achievements is indeed what successive generations have continued and transmitted; because the worthy possess this Way, the Way resides in the worthy and has not fallen to the ground. In the Way there are minor principles, and those among men who are not worthy remember them. The remaining threads of their institutions and regulations are indeed what later generations recite and model themselves upon; because the unworthy possess this Way, the Way resides in the unworthy and has not fallen to the ground.

"Our Master learns from the worthy—learning the major principles of the Way—and yet does not neglect the minor ones; thus the worthy are his teachers, yet he does not learn exclusively from the worthy. He learns from the unworthy—learning the minor principles of the Way—and yet exhausts the major ones; thus the unworthy are his teachers, yet he does not learn exclusively from the unworthy. The Way has been handed down to enlighten and aid later generations, always finding people to broaden its flourishing, so that combining the major and the minor, all serve as resources for sage learning. His learning is earnestly devoted to modeling himself on King Wen and King Wu, always relying on people to continue its transmission, so that whether worthy or unworthy, from all he gains the benefit of a teacher. From whom did the Master not learn? Whom did he not take as a teacher? And what fixed teacher could he have?

"At this point, the Way of King Wen and King Wu that resided in others came to reside once more in the Master; that which had not fallen to the ground would be luminously handed down for ten thousand generations! May Gongsun Chao 公孫朝 understand this!"

Even so, Zhongni 仲尼 (Confucius) did not merely study King Wen and King Wu; he studied the Way of King Wen and King Wu with the intention of putting it into practice. Therefore, in his thoughts of making an Eastern Zhou 東周 and in his discourse on how government flourishes when the right men are present, he was always earnestly devoted, for in his heart he truly wished to cause the…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
和永清之治復見于今日而所學不徒託之空
言也已故君子觀于夢寐周公而益信吾夫子
師文武之心
詩曰妻子好合如鼓瑟琴兄弟旣翕和樂
且耽宜爾室家樂爾妻帑子曰父母其
順矣乎
梁爲熹
同考試官教諭梁批詞旨明透進道之序躍
然
===
同考試官教諭侯批講詩詞聖言渾融雅暢
而道之序自見傑作也
考試官訓導唐批見深語到
考試官教諭鄭批精醇
中庸引言道之行於家而進道之序見矣夫宜
家而親因以順焉道之行於家者然也觀此而
進道之序不有明徵乎中庸明費隱也意謂風
化之自始于家庭故善觀道者觀諸家而已嘗
即道行于家者觀之而知進道之有序焉彼常
punctuated:
和永清之治，復見于今日，而所學不徒託之空言也已。故君子觀于夢寐周公，而益信吾夫子師文武之心。

《詩》曰：「妻子好合，如鼓瑟琴；兄弟旣翕，和樂且耽。宜爾室家，樂爾妻帑。」子曰：「父母其順矣乎！」
梁爲熹
同考試官教諭梁批：詞旨明透，進道之序躍然。
同考試官教諭侯批：講詩詞、聖言渾融雅暢，而道之序自見，傑作也。
考試官訓導唐批：見深語到。
考試官教諭鄭批：精醇。

《中庸》引言道之行於家，而進道之序見矣。夫宜家而親因以順焉，道之行於家者然也。觀此，而進道之序不有明徵乎？《中庸》明費隱也，意謂風化之自始于家庭，故善觀道者觀諸家而已。嘗即道行于家者觀之，而知進道之有序焉。彼《常
translation_en:
… harmonious and eternally tranquil governance be seen again in the present day, so that what he learned would not be merely consigned to empty words. Therefore, when the gentleman observes his dreaming of the Duke of Zhou, he believes all the more in our Master's intent in taking Kings Wen and Wu as his teachers.

The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: "Loving union with wife and children is like the strumming of zithers and lutes; when brothers are in harmony, there is peaceful joy and great delight. Thus you bring order to your family and household, and give joy to your wife and children." The Master said: "How utterly contented the parents will be!"
By Liang Weixi 梁爲熹.
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Liang: The phrasing and meaning are clear and penetrating; the sequence of advancing in the Way leaps vividly to life.
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Hou: It expounds the words of the Ode and the sayings of the Sage with seamless, elegant fluency, while the sequence of the Way naturally manifests itself—a masterpiece.
Comment by Examiner Assistant Instructor Tang: Deep in insight and apt in expression.
Comment by Examiner County Director of Studies Zheng: Refined and pure.

The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) cites words showing how the Way is practiced in the family, and thus the sequence of advancing in the Way becomes evident. Indeed, when one brings order to the family and the parents are thereby contented, such is how the Way is practiced in the family. Observing this, is there not clear proof of the sequence of advancing in the Way? In elucidating how the Way is both vast in reach and subtle in essence, the Doctrine of the Mean means to say that the origin of moral transformation begins within the family household; therefore, those who are skilled at observing the Way simply observe it in the family. When we examine it through how the Way is practiced in the family, we know that there is a sequence to advancing in the Way. That Ode "Cherry-tree…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
棣之詩爲宜家而發也言妻子之合而有鼓瑟
琴之和言兄弟之翕而有樂且耽之美室家之
宜妻帑之樂胥此矣是詩也特妻子兄弟之詠
而未及於父母也乃夫子則謂其父母之可順
焉何哉蓋妻子兄弟之身未始不與父母相聯
屬則父母之心亦未始不與妻子兄弟相流通
者也玆惟道隆于家而一家之恩義既交孚而
罔間則心通于親而一念之豫順自浹洽而無
違好合妻子之心也亦父母之心也而和於妻
===
子者不可必其和於父母乎允若之化固自其
刑于者基之矣既翕兄弟之願也亦父母之願
也而宜於兄弟者不可必其宜於父母乎底豫
之風固自其友于者始之矣然則詩人所詠其
㫖深哉吁君子觀道於妻子兄弟而思順親之
化又觀道於父母而思聚順之原則道之行遠
自邇登高自卑也此其一徵矣乎雖然宜家之
驗非止順親已也推而極之雖天下之順亦不
外此蓋化行自近而正家固正天下之本也𫝊
punctuated: 棣之詩，爲宜家而發也。言妻子之合，而有「鼓瑟琴」之和；言兄弟之翕，而有「樂且耽」之美。「室家之宜」、「妻帑之樂」，胥此矣。是詩也，特妻子、兄弟之詠，而未及於父母也；乃夫子則謂其父母之可順焉，何哉？蓋妻子、兄弟之身，未始不與父母相聯屬；則父母之心，亦未始不與妻子、兄弟相流通者也。玆惟道隆于家，而一家之恩義既交孚而罔間；則心通于親，而一念之豫順自浹洽而無違。「好合」，妻子之心也，亦父母之心也；而和於妻子者，不可必其和於父母乎？允若之化，固自其「刑于」者基之矣。「既翕」，兄弟之願也，亦父母之願也；而宜於兄弟者，不可必其宜於父母乎？底豫之風，固自其「友于」者始之矣。然則詩人所詠，其㫖深哉！吁！君子觀道於妻子、兄弟，而思順親之化；又觀道於父母，而思聚順之原，則道之「行遠自邇，登高自卑」也，此其一徵矣乎！雖然，宜家之驗，非止順親已也；推而極之，雖天下之順，亦不外此。蓋化行自近，而正家固正天下之本也。𫝊
translation_en: … Ode of the Cherry Tree ("Changdi") was composed to express bringing harmony to the household. It speaks of the union with wife and children, having the harmony of "strumming zithers and lutes"; it speaks of the concord among brothers, having the beauty of "rejoicing and delighting." "Ordering well one's household" and "bringing joy to one's wife and children" are all encompassed in this. This ode is merely a song about wives, children, and brothers, without yet mentioning parents; yet the Master said that through this, one's parents will be in accord and pleased—why is that? It is because the persons of wives, children, and brothers have never failed to be interconnected with parents, and thus the hearts of parents have likewise never failed to flow in sympathy with wives, children, and brothers. Now, only when the Way flourishes within the home, and the affection and righteousness of the whole family are mutually trusted without rift, will one's heart communicate with one's parents, and the joyful accord of a single thought will naturally permeate without discrepancy. "Loving union" is the heart of wife and children, and it is also the heart of parents; for one who is harmonious with wife and children, may we not be certain of his harmony with his parents? The transformation of sincere compliance is indeed founded upon "setting an example for one's wife." "Being in concord" is the wish of brothers, and it is also the wish of parents; for one who does right by his brothers, may we not be certain of his doing right by his parents? The custom of bringing parents to delight indeed begins with "brotherly affection." This being so, how profound is the purport of what the poet sang! Ah! When the gentleman observes the Way among wives, children, and brothers, and contemplates the transformation that brings accord to parents; and when he further observes the Way in relation to parents, and contemplates the source of gathered compliance—that the Way "to go far must start from what is near, and to ascend high must start from what is low," is this not one proof of it? Even so, the efficacy of ordering the household does not stop merely at pleasing one's parents; extended to the utmost, even the compliance of the whole world is nothing outside of this. For moral transformation proceeds from what is near, and rectifying the family is truly the root of rectifying the world. Having…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
讀詩至文王之化御于家邦而必本諸刑于其
義不亦深切著明矣乎有家國天下之責者當
自得之
士之仕也猶農夫之耕也農夫豈爲出疆
舍其耒耜哉
陳見龍
同考試官教諭李批發揮載質意親切且體
格醇正思致俊拔佳士也取之
同考試官教諭梁批是題口氣最難體貼而
===
平正冠冕卓爾大雅獨見此作取之
考試官訓導唐批典雅純粹
考試官教諭鄭批典確
士必載質而出例之農可知也夫士必仕載質
所以仕也不然是農夫而舍耒耜矣可乎哉孟
子例言以曉周霄者意曰君子之在天下謂道
不可以不行故身在必出謂身不容以苟就故
進必以禮子疑士之載質也亦卽農夫觀之乎
蓋士謀道者也以道爲志則得之不忍私其身
punctuated:
讀《詩》至「文王之化御于家邦」，而必本諸「刑于」，其義不亦深切著明矣乎！有家國天下之責者，當自得之。
「士之仕也，猶農夫之耕也；農夫豈爲出疆舍其耒耜哉？」
陳見龍
同考試官教諭李批：發揮「載質」意親切，且體格醇正，思致俊拔，佳士也。取之。
同考試官教諭梁批：是題口氣最難體貼，而平正冠冕，卓爾大雅，獨見此作。取之。
考試官訓導唐批：典雅純粹。
考試官教諭鄭批：典確。
士必載質而出，例之農可知也。夫士必仕，載質所以仕也；不然，是農夫而舍耒耜矣，可乎哉？孟子例言以曉周霄者，意曰：君子之在天下，謂道不可以不行，故身在必出；謂身不容以苟就，故進必以禮。子疑士之載質也，亦卽農夫觀之乎？蓋士，謀道者也，以道爲志，則得之不忍私其身，
translation_en:
… When reading the Book of Odes (Shi) up to the passage where King Wen’s transforming influence governed his family and state, and seeing that it necessarily took root in setting an example for his consort, is its meaning not deeply incisive and brilliantly clear! Those who bear the responsibility for family, state, and All Under Heaven ought to grasp this for themselves.

"A scholar-official's taking office is like a farmer's plowing; would a farmer cast aside his plowshare and handle just because he is crossing a border?"

Chen Jianlong 陳見龍
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li 李 comments: It develops the meaning of "carrying ceremonial gifts of introduction" intimately and aptly; moreover, its formal structure is pure and proper, and its train of thought is outstanding and elevated—a fine scholar! Selected.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Liang 梁 comments: The tone of this topic is most difficult to capture empathetically, yet in this piece alone one sees a balanced, dignified, and surpassingly refined elegance. Selected.
Examiner and Assistant Instructor Tang 唐 comments: Classically elegant and pure.
Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭 comments: Classical and precise.

That a scholar-official must carry ceremonial gifts of introduction when going forth can be understood by analogy with the farmer. Now, a scholar-official must serve in office, and carrying ceremonial gifts is the means by which he enters office; otherwise, he would be like a farmer who casts aside his plowshare and handle—how could that be permissible? What Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) meant in speaking by analogy to enlighten Zhou Xiao 周霄 was this: When a gentleman is in the world, he holds that the Way cannot go unpracticed, and therefore, so long as he lives, he must go forth to serve; yet he also holds that his person must not casually take up a post, and therefore his advancement must accord with ritual propriety. Since you doubt why a scholar-official carries ceremonial gifts when going forth, why not simply observe the case of the farmer? For the scholar-official is one who seeks the Way; taking the Way as his aspiration, once he attains it he cannot bear to keep it privately for himself, …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而皇皇然思以應廟廊之求者其心也固無論
其出疆與否而皆然也猶之農夫謀食者也以
食爲念則求之無敢愛其力而汲汲然思以盡
甽畝之務者其心也亦無論其出疆與否而皆
然也然士欲仕而仕之禮質是已農欲耕而耕
之具耒耜是已使農之耒耜可以出疆舍則士
之質亦可以無載也孰知農夫之出旣不擇地
而耕則耒耜之用豈爲出疆而舍百畝之不易
彼誠憂之則凡所以爲明農計者必有身出而
===
器與之俱矣况士將委質人國者而可一日廢
先資之信哉百穀之未播彼誠念之則凡所以
爲力穡謀者必有身往而器與之偕矣况士將
傳質爲臣者而可一日廢見君之禮哉蓋良農
能耕不能使耕之舍乎耒耜彼舍焉者不欲耕
者也非農之常也君子能仕不能使仕之不載
乎質彼不載焉者不欲仕者也非士之常也知
乎此而君子之載質可無疑矣噫孟氏之梁之
齊出疆者數矣而卒不合豈獨無質哉非堯舜
punctuated: 而皇皇然思以應廟廊之求者，其心也，固無論其出疆與否而皆然也。猶之農夫謀食者也，以食爲念，則求之無敢愛其力，而汲汲然思以盡甽畝之務者，其心也，亦無論其出疆與否而皆然也。然士欲仕，而仕之禮，質是已；農欲耕，而耕之具，耒耜是已。使農之耒耜可以出疆舍，則士之質亦可以無載也。孰知農夫之出，旣不擇地而耕，則耒耜之用，豈爲出疆而舍？百畝之不易，彼誠憂之，則凡所以爲明農計者，必有身出而器與之俱矣；况士將委質人國者，而可一日廢先資之信哉？百穀之未播，彼誠念之，則凡所以爲力穡謀者，必有身往而器與之偕矣；况士將傳質爲臣者，而可一日廢見君之禮哉？蓋良農能耕，不能使耕之舍乎耒耜，彼舍焉者，不欲耕者也，非農之常也；君子能仕，不能使仕之不載乎質，彼不載焉者，不欲仕者也，非士之常也。知乎此，而君子之載質可無疑矣。噫！孟氏之梁、之齊，出疆者數矣，而卒不合，豈獨無質哉？非堯、舜
translation_en: …and anxiously seeks to answer the call of the court—such is his heart, and it is certainly so regardless of whether he crosses the border or not. It is just like the farmer, who plans for food: taking food as his concern, in seeking it he dares not spare his strength, and eagerly seeks to fulfill his duties in the fields—such is his heart, and it too is so regardless of whether he crosses the border or not. Now, the scholar wishes to take office, and the rite for taking office is the introductory gift; the farmer wishes to plow, and the implements for plowing are the plowhandle and plowshare. Suppose a farmer's plowhandle and plowshare could be left behind when crossing the border; then a scholar's introductory gift could also go uncarried. Who does not know that when a farmer goes forth, since he does not pick and choose the land before plowing, how could the use of his plowhandle and plowshare be abandoned just because he crosses a border? If he truly worries that his hundred mu of land are not well-tilled, then in all his plans for husbandry, whenever he goes out in person, his tools must surely go with him; how much more so for a scholar who is about to pledge himself in service to another state—could he for a single day dispense with the token of good faith presented in advance? If the farmer truly bears in mind that the hundred grains are not yet sown, then in all his counsels for diligent farming, whenever he goes forth in person, his tools must surely accompany him; how much more so for a scholar who is about to present his gift to become a minister—could he for a single day dispense with the rite of audiencia with a ruler? Indeed, a good farmer is able to plow, but he cannot make plowing dispense with the plowhandle and plowshare; one who leaves them behind is someone who does not wish to plow, which is not the normal way of a farmer. A gentleman is able to serve in office, but he cannot make serving in office dispense with carrying an introductory gift; one who does not carry it is someone who does not wish to serve, which is not the normal way of a scholar. Understand this, and there can be no doubt about the gentleman's carrying of an introductory gift. Alas! Mencius went to Liang and went to Qi, crossing the borders several times, yet in the end he did not find a match—was it because he alone had no introductory gift? Unless it was the Way of Yao and Shun…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之道不陳非仁義之猷不言是孟氏之質也吾
能載質以待用而不能必人之我用用不用人
也孟氏則俟之而已胡肯以輕售也噫是又孔
氏家法也
易
君子黃中通理正位居體
吳國光
同考試官學正趙批場中發中順類多支蔓
子能刋落陳言直攄心蘊深于易者錄之
===
同考試官教諭李批剟琱追雅不厭咀嚼
考試官訓導唐批潔淨
考試官教諭鄭批純正
文言著君子中順之德所以釋黃裳之義也夫
黃中而通理中也正位而居體順也合而觀之
黃裳之義明矣甞謂人君之所貴者德而君德
之所貴者則有要也六五之所以取象于黃裳
者何哉吾有以觀其深矣彼人君以一人而建
極于上其德尚中自夫或失則偏非中也非可
punctuated:
之道不陳，非仁義之猷不言，是孟氏之質也。吾能載質以待用，而不能必人之我用。用不用，人也；孟氏則俟之而已，胡肯以輕售也？噫！是又孔氏家法也。

《易》
「君子黃中通理，正位居體。」
吳國光
同考試官學正趙批：場中發中順類多支蔓，子能刋落陳言，直攄心蘊，深于《易》者。錄之。
同考試官教諭李批：剟琱追雅，不厭咀嚼。
考試官訓導唐批：潔淨。
考試官教諭鄭批：純正。

《文言》著君子中順之德，所以釋「黃裳」之義也。夫「黃中」而「通理」，中也；「正位」而「居體」，順也。合而觀之，「黃裳」之義明矣。甞謂人君之所貴者德，而君德之所貴者則有要也。六五之所以取象于「黃裳」者何哉？吾有以觀其深矣。彼人君以一人而建極于上，其德尚中。自夫或失則偏，非中也，非可
translation_en:
… the Way [of Yao and Shun], he did not set it forth; if it was not a plan of benevolence and righteousness, he did not speak of it—such was the introductory gift of Mencius. One can carry one's gift and wait to be employed, yet one cannot compel others to employ one. Whether one is employed or not rests with others; Mencius simply waited for it—how would he be willing to sell himself lightly? Alas! This too was the family tradition of Confucius.

Book of Changes (Yi)
"The superior man is yellow and central, penetrating the patterns; he occupies the correct position and abides in the body."
By Wu Guoguang 吳國光.
Associate Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Zhao 趙 comments: In the examination hall, essays expounding upon centrality and compliance were mostly rambling and diffuse. You were able to pare away clichés and directly express the inner store of your mind—one who is profound in the Book of Changes. Recorded.
Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Li 李 comments: Chiseling away ornate artifice to pursue elegance; one never tires of savoring it.
Examiner Assistant Instructor Tang 唐 comments: Lucid and pure.
Examiner County Director of Studies Zheng 鄭 comments: Pure and orthodox.

The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) sets forth the superior man's virtues of centrality and compliance in order to explain the meaning of "a yellow lower garment." Now, to be "yellow and central" and "penetrating the patterns" is centrality; to "occupy the correct position" and "abide in the body" is compliance. Viewed together, the meaning of "a yellow lower garment" becomes clear. I have always held that what a ruler values is virtue, and what is valued in a ruler's virtue has its essentials. Why is it that the Six in the Fifth place takes its image from "a yellow lower garment"? I have a way to observe its depth. When the ruler, as one man, establishes the supreme standard above, his virtue prizes centrality. Once he errs and becomes one-sided, it is not centrality, nor can it…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以語黃也惟君子則精一之功以純而德之在
內者立天下之大中焉語中之統體則萬理貫
徹而不遺何若是其通也語中之散殊則脉絡
分明而不亂何若是其理也合之大而析之精
而天然自有之妙會于君子之心矣是故以中
德而象於黃也謂其色之中也人君以一人而
正位于上其德尚順自夫或失則戾非順也非
可以語裳也惟君子則謙遜之衷恒存而位之
所居者布天下之大順焉貴為天子而虛其心
===
以禮天下之士待臣之體則然也尊為元后而
抑其心以下天下之人待民之體則然也位愈
高而德愈下而柔嘉巽順之懿達于君子之身
矣是故以順德而象于裳也謂其飾之下也要
之中存于內立其體也而實為順之基順見于
外達其用也而實為中之驗觀此而黃裳之義
寧有餘蘊哉愚甞仰稽于古譚治道之盛者莫
過于堯舜君德之盛亦莫過于堯舜也二典所
稱曰允執厥中曰溫恭克讓夫非中順主哉而
punctuated: 以語黃也。惟君子則精一之功以純，而德之在內者，立天下之大中焉。語中之統體，則萬理貫徹而不遺，何若是其通也？語中之散殊，則脉絡分明而不亂，何若是其理也？合之大而析之精，而天然自有之妙，會于君子之心矣。是故以中德而象於黃也，謂其色之中也。人君以一人而正位于上，其德尚順。自夫或失則戾，非順也，非可以語裳也。惟君子則謙遜之衷恒存，而位之所居者，布天下之大順焉。貴為天子，而虛其心以禮天下之士，待臣之體則然也；尊為元后，而抑其心以下天下之人，待民之體則然也。位愈高而德愈下，而柔嘉巽順之懿，達于君子之身矣。是故以順德而象于裳也，謂其飾之下也。要之，中存于內，立其體也，而實為順之基；順見于外，達其用也，而實為中之驗。觀此，而黃裳之義寧有餘蘊哉？愚甞仰稽于古，譚治道之盛者，莫過于堯舜；君德之盛，亦莫過于堯舜也。《二典》所稱曰「允執厥中」，曰「溫恭克讓」，夫非中順主哉？而
translation_en:
… speak of "yellow." Only with the superior man is the effort of refinement and single-mindedness pure, so that the virtue within him establishes the great centrality of the world. Speaking of centrality as a unified whole, the myriad principles penetrate throughout without omission—how could it be so pervasive? Speaking of centrality in its varied particulars, the veins and threads are distinct without confusion—how could it be so orderly? Vast when combined and subtle when analyzed, its natural, inherent wonder converges in the mind of the superior man. Therefore, central virtue is symbolized by yellow, referring to its being the central color.

When a ruler, as one man, occupies the correct position above, his virtue prizes compliance. Once he errs and becomes refractory, it is not compliance, and one cannot speak of the "lower garment." Only with the superior man is an inner heart of humility and deference constantly preserved, so that from the position he occupies he spreads great compliance throughout the world. Noble as the Son of Heaven, he empties his mind to treat the scholars of the world with courtesy—such is the proper form for treating ministers. Exalted as the supreme sovereign, he restrains his mind to humble himself before the people of the world—such is the proper form for treating the people. The higher his position, the lowlier his virtue, and the excellence of gentle goodness and humble compliance is realized in the person of the superior man. Therefore, compliant virtue is symbolized by the lower garment, referring to its being the lower ornament.

In sum, centrality is preserved within, establishing the substance, and in fact serves as the foundation of compliance; compliance is manifested without, extending the function, and in fact serves as the verification of centrality. Viewing it thus, how could there be any remaining profundity in the meaning of "a yellow lower garment" left unexpressed?

I have respectfully examined antiquity: among those who discuss the flourishing of the way of governance, none surpass Yao and Shun; and in the flourishing of ruler's virtue, none surpass Yao and Shun either. What the Two Canons praise as "sincerely hold fast the Mean" and "gentle, respectful, and capable of yielding"—were they not masters of centrality and compliance? And when one …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
窺其原則兢兢業業爲之也然則欲全中順之
德可無主敬之心乎故曰敬者聖學之所以成
始而成終也
言行君子之樞機樞機之發榮辱之主也
陳建中
同考試官教諭李批樞機二字講多未融是
篇精暢古雅不羣經義之佳者
考試官訓導唐批精致
考試官教諭鄭批瑩潤
===
大傳喻言行之切於人而明其所係之重焉夫
善否不同而榮辱因之是所係固甚重也君子
於言行其可苟焉而已哉大傳什中孚九二爻
義如此今夫中孚之理妙於感通而感通之要
存乎言行人之忽於言行而不加擬議之功者
亦未審其所係之何如耳彼樞運而戶斯闢機
動而矢斯隨言天下之至速者莫喻於此矣今
言出乎身卽加乎民觸則必應若有所轉移於
其間是言焉一樞機也行發乎邇卽見乎遠感
punctuated:
窺其原，則兢兢業業爲之也。然則欲全中順之德，可無主敬之心乎？故曰：「敬者，聖學之所以成始而成終也。」

「言行，君子之樞機；樞機之發，榮辱之主也。」

陳建中
同考試官教諭李批：樞機二字，講多未融；是篇精暢古雅不羣，經義之佳者。
考試官訓導唐批：精致。
考試官教諭鄭批：瑩潤。

《大傳》喻言行之切於人，而明其所係之重焉。夫善否不同而榮辱因之，是所係固甚重也；君子於言行，其可苟焉而已哉？《大傳》什《中孚》九二爻義如此。今夫中孚之理妙於感通，而感通之要存乎言行。人之忽於言行而不加擬議之功者，亦未審其所係之何如耳。彼樞運而戶斯闢，機動而矢斯隨，言天下之至速者莫喻於此矣。今言出乎身，卽加乎民，觸則必應，若有所轉移於其間，是言焉一樞機也；行發乎邇，卽見乎遠，感…
translation_en:
…when we look into their source, they practiced it through cautious and conscientious effort. This being so, if one wishes to perfect the virtues of centrality and compliance, how can one lack a mind anchored in reverence? Therefore it is said: "Reverence is that whereby the learning of the sages completes both the beginning and the end."

"Words and deeds are the hinge and trigger of the noble man; the release of the hinge and trigger is the master of glory and disgrace."

Chen Jianzhong 陳建中
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li 李 comments: Most candidates failed to smoothly integrate their explanations of the two words "hinge and trigger" (shuji 樞機); this essay is refined, fluent, classically elegant, and outstanding—a fine example of an exposition on the Classics.
Examiner and Assistant Instructor Tang 唐 comments: Refined and meticulous.
Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭 comments: Lustrous and polished.

The Great Commentary (Dazhuan 大傳) uses a metaphor to show how intimately words and deeds pertain to a person, and clarifies the gravity of what depends on them. Now, because good and bad differ and glory or disgrace follows accordingly, what depends on them is truly of great weight; how then could the noble man be careless in his words and deeds? Such is the Great Commentary's explanation [什, graphic error for 釋] of the meaning of the second yang line of the Zhongfu 中孚 (Inner Trust) hexagram. Now, the principle of inner trust is wondrous in its capacity to move and connect, and the essential key to moving and connecting lies in words and deeds. Those who are negligent in their words and deeds and fail to apply the effort of deliberation and discussion simply have not examined what really depends on them. When a hinge turns, the door opens; when a crossbow trigger moves, the arrow immediately follows—in speaking of the swiftest things in the world, nothing illustrates it better than this. Now when words go forth from one's person, they immediately affect the people; once touched, there is bound to be a response, as though something were shifting them from within—thus words are a hinge and trigger. When deeds are initiated nearby, they immediately become visible far away; once moved…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則必孚若有所斡旋於其內是行為一樞機也
樞機之發所係豈其微哉自其應之於千里之
外也言而民信行而民悅何榮也顧榮非自榮
而樞機之善實為榮之主焉善為主則榮為應
人情莫不欲榮也而孰知主是榮者之有所在
乎自其違之於千里之外也令之而不從推之
而不協何辱也顧辱非自辱而樞機之不善實
為辱之主焉不善為主則辱為應人情莫不惡
辱也而孰知主是辱者之有所存乎夫樞機為
===
榮之主是榮固自已求之也樞機為辱之主是
辱亦自已求之也觀其所主而擬議以致其慎
者信乎其不容緩矣雖然慎之之功非可以襲
取焉也古之君子豫養於暗室屋漏之中不動
而敬不言而信故孚誠所積而潛通默喻捷於
響桴若養之不豫直取一言一動而矯飾之乃
曰吾將如是而化邦如是而格豚魚也亦繆於
中孚之旨矣
書
punctuated:
則必孚，若有所斡旋於其內，是行為一樞機也。樞機之發，所係豈其微哉？自其應之於千里之外也，言而民信，行而民悅，何榮也！顧榮非自榮，而樞機之善實為榮之主焉。善為主，則榮為應。人情莫不欲榮也，而孰知主是榮者之有所在乎？自其違之於千里之外也，令之而不從，推之而不協，何辱也！顧辱非自辱，而樞機之不善實為辱之主焉。不善為主，則辱為應。人情莫不惡辱也，而孰知主是辱者之有所存乎？夫樞機為榮之主，是榮固自已求之也；樞機為辱之主，是辱亦自已求之也。觀其所主，而擬議以致其慎者，信乎其不容緩矣。雖然，慎之之功，非可以襲取焉也。古之君子，豫養於暗室屋漏之中，不動而敬，不言而信。故孚誠所積，而潛通默喻，捷於響桴。若養之不豫，直取一言一動而矯飾之，乃曰「吾將如是而化邦，如是而格豚魚也」，亦繆於《中孚》之旨矣。
書
translation_en:
… when they are moved, they will surely be inspired with trust, as though there were something directing things from within—thus conduct is a pivot and trigger. When the pivot and trigger are set in motion, how could what depends upon them be slight?

Viewed from the way they are responded to from a thousand *li* away: one speaks and the people believe, one acts and the people rejoice—what glory this is! Yet glory does not come of itself; the goodness of the pivot and trigger is in truth the master of glory. When goodness is the master, glory is the response. In human feeling, no one does not desire glory, yet who knows that there is something in which the master of this glory resides? Viewed from the way they are defied from a thousand *li* away: one commands them and they do not obey, one extends things to them and they do not harmonize—what disgrace this is! Yet disgrace does not come of itself; the lack of goodness of the pivot and trigger is in truth the master of disgrace. When lack of goodness is the master, disgrace is the response. In human feeling, no one does not hate disgrace, yet who knows that there is something in which the master of this disgrace abides?

Now, since the pivot and trigger are the master of glory, glory is assuredly sought from within oneself; and since the pivot and trigger are the master of disgrace, disgrace is likewise sought from within oneself. Observing what they master, and deliberating and discussing so as to exercise the utmost caution—truly this brooks no delay! Even so, the work of exercising caution cannot be seized through outward contrivance. The noble man of antiquity cultivated himself beforehand in the unseen corners of a dark room, reverent before even making a move, trustworthy before even uttering a word. Therefore, through the accumulation of sincere trust, unseen communication and silent understanding were swifter than an echo or the strike of a drumstick. If one does not cultivate oneself beforehand, and merely takes each single word and each single movement and artificially adorns them, saying, "By doing thus I shall transform the state, and by doing thus I shall move even pigs and fishes," this too goes against the purport of the hexagram Inner Trust (*Zhongfu*).

Book of Documents (*Shu*)

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
稽于衆舍己從人不虐無告不廢困窮
黃希奭
同考試官訓導劉批意亮詞徹明良克艱之
意躍然在目可以式矣
考試官訓導唐批發克艱意超脫可誦錄
之
考試官教諭鄭批簡鬯
虞聖歷舉克艱之事見效之所由致也蓋有其
效者必有其事也使非忘私愛民好士之至何
===
以臻至治之效哉帝舜言此將以歸美于堯也
意謂人君統治于上善吾善焉民吾民焉賢吾
賢焉而欲盡道其間亦甚難也允能克艱效莫
大矣然其事何如彼嘉言至賾若難乎廣延也
今日罔伏則入告悉一時之謀猷矣而曷以臻
此必其咨訪心虛有得於稽衆之公從善量廣
無有于舍己之吝夫稽衆可能也而舍己以從
之則忘私之至矣持此心以樂取天下善尚有
懷讜論而不欲盡者耶萬民至衆若難乎得所
punctuated:
「稽于衆，舍己從人，不虐無告，不廢困窮。」
黃希奭
同考試官訓導劉批：意亮詞徹，明良克艱之意躍然在目，可以式矣。
考試官訓導唐批：發克艱意，超脫可誦，錄之。
考試官教諭鄭批：簡鬯。
虞聖歷舉克艱之事，見效之所由致也。蓋有其效者，必有其事也。使非忘私、愛民、好士之至，何以臻至治之效哉？帝舜言此，將以歸美于堯也。意謂：人君統治于上，善吾善焉，民吾民焉，賢吾賢焉，而欲盡道其間，亦甚難也。允能克艱，效莫大矣。然其事何如？彼嘉言至賾，若難乎廣延也。今日「罔伏」，則入告悉一時之謀猷矣，而曷以臻此？必其咨訪心虛，有得於稽衆之公；從善量廣，無有于舍己之吝。夫稽衆可能也，而舍己以從之，則忘私之至矣。持此心以樂取天下善，尚有懷讜論而不欲盡者耶？萬民至衆，若難乎得所…
translation_en:
"He consulted the multitude, setting aside his own views to follow others; he did not oppress the helpless, nor did he neglect the straitened and poor." [Book of Documents (Shujing), "Counsels of the Great Yu"]

Huang Xishi 黃希奭

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Liu comments: The conception is bright and the diction penetrating. The spirit of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers overcoming the difficulties of their offices leaps right before the eyes; it may serve as a model.
Examiner, Assistant Instructor Tang comments: It brings out the meaning of overcoming the difficulties of office in a transcendent and recitable manner. Record it for publication.
Examiner, Instructor Zheng comments: Concise and fluent.

The sage of Yu [Shun] enumerates in turn the deeds of overcoming the difficulties of office, showing whereby such efficacy was brought about. For wherever there is an effect, there must be the corresponding deeds. Were it not for the utmost selflessness, love of the people, and fondness for worthy men, how could the efficacy of supreme governance be attained? Emperor Shun spoke these words intending to attribute this perfection to Yao.

His meaning was as follows: When a ruler exercises supreme governance from above, the good is his good, the people are his people, and the worthy are his worthies—yet to fulfill the Way completely among them is exceedingly difficult. If one is truly able to overcome these difficulties, no efficacy could be greater. Yet what are the actual deeds involved?

Those admirable words are most intricate and varied, so that it seems difficult to invite them broadly. Now, when it is said that "none were concealed," it means that the counsels brought in and reported encompassed all the plans and deliberations of the age—and how was this attained? Surely it was because in consulting and inquiring his mind was open, attaining the impartiality of consulting the multitude; and in following the good his capacity was broad, free from any grudging reluctance to set aside his own views. Now, consulting the multitude is something one may be able to do; but to set aside one's own views in order to follow them is the ultimate of forgetting self-interest. Holding fast to such a mind in gladly taking what is good from all under Heaven, would there still be anyone harboring upright counsels who did not wish to voice them in full?

The myriad people are most numerous, so that it seems difficult for all of them to find their proper place…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也今日咸寧則是至仁被一時之億兆矣而何
道以洽之必其恩深懷保而厚澤首加於窮民
德普惠鮮而苛政不及於無告夫不虐可能也
無告而不虐則愛民之至矣持此心以撫綏天
下民尚有失所而不獲安者耶賢人至無盡若
難乎悉致也今日無遺則是登崇盡一時之豪
傑矣而何道以徠之必其賢有可舉雖側陋而
必揚才有可用雖世類而不拘夫不廢可能也
困窮而不廢則好士之至矣持此心以鼓舞天
===
下士尚有抱其道而甘於在野者耶是爲言爲
民爲賢勢若至渙而難萃而取言愛民好士道
則克盡而無虧此道盡而效自因之矣斯帝堯
之所獨能而我君臣所當交勉者也吁舜之克
艱亦可見矣雖然舜之爲君好察邇言則罔伏
矣好生洽民則不虐矣闢門求賢則不廢矣而
顧爲是退託者何哉蓋聖心至虛視己能恒若
未能此所以治益治而聖益聖也後世夜前席
以納言行小惠以愛民亟問餽而好士視此可
punctuated: 也，今日「咸寧」，則是至仁被一時之億兆矣。而何道以洽之？必其恩深懷保，而厚澤首加於窮民；德普惠鮮，而苛政不及於無告。夫不虐可能也，無告而不虐，則愛民之至矣。持此心以撫綏天下，民尚有失所而不獲安者耶？賢人至無盡，若難乎悉致也，今日「無遺」，則是登崇盡一時之豪傑矣。而何道以徠之？必其賢有可舉，雖側陋而必揚；才有可用，雖世類而不拘。夫不廢可能也，困窮而不廢，則好士之至矣。持此心以鼓舞天下，士尚有抱其道而甘於在野者耶？是爲言、爲民、爲賢，勢若至渙而難萃；而取言、愛民、好士，道則克盡而無虧。此道盡而效自因之矣，斯帝堯之所獨能，而我君臣所當交勉者也。吁！舜之克艱亦可見矣。雖然，舜之爲君，好察邇言，則罔伏矣；好生洽民，則不虐矣；闢門求賢，則不廢矣。而顧爲是退託者，何哉？蓋聖心至虛，視己能恒若未能，此所以治益治而聖益聖也。後世夜前席以納言，行小惠以愛民，亟問餽而好士，視此可
translation_en: … [difficult to ensure they find their proper place]; yet when today it is said that "all the myriad people enjoy peace," then supreme benevolence has extended to the millions of the age! And by what Way does one suffuse them with it? Surely one's grace runs deep in cherishing and protecting them, so that generous bounty is bestowed first upon the destitute; one's virtue is universal in showing kindness to the widowed and needy, so that harsh governance never reaches those who have no one to appeal to. Now, refraining from oppression is within reach; but not oppressing those who have no one to appeal to—that is the ultimate in loving the people. Holding fast to this mind to soothe and pacify All under Heaven, could there still be any among the people who lose their livelihood and fail to find peace? Worthy men are utterly inexhaustible, so it seems difficult to summon them all; yet when today it is said that "no worthy is left behind," then all the outstanding talents of the age have been elevated and honored! And by what Way does one attract them? Surely when there is worthiness fit to be promoted, even those of humble and obscure station are certain to be raised up; when there is talent fit to be employed, one is not bound by hereditary status or background. Now, refraining from neglect is within reach; but not neglecting those in distress and poverty—that is the ultimate in loving scholars. Holding fast to this mind to inspire All under Heaven, could there still be any among the scholars who clasp their Way to themselves and remain content to stay in the wilderness? Thus, with regard to words, the people, and the worthy, circumstances may seem utterly scattered and difficult to bring together; yet in adopting good words, loving the people, and loving scholars, the Way is fulfilled completely and without deficiency. Once this Way is fulfilled, the results naturally follow from it. This is what Emperor Yao alone was able to achieve, and what we, sovereign and ministers, ought mutually to strive after. Ah! How Shun understood the difficulty of his task can also be seen here. Even so, in Shun's rule as sovereign: he loved to examine near-at-hand words, so no good words were hidden; his love of life suffused the people, so the helpless were not oppressed; he threw open the gates of the four quarters to seek the worthy, so those in poverty were not neglected. Why then did he nevertheless make such modest disclaimers? It is because the mind of the sage is supremely humble, ever regarding what he is already capable of as though he had not yet achieved it; this is why his governance became ever better governed and his sageliness ever more sage. When rulers of later ages moved forward on their mats at night to receive advice, practiced petty favors to love the people, or sent frequent inquiries and gifts of food to show fondness for scholars, compared with this they might well…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以不愧矣
自殷王中宗及高宗及祖甲及我周文王
茲四人迪哲
陳紹虞
同考試官訓導唐批發揮迪哲二字理精詞
練經義之最佳者宜錄以式
考試官訓導唐批得周公告成王之旨
考試官教諭鄭批明實
大臣申言古人無逸之實惟行其所知而已夫
===
小人之依非知之難而行之難也商周盛王能
迪哲矣斯為無逸之實與周公申之以勉成王
也意謂君人者孰不思為小民計哉而率難善
治者凡以不知法古力行耳我思古人知民依
者有矣然知之而不能行猶弗知也矧曰其能
迪哲乎惟觀于殷有中宗高宗祖甲其人焉觀
于周有文王其人焉茲四人也本濬哲之神以
周悉乎民隱旣眞知而不遺推明哲之懿以善
體乎民情自允蹈而無歉治民祗懼中宗以之
punctuated:
以不愧矣。

自殷王中宗，及高宗，及祖甲，及我周文王，茲四人迪哲。
陳紹虞
同考試官訓導唐批：發揮「迪哲」二字，理精詞練，經義之最佳者，宜錄以式。
考試官訓導唐批：得周公告成王之旨。
考試官教諭鄭批：明實。

大臣申言古人無逸之實，惟行其所知而已。夫小人之依，非知之難，而行之難也。商、周盛王能迪哲矣，斯為無逸之實與！周公申之以勉成王也，意謂：君人者孰不思為小民計哉？而率難善治者，凡以不知法古力行耳。我思古人，知民依者有矣，然知之而不能行，猶弗知也，矧曰其能迪哲乎？惟觀于殷，有中宗、高宗、祖甲其人焉；觀于周，有文王其人焉。茲四人也，本濬哲之神，以周悉乎民隱，旣眞知而不遺；推明哲之懿，以善體乎民情，自允蹈而無歉。治民祗懼，中宗以之，
translation_en:
… not feel ashamed before this?

"From the Yin king Zhongzong, to Gaozong, to Zujia, and to our Zhou King Wen—these four men walked in wisdom." (Book of Documents, "Against Luxurious Ease" [Wuyi])
By Chen Shaoyu 陳紹虞.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Tang 唐: In elaborating on the two words "walked in wisdom" (dizhe 迪哲), the reasoning is refined and the diction polished. It is the finest of the essays on the Classics and ought to be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Assistant Instructor Tang 唐: It grasps the purport of the Duke of Zhou's admonition to King Cheng.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭: Clear and substantive.

When the great minister reiterated the reality of how the ancients avoided luxurious ease, it consisted solely in putting into practice what they knew. Now, as for what the common people depend upon, it is not knowing it that is difficult, but practicing it that is difficult. The flourishing kings of Shang and Zhou were able to walk in wisdom—was this not the very reality of avoiding luxurious ease! In reiterating this to encourage King Cheng, the Duke of Zhou meant to say: Who among rulers of men does not think of taking counsel for the common people? Yet the reason they generally find it difficult to achieve good governance is simply that they do not know how to emulate antiquity and strive in practice. When I reflect upon the ancients, there were indeed those who knew what the people depend upon; yet to know it and be unable to practice it is the same as not knowing it—how much less could one say that they were able to walk in wisdom? Only when we look to Yin, there were such men as Zhongzong, Gaozong, and Zujia; and when we look to Zhou, there was such a man as King Wen. These four men grounded themselves in the spirit of profound wisdom so as to thoroughly comprehend the hidden sufferings of the people, truly knowing them without oversight; and they extended the excellence of their clear wisdom so as to sympathetically embody the conditions of the people, naturally treading the path in earnest without deficiency. Governing the people with reverent caution—this Zhongzong practiced; …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而高宗之嘉靖殷邦亦能蹈其知焉思其艱必
圖其易而實德之孚于民者合先後而其揆一
也保惠庶民祖甲以之而文王之咸和萬民亦
能踐其知焉知其依必奠其麗而實惠之及于
民者協異代而其道同也以小民艱難之狀爲
九重獨見之猷而知之眞者又何甞不行之至
乎商周之際所以惠養黎元者其在斯矣舉閭
閻疾苦之情爲廟堂灼知之晢而察之精者又
何甞不行之力乎二代之盛所以造福生靈者
===
其在兹矣夫惟其迪哲也是三宗文王所以永
也可爲無逸者之法反是而不能迪哲也則非
所以紹前脩也寧不足爲嗣王戒哉吁周公之
忠愛亦云至矣雖然成王亦令主也而無逸之
訓邠風之作周公所爲惓惓而不置者豈過計
哉蓋周家以農事開國王業根本係焉周公欲
成王法祖爲政甞懼其以逸心乗之故也厥後
成王果能繼美文王四三宗而稱哲王焉何莫
非周公之功哉
punctuated: 而高宗之嘉靖殷邦，亦能蹈其知焉。思其艱，必圖其易，而實德之孚于民者，合先後而其揆一也。保惠庶民，祖甲以之；而文王之咸和萬民，亦能踐其知焉。知其依，必奠其麗，而實惠之及于民者，協異代而其道同也。以小民艱難之狀，爲九重獨見之猷，而知之眞者，又何甞不行之至乎？商周之際，所以惠養黎元者，其在斯矣。舉閭閻疾苦之情，爲廟堂灼知之晢，而察之精者，又何甞不行之力乎？二代之盛，所以造福生靈者，其在兹矣。夫惟其迪哲也，是三宗、文王所以永也，可爲無逸者之法；反是而不能迪哲也，則非所以紹前脩也，寧不足爲嗣王戒哉？吁！周公之忠愛亦云至矣。雖然，成王亦令主也，而《無逸》之訓、《邠風》之作，周公所爲惓惓而不置者，豈過計哉？蓋周家以農事開國，王業根本係焉。周公欲成王法祖爲政，甞懼其以逸心乗之故也。厥後成王果能繼美文王，四三宗而稱哲王焉，何莫非周公之功哉！
translation_en:
… while Gaozong, in bringing tranquil order to the state of Yin, was likewise able to put his knowledge into practice. Contemplating the hardships, they invariably planned for what would bring ease, so that in the way their substantial virtue won the trust of the people, earlier and later rulers followed the exact same principle.
