For even those of the highest wisdom cannot be entirely free of desires, while petty men are clever at spying out openings. How much more so when one occupies the exalted position of the Son of Heaven, facing the multitudes who surround him awaiting his commands, where a single word let slip [?] is echoed a thousand li away! Should there be a single moment of carelessness, how can one know that they will not strike at his mind with immortals, construction projects, magicians, and hounds and horses to make it extravagant and dissipated? Emperors Wu and Xuan of the Han, and Emperors Zhenzong and Shenzong of the Song, are clear mirrors of this.

Therefore, knowing how to maintain the mind, and also knowing how to be cautious to the end: if he relies upon the assistance and guidance of the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries, thoroughly examines the recitations and admonitions of the Palace Attendants and Advisors, investigates the substantive achievements of the Six Ministers, scrutinizes the counsels submitted by the Censorate and the Ministries, traces the rise and fall of the Six Dynasties, takes the institutions established by the Imperial Ancestors as a mirror, and furthermore illuminates the path of desirelessness, broadens the transformation of harmony and concord, clarifies the Way of spontaneity, surveys the meaning of the Six Arts, weighs the substance and refinement of Yu and Xia, determines what to abrogate and what to add from Yin and Zhou, and does not merely indulge in elaborate formalities to dazzle the eyes and ears of onlookers, but discards flashiness and chooses substance—then the whole world will clearly understand wherein the Sage's learning lies, the great transformation can be accomplished, ritual yielding can bepromoted, and even the flourishing ages of the Three Kings and Five Emperors could not surpass this!

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第二問
黃希奭
同考試官訓導唐批學術事功一原即漢唐
宋諸賢各有所得子獨闡明詳盡考據精確而末
叚尤見尚友之志取之
考試官訓導唐批學術事功原非二物世
儒岐而二之蓋未之深體也是作俯仰品隲得其
源委異日必能推學建功者取之
考試官教諭鄭批辨博峻整
===
夫所稱於天下爲大儒者必有振古之學
術而後有振古之事功要之學術事功非
二也古之學者天地之變動日月星辰之
運行萬物之散聚山川谿谷之險易阸塞
皇帝王伯之汙隆與夫墳典丘索陰符揣
摩奇正權變靡不習貫而用之以正出之
以時故雖勇奪三軍而不攘臂於睚眦之
小智蓋天下而不角勝於閭伍之間辯屈
羣策而不輕試於脣吻之末力高一世而
punctuated:
第二問
黃希奭
同考試官訓導唐批：學術事功一原，即漢、唐、宋諸賢各有所得。子獨闡明詳盡，考據精確，而末叚尤見尚友之志，取之。
考試官訓導唐批：學術事功，原非二物，世儒岐而二之，蓋未之深體也。是作俯仰品隲，得其源委，異日必能推學建功者，取之。
考試官教諭鄭批：辨博峻整。
夫所稱於天下爲大儒者，必有振古之學術，而後有振古之事功，要之學術事功非二也。古之學者，天地之變動，日月星辰之運行，萬物之散聚，山川谿谷之險易阸塞，皇、帝、王、伯之汙隆，與夫《墳》、《典》、《丘》、《索》、《陰符》、揣摩、奇正、權變，靡不習貫，而用之以正，出之以時。故雖勇奪三軍，而不攘臂於睚眦之小；智蓋天下，而不角勝於閭伍之間；辯屈羣策，而不輕試於脣吻之末；力高一世，而
translation_en:
Second Policy Question
Huang Xishi 黃希奭

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Tang 唐: "Scholarship and practical achievement share a single source, and the various worthies of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties each attained something of it. You alone have elucidated this thoroughly and exhaustively, with precise and accurate textual evidence, and the final section especially reveals an aspiration to befriend the ancients. Accepted."
Comment by Examiner and Assistant Instructor Tang 唐: "Scholarship and practical achievement are originally not two separate things; vulgar scholars of the world diverge and split them in two simply because they have not deeply embodied them. This essay surveys and evaluates past and present, grasping both their origins and developments. In the future he will surely be one who can extend his learning to establish achievements. Accepted."
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭: "Erudite in argument, lofty and well-ordered."

Now, those who are acclaimed throughout the empire as great Confucians must first possess scholarship that resonates through antiquity before they can achieve deeds that resonate through antiquity; in sum, scholarship and practical achievement are not two separate things. Among the scholars of antiquity—whether it was the transformations and movements of Heaven and Earth, the revolutions of the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, the dispersal and gathering of the myriad things, the strategic ruggedness, ease, and passes of mountains, rivers, streams, and valleys, the decline and flourishing of August Ones, Emperors, Kings, and Hegemons, as well as the Three Mounds (San fen), Five Canons (Wu dian), Eight索 (Ba suo), Nine Hills (Jiu qiu), the Hidden Tally (Yinfu), the art of gauging intentions, unorthodox and orthodox tactics, and expedient adaptation—there was nothing they did not thoroughly master, applying it with rectitude and bringing it forth at the proper time. Therefore, although their courage could strip the spirit from three armies, they would not roll up their sleeves over petty glares of resentment; although their wisdom covered the empire, they would not vie for victory among village lanes; although their eloquence could bend all counsels, they would not lightly test it in trivial verbal sparring; although their strength surpassed their generation, they would…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不爲舉鼎絕臏之事行必大道有時乎徑
竇可由約誓是尊有時乎要盟不信可經
可權可靜可動尸居而龍見雷聲而淵默
養其全鋒以待天下顧盼呼吸而豎峻偉
不羣之業其發也若機括其炳也若日月
掀揭照耀萬世之所咄嗟慨噫鼓掌而甘
心焉者也乃今之爲學術者好申一隅之
說多謬通方之論貴席上者以清淨爲腐
議束名實者以柱下爲誕詞從橫游談則
===
病其辯譎權謀功利則詆其詭曲吾以爲
才智有偏兼而其致用有遇合要以適時
應變取節焉耳矣夫玉卮無當賤於瓦缶
太阿不割不直鈆刀彼其侈談而無益於
用也何異哉至其語事功則又曰德衰於
符斗信折於繩契爲誕而已矣忠敞於管
晏質破於申韓爲名而已矣噫彼徒知上
古之不符斗不繩契而不知今之民則符
斗繩契之民也知其治之不必管晏申韓
punctuated: 不爲舉鼎絕臏之事。行必大道，有時乎徑竇可由；約誓是尊，有時乎要盟不信。可經可權，可靜可動，尸居而龍見，雷聲而淵默，養其全鋒以待天下，顧盼呼吸而豎峻偉不羣之業。其發也若機括，其炳也若日月，掀揭照耀，萬世之所咄嗟慨噫、鼓掌而甘心焉者也。乃今之爲學術者，好申一隅之說，多謬通方之論。貴席上者，以清淨爲腐議；束名實者，以柱下爲誕詞；從橫游談，則病其辯譎；權謀功利，則詆其詭曲。吾以爲才智有偏兼，而其致用有遇合，要以適時應變、取節焉耳矣。夫玉卮無當，賤於瓦缶；太阿不割，不直鈆刀。彼其侈談而無益於用也，何異哉？至其語事功，則又曰：「德衰於符斗，信折於繩契，爲誕而已矣；忠敞於管、晏，質破於申、韓，爲名而已矣。」噫！彼徒知上古之不符斗、不繩契，而不知今之民則符斗、繩契之民也；知其治之不必管、晏、申、韓，
translation_en:
… would not engage in such feats as lifting a tripod only to snap his kneecap. In conduct, he invariably walked the Great Way, yet at times a shortcut or side passage could be taken; covenants and oaths he held in honor, yet at times a coerced alliance would not be kept. Capable of adhering to the constant standard or exercising expedient adaptation, capable of stillness or action, sitting motionless like a ritual impersonator of the dead yet appearing like a dragon, thundering aloud yet silent as the abyss—he nourished his keen edge intact to await the needs of the world, and within the span of a glance or a breath established towering, extraordinary achievements. When he launched into action, it was like the release of a crossbow trigger; in his brilliance, he was like the sun and moon—uplifting and illuminating, someone over whom ten thousand generations exclaim and sigh in admiration, clapping their hands in wholehearted satisfaction.

Yet those who pursue learning today are fond of advancing one-sided doctrines and often err with respect to comprehensive views. Those who prize the treasures displayed upon the mat regard Daoist purity and quietude as stale talk; those who bind themselves to names and actualities regard the teachings of the Archivist Beneath the Pillar (Laozi) as absurd words. As for the wandering persuaders of the Vertical and Horizontal alliances, they fault them for specious and deceitful rhetoric; as for tactical calculation and utilitarian advantage, they disparage them as crooked and devious. In my view, talent and wisdom may be partial or comprehensive, and their practical application depends on opportunity and circumstance; the essential point is simply to suit the times, respond to change, and select what is appropriate in measure. Now, a jade goblet without a bottom is worth less than an earthen jar; if the great sword Tai'e cannot cut, it is worth no more than a lead knife. How are those who indulge in extravagant talk without being of any practical use any different from these?

When they speak of practical achievements, they go on to say: "Virtue declined with tallies and peck-measures, and trustworthiness was broken with knotted cords and notched tallies—such things are mere deceit! Loyalty was worn away[?] by Guan Zhong 管仲 and Yan Ying 晏嬰, and simplicity was shattered by Shen Buhai 申不害 and Han Fei 韓非—such things are mere pursuit of fame!" Alas! They merely know that high antiquity did not use tallies and peck-measures or knotted cords and notched tallies, without realizing that the people of today are a people of tallies, peck-measures, knotted cords, and notched tallies; they know that governance need not rely on Guan Zhong, Yan Ying, Shen Buhai, and Han Fei, …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而不知時之趨為申韓管晏也夫伏羲無
制令夏后氏不負言殷人誓周人盟今取
必於符斗繩契固不可而謂其盡廢符斗
繩契能爲治乎謂申韓管晏之為王道固
不可而謂其因俗適事無益於時也亦非
達權知變之論矣試卽古今所記述表著
者舉其一二上下之蓋自羲農而降語學
術則孔孟其人矣當其時反鄆讙墮三都
誅少正卯以及王齊反掌羞稱伯功事功
===
統是矣至於夾谷之會請具司馬井田世
祿推移於去籍之後此非其識時達變不
可以尺度拘也乎語事功則伊周其人也
當其時耕莘野樂堯舜一見而言素王九
主之事以及周禮太平之書兼三王施四
事則學術盡是矣至於鳴條之役東山之
舉以身當天下之大任而後世無異議當
時無貶詞又非其聖人之權而得於所養
者深乎故謂孔孟之專於學術伊周之專
punctuated: 而不知時之趨為申、韓、管、晏也。夫伏羲無制令，夏后氏不負言，殷人誓，周人盟。今取必於符斗繩契，固不可；而謂其盡廢符斗繩契能爲治乎？謂申、韓、管、晏之為王道，固不可；而謂其因俗適事無益於時也，亦非達權知變之論矣。試卽古今所記述表著者，舉其一二上下之。蓋自羲、農而降，語學術則孔、孟其人矣。當其時，反鄆、讙，墮三都，誅少正卯，以及王齊反掌，羞稱伯功，事功統是矣。至於夾谷之會，請具司馬；井田、世祿，推移於去籍之後，此非其識時達變，不可以尺度拘也乎？語事功則伊、周其人也。當其時，耕莘野，樂堯、舜，一見而言素王、九主之事，以及《周禮》太平之書，兼三王，施四事，則學術盡是矣。至於鳴條之役，東山之舉，以身當天下之大任，而後世無異議，當時無貶詞，又非其聖人之權，而得於所養者深乎？故謂孔、孟之專於學術，伊、周之專
translation_en:
…and yet fail to understand that the trend of the times moves toward the ways of Shen Buhai, Han Fei, Guan Zhong, and Yan Ying. Now, Fuxi had no statutes or ordinances; the rulers of the Xia dynasty did not go back on their word; the people of Yin made solemn oaths; and the people of Zhou entered into covenants. Today, to insist solely on tallies, dry measures, knotted cords, and contracts is certainly unacceptable; yet can one claim that governance can be achieved by completely abolishing tallies, dry measures, knotted cords, and contracts? To say that the methods of Shen Buhai, Han Fei, Guan Zhong, and Yan Ying constitute the Kingly Way is certainly unacceptable; yet to claim that their adapting to customs and suiting practical affairs was of no benefit to their times is likewise not the discourse of one who grasps moral discretion and understands changing circumstances.

Let us take a few prominent examples recorded from antiquity to the present and evaluate them from top to bottom. Since the time of Fuxi and Shennong, when speaking of scholarly learning, Confucius and Mencius are the exemplars. In their own times—whether securing the return of the lands of Yun and Huan, dismantling the fortifications of the Three Capitals, and executing Shaozheng Mao, or making Qi a true kingdom as easily as turning over one's hand and disdaining to speak of the achievements of the hegemons—practical achievements were all encompassed therein. As for requesting that military officers be readied at the meeting at Jiagu, or adapting the well-field system and hereditary emoluments after the records had been destroyed—was this not because they recognized the times and understood change, refusing to be bound by rigid measurements?

When speaking of practical achievements, Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou are the exemplars. In their own times—whether plowing in the wilds of Xin, delighting in the way of Yao and Shun, and speaking at a first audience of the affairs of the Uncrowned King and the Nine Rulers, or composing the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) as a book of grand peace, combining the virtues of the Three Kings to implement the four matters—scholarly learning was wholly exhausted therein. As for the campaign at Mingtiao and the expedition to the Eastern Mountains, whereby they personally shouldered the great responsibility of the realm without dissenting opinions in later ages or disparaging words in their own day—was this not the moral discretion of sages, derived deeply from their self-cultivation? Therefore, to claim that Confucius and Mencius were devoted exclusively to scholarly learning, and that Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou were devoted exclusively…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於事功是世儒曲學之談而非聖賢達天
之學也秦漢而下其以事功學術稱者班
班史冊吾未暇論論其著者董仲舒之潛
心大業罷黜百家韓愈之攘斥異端推尊
孟氏吾以為二氏之學術無以尚之矣蓋
其當秦灰絕學之後佛老縱橫之餘則或
治春秋而推陰陽災異之變或擯佛老而
倡仁義禮樂之統使後世知六藝之科孔
子之術明先王之道而不絕如綫者則董
===
韓之功也乃其用之不究漢唐之君有責
矣說者猶有遺議何耶毋亦以政府之書
膠西之事乎此則所遭之窮而於二氏無
損也子房運籌決勝佐成帝業仁傑潛授
豪賢卒正主器吾以為二子之事功無以
加之矣蓋其當羣雄逐鹿之餘諸武用事
之際則或噓赤帝之精於灞上取虞淵之
日於天中使天下後世知發縱指示之功
間關維護之力則狄張之翼運豈可少也
punctuated: 於事功，是世儒曲學之談，而非聖賢達天之學也。秦漢而下，其以事功、學術稱者，班班史冊，吾未暇論，論其著者。董仲舒之潛心大業，罷黜百家；韓愈之攘斥異端，推尊孟氏，吾以為二氏之學術，無以尚之矣。蓋其當秦灰絕學之後，佛老縱橫之餘，則或治《春秋》而推陰陽災異之變，或擯佛老而倡仁義禮樂之統，使後世知六藝之科、孔子之術，明先王之道而不絕如綫者，則董、韓之功也。乃其用之不究，漢唐之君有責矣。說者猶有遺議，何耶？毋亦以政府之書、膠西之事乎？此則所遭之窮，而於二氏無損也。子房運籌決勝，佐成帝業；仁傑潛授豪賢，卒正主器，吾以為二子之事功，無以加之矣。蓋其當羣雄逐鹿之餘，諸武用事之際，則或噓赤帝之精於灞上，取虞淵之日於天中，使天下後世知發縱指示之功，間關維護之力，則狄、張之翼運，豈可少也！
translation_en:
… exclusively on practical achievements is the talk of vulgar scholars of crooked learning, and not the Heaven-reaching learning of sages and worthies.

From the Qin and Han dynasties onward, those renowned for practical achievements and scholarly learning are recorded everywhere in the histories. I do not have the leisure to discuss them all, so I shall discuss the most prominent among them. Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 devoted his mind to the great enterprise and dismissed the Hundred Schools; Han Yu 韓愈 repelled heterodoxies and revered Master Meng (Mencius 孟子). I consider that the scholarly learning of these two masters cannot be surpassed. For living as they did after the ashes of the Qin had extinguished learning, or in the wake of the unbridled spread of Buddhism and Daoism, one mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) to deduce the transformations of yin and yang and of disasters and anomalies, while the other rejected Buddhism and Daoism to champion the orthodox transmission of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music. That later generations knew the disciplines of the Six Arts and the teachings of Confucius, and that the Way of the Former Kings was illuminated and kept from snapping like a mere thread—this was the achievement of Dong and Han. That their employment was not carried through to the utmost was the fault of the rulers of Han and Tang. Why, then, do commentators still have lingering criticisms of them? Is it not because of the letters to the chief minister's office [Han Yu's letters seeking office] and the affair of Jiaoxi [Dong Zhongshu's service as Chancellor there]? Yet these were due to the straitened circumstances they encountered, and they do no detriment to the two masters.

Zifang 子房 [Zhang Liang 張良] devised strategies in the command tent to secure victory from afar, assisting in the completion of the imperial enterprise; Renjie 仁傑 [Di Renjie 狄仁傑] secretly recommended heroic worthies and ultimately restored the rightful heir to the throne. I consider that the practical achievements of these two men cannot be exceeded. For living as they did amidst the contention of rival warlords for the empire, or at a time when the Wu 武 clan held sway over state affairs, one breathed life into the spirit of the Red Emperor at Bashang 灞上, while the other retrieved the sun from the Abyss of Yu [where it sets] and restored it to the center of the heavens. Causing all under Heaven and later generations to know the merit of unleashing and directing the hunt, and the power of arduous protection and preservation—how could the assistance given to the dynastic destiny by Di and Zhang be dispensed with! …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
或者乃有雌黃何耶毋亦以黃石之書屈
身之誚乎而不知此正所謂奇正之變以
建大勳蓋庶幾乎用權而不離乎經者其
於二子何病也在宋之以學術稱者敦頤
發祕於太極二程妙契乎性心橫渠著論
於正蒙朱子集成於諸儒可謂用心於性
命之學而上接乎千古不傳之祕矣然宋
之天下文勝而武衰詞多而功少至黨人
之錮與之相終始南渡之後寢以微廢諸
===
子謂何夫綿蕞之儀非馬上之習也端甫
之服非鞬弧之具也則其用之不果究者
諸賢之遘會有然而謂其學術可少耶其
以事功稱者則有慶曆煕寧諸君子韓琦
之號令西賊寒心仲淹之備邊諸羌輸戴
富弼以二字折契丹之氣歐陽脩以黨論
正朝廷之綱天下想望以爲中興復見也
然未幾而忠邪並進法制紛更則或以危
言而出將以飛語而落外何其銳治之不
punctuated:
或者乃有雌黃，何耶？毋亦以黃石之書、屈身之誚乎？而不知此正所謂奇正之變以建大勳，蓋庶幾乎用權而不離乎經者，其於二子何病也？
在宋之以學術稱者：敦頤發祕於《太極》，二程妙契乎性心，橫渠著論於《正蒙》，朱子集成於諸儒，可謂用心於性命之學，而上接乎千古不傳之祕矣。然宋之天下，文勝而武衰，詞多而功少，至黨人之錮與之相終始，南渡之後，寢以微廢，諸子謂何？夫綿蕞之儀，非馬上之習也；端甫之服，非鞬弧之具也。則其用之不果究者，諸賢之遘會有然，而謂其學術可少耶？其以事功稱者，則有慶曆、煕寧諸君子：韓琦之號令，西賊寒心；仲淹之備邊，諸羌輸戴；富弼以二字折契丹之氣；歐陽脩以《黨論》正朝廷之綱。天下想望，以爲中興復見也。然未幾而忠邪並進，法制紛更，則或以危言而出，將以飛語而落外，何其銳治之不
translation_en:
…Why then do some critics still find fault with them? Is it not because of the book received from Master Yellow Stone (Huangshi) and the reproach of submitting in humiliation to a usurper? Yet they fail to realize that this was precisely what is called alternating between the unorthodox and the orthodox to establish great merit; they came close to employing expediency without departing from constant principle—what blemish is this upon the two men?

In the Song dynasty, among those renowned for scholarship: Zhou Dunyi (周敦頤) unveiled the mysteries of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu), the two Cheng brothers (Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤) attained a subtle understanding of human nature and the mind, Zhang Zai (張載, Hengqu 橫渠) set forth his discourses in Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng), and Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) synthesized the teachings of all the Confucian scholars. They may well be said to have devoted their minds to the learning of human nature and destiny, connecting back to the secrets that had gone untransmitted for a thousand ages. Yet in the empire of the Song, civil culture prevailed while martial vigor declined, words were many while achievements were few; the proscription of partisans lasted throughout the dynasty from beginning to end, and after the crossing to the south it gradually sank into weakness and ruin. What did these masters have to say to that? Now, the court rituals practiced with ropes and straw markers are not the habits of horseback, and ceremonial robes and caps are not the gear of bow-cases and bows. That their practical application was never fully realized was due to the circumstances these worthies encountered—how could one say that their scholarship was dispensable?

Among those renowned for practical achievements, there were the gentlemen of the Qingli (1041–1048) and Xining (1068–1077) eras: Han Qi's (韓琦) commands struck terror into the hearts of the Western rebels; Fan Zhongyan's (范仲淹) border defenses won the submission and allegiance of the various Qiang tribes; Fu Bi (富弼) broke the arrogance of the Khitan with two words; and Ouyang Xiu (歐陽脩) rectified the guiding principles of the court with his Discourse on Factions (Pengdang lun). The empire looked up to them in hopeful expectation, believing that a dynastic revival was being seen once more. Yet before long, the loyal and the wicked advanced together, laws and institutions were confusedly altered, and some were sent out of court for their bold words, or relegated to the provinces because of flying slanders—why was that eager quest for governance not…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
終也豈諸賢之所託有然耶抑固天耶夫
雅鄭竝奏師曠不能適五音驥駑聯衡造
父不能致千里用不同也宋之所以寢至
微弱而不克自振者自棄干城也於諸賢
奚尤吾嘗合而論之學術則孔孟尚矣粹
乎其無議矣董子其源乎韓子其流乎濂
洛關閩其大明中天乎吾獨慨干戈倥偬
之中禮樂未遑之日乃能振絕學於微言
倡六藝於往緒卽漢武不能用舒而其改
===
正朔易服色庶幾亦略見施行雖有江都
之命吾知舒之心固無憾矣自漢迄唐幾
數百年異端之起而日熾卒無有一言當
其鋒者而獨爲廬居火書之說天下始而
疑終而信乃始羣然而攻之所謂起衰濟
溺焉者不爲溢美卽唐宗之不能用愈而
愈固可有詞於天下後世矣此其於濂洛
關閩諸子殆未可以軒輊論也要之韓董
當其難而濂洛諸賢則因而醇之焉耳伊
punctuated:
終也！豈諸賢之所託有然耶？抑固天耶？夫雅、鄭竝奏，師曠不能適五音；驥、駑聯衡，造父不能致千里，用不同也。宋之所以寢至微弱而不克自振者，自棄干城也，於諸賢奚尤！

吾嘗合而論之，學術則孔、孟尚矣，粹乎其無議矣。董子其源乎？韓子其流乎？濂、洛、關、閩其大明中天乎？吾獨慨干戈倥偬之中、禮樂未遑之日，乃能振絕學於微言，倡六藝於往緒。卽漢武不能用舒，而其改正朔、易服色，庶幾亦略見施行；雖有江都之命，吾知舒之心固無憾矣。自漢迄唐，幾數百年，異端之起而日熾，卒無有一言當其鋒者。而獨爲「廬居火書」之說，天下始而疑、終而信，乃始羣然而攻之，所謂「起衰濟溺」焉者，不爲溢美。卽唐宗之不能用愈，而愈固可有詞於天下後世矣。此其於濂、洛、關、閩諸子，殆未可以軒輊論也。要之，韓、董當其難，而濂、洛諸賢則因而醇之焉耳。伊、
translation_en:
…carried through to the end! Was this due to the circumstances in which these worthies placed their trust, or was it simply Heaven's will? When courtly odes and the airs of Zheng are played together, even Music Master Kuang (Shi Kuang 師曠) cannot harmonize the five tones; when a thoroughbred and a nag are yoked side by side, even Zaofu 造父 cannot cover a thousand li—because their capacities are not the same. The reason the Song dynasty gradually sank into weakness and could not rouse itself was that it cast away its own bulwarks; how could those worthies be blamed?

I have considered them together and discussed them as a whole. As for scholarly learning, Confucius (Kong 孔) and Mencius (Meng 孟) stand supreme—pure and beyond all criticism! Was Master Dong (Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒) its source? Was Master Han (Han Yu 韓愈) its stream? And were the masters of Lian 濂, Luo 洛, Guan 關, and Min 閩 its great illumination at the zenith of heaven? What moves me in particular is that amid the pressing turmoil of warfare, in days when there was not yet leisure for rites and music, Dong Zhongshu was able to revive lost learning from subtle words and champion the Six Arts from past traditions. Even though Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wu 漢武) could not employ Zhongshu, in his altering the beginning of the calendar year and changing the color of court vestments, Zhongshu's ideas were after all roughly put into practice; even though he received the appointment to Jiangdu 江都, I know that in his heart Zhongshu certainly had no regrets. From the Han down to the Tang, for several hundred years, heterodox teachings arose and grew more rampant by the day, and in the end there was not a single word to withstand their锋芒 [spearhead]. Yet Han Yu alone put forth the doctrine of "turning their dwellings into ordinary homes and burning their books." At first the empire doubted it, but in the end believed it, and only then began to band together to attack heterodoxy; what is called "raising up the decadent and rescuing the drowning" is no exaggerated praise. Even though the Tang emperors could not employ Yu, Yu certainly had words with which to justify himself before the world and posterity. Compared with the masters of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min, one can hardly rank them higher or lower. In short, Han Yu and Dong Zhongshu faced the difficult beginnings, whereas the worthies of Lian and Luo built upon them and refined their learning into purity. As for the achievements of Yi…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
周之事功遠矣莫可追矣子房用高帝者
也仁傑用武后者也韓范富歐則用於慶
曆熙寧者也用人者進退之權在我用於
人者進退之權在人吾獨念羣雄角逐之
時乃以其眇然之身歸漢以圖韓仇旣絕
棧以杜侵道已而仇報身爲帝師乃從赤
松子以終其爲韓之忠隱然有所託而高
祖不疑焉非良之善藏用而然乎周紀亂
唐之日仁傑以身犯不測之地至於觸柱
===
被面幽囚折辱而不辭旣乃帛書暴寃抑
何慘也而卒以反周爲唐豪傑之所扼掔
切齒而莫能振乃以孑然之軀不動聲色
談笑而正之天下晏然不見其迹其亦偉
矣二人者其間固自有權術存焉故語其
光明正大則或謝慶曆諸君子而要其用
權濟變則宋之諸賢不無少遜之矣然而
張狄得用其權慶曆諸賢之不能用其權
亦天也雖然學術事功均繫於所養故古
punctuated: 周之事功遠矣，莫可追矣。子房用高帝者也，仁傑用武后者也，韓、范、富、歐則用於慶曆、熙寧者也。用人者，進退之權在我；用於人者，進退之權在人。吾獨念羣雄角逐之時，乃以其眇然之身歸漢，以圖韓仇。旣絕棧以杜侵道，已而仇報，身爲帝師，乃從赤松子以終。其爲韓之忠，隱然有所託，而高祖不疑焉，非良之善藏用而然乎？周紀亂唐之日，仁傑以身犯不測之地，至於觸柱被面，幽囚折辱而不辭。旣乃帛書暴寃，抑何慘也！而卒以反周爲唐。豪傑之所扼掔切齒而莫能振，乃以孑然之軀，不動聲色，談笑而正之，天下晏然不見其迹，其亦偉矣！二人者，其間固自有權術存焉。故語其光明正大，則或謝慶曆諸君子；而要其用權濟變，則宋之諸賢不無少遜之矣。然而張、狄得用其權，慶曆諸賢之不能用其權，亦天也。雖然，學術、事功均繫於所養。故古
translation_en:
… and the Duke of Zhou are far off in antiquity, beyond reach. Zifang [Zhang Liang 張良] was one who made use of Emperor Gao [of Han]; Renjie [Di Renjie 狄仁傑] was one who made use of Empress Wu; whereas Han [Qi 韓琦], Fan [Zhongyan 范仲淹], Fu [Bi 富弼], and Ouyang [Xiu 歐陽修] were ones who were made use of during the Qingli (1041–1048) and Xining (1068–1077) eras. For those who make use of others, the authority to advance or withdraw rests with oneself; for those who are made use of by others, the authority to advance or withdraw rests with others.

I particularly reflect upon how, at a time when rival heroes were contending for mastery, [Zhang Liang] took his slight frame and gave his allegiance to Han in order to avenge the state of Han. After he burned the plank roads to block the route of invasion, and once his vengeance was achieved and he himself had become the Emperor's teacher, he then followed Master Redpine to live out his days. His loyalty to the state of Han was tacitly entrusted to this course, and yet Gaozu did not suspect him—was this not because Liang was skilled at concealing his utility?

In the days when the Zhou regime threw the Tang into disorder, Renjie exposed himself to unfathomable peril, even to the point of striking his head against a pillar and covering his face in blood, enduring imprisonment and humiliation without shrinking. Then he wrote on silk to expose the injustice done to him—how tragic that was! Yet in the end he turned the Zhou back into the Tang. What heroic men had wrung their wrists and gnashed their teeth over without being able to rectify, he, as a solitary figure, set right amidst calm talk and laughter without betraying a sign on his face or in his voice, leaving the empire tranquil and showing no trace of his handiwork—how magnificent indeed!

With these two men, there was certainly tactical statecraft at work in what they did. Thus, if one speaks of being open and upright, they might perhaps yield to the gentlemen of the Qingli era; yet if one sums up their use of expediency to rescue the times from crisis, the worthies of the Song cannot but fall somewhat short of them. Even so, that Zhang and Di were able to exercise their expediency, while the worthies of the Qingli era were unable to exercise theirs, was also Heaven's doing.

Nevertheless, scholarly learning and practical achievements both depend upon one's inner cultivation. Thus in antiquity…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之英雄豪傑其才智勇力非不足以建天
下之事成天下之功然養之未足則不勝
其矜能憍躁之態視天下無不可爲者如
此則其用在外而不在内其才智易見其
勇力易折往往技癢無成焉彼何甞不學
其術疎也故善養者深沉微奥斂其鋒椎
然其蟄屈頹然其如廢也斯可以有爲於
天下兵法曰始如處子敵人開戶繼如脫
兎敵不及距斯可以語養矣
===
第三問
劉堯佐
同考試官學正趙批守令本以親民而久任
繼以超遷則不惟可以措民于治而吏亦無顧慮
覬慕之私是策獨得此意取之
考試官訓導唐批久任之法至爲便民而
振作鼓舞亦不可廢如寛文法一内外尤其先務
者此策得之議行卽何稱兩漢良吏盛哉
考試官敎諭鄭批通曉吏治澤以古雅
punctuated:
之英雄豪傑，其才智勇力非不足以建天下之事、成天下之功；然養之未足，則不勝其矜能憍躁之態，視天下無不可爲者。如此，則其用在外而不在内，其才智易見，其勇力易折，往往技癢無成焉。彼何甞不學？其術疎也。故善養者，深沉微奥，斂其鋒，椎然其蟄屈，頹然其如廢也，斯可以有爲於天下。《兵法》曰：「始如處子，敵人開戶；繼如脫兎，敵不及距。」斯可以語養矣。

第三問
劉堯佐
同考試官學正趙批：守令本以親民，而久任繼以超遷，則不惟可以措民于治，而吏亦無顧慮覬慕之私。是策獨得此意，取之。
考試官訓導唐批：久任之法，至爲便民，而振作鼓舞，亦不可廢。如寛文法、一内外，尤其先務者。此策得之。議行，卽何稱兩漢良吏盛哉！
考試官敎諭鄭批：通曉吏治，澤以古雅。
translation_en:
… heroes and outstanding men of old were not lacking in the talent, wisdom, courage, and strength needed to establish great enterprises in the world and accomplish great achievements in the world. Yet if their self-cultivation was insufficient, they could not overcome their boastful, arrogant, and impetuous demeanor, viewing nothing in the world as beyond their capability. When it is like this, their application lies on the outside and not on the inside; their talent and wisdom are easily exposed, their courage and strength are easily broken, and all too often they itch to display their skills yet achieve nothing. How could it be that they never studied? Rather, their art was crude. Therefore, those who excel at self-cultivation are deep, composed, subtle, and profound. They sheathe their sharp edge—blunt as if hibernating and coiled up, listless as if discarded and useless. Only then can they accomplish great things in the world. As the Art of War (Bingfa) says: "At first, be like a maiden, so the enemy opens his door; afterward, be like abolting hare, so the enemy cannot resist in time." Of this, one may truly speak of self-cultivation!

Third Policy Question
Liu Yaozuo 劉堯佐
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Subprefectural Instructor: Prefects and magistrates are fundamentally appointed to be close to the people. If long tenure is followed by exceptional promotion, not only can the people be placed in a state of good order, but officials too will be free from selfish anxieties and ambitious cravings. This policy essay alone grasps this meaning; I select it.
Comment by Examiner Tang, Assistant Instructor: The method of long tenure is most beneficial to the people, yet rousing and encouraging officials must not be neglected either. Relaxing legalistic regulations and equalizing the weight of inner [metropolitan] and outer [provincial] posts are especially urgent priorities. This policy essay grasps it. If its proposals were put into practice, why would we need to praise only the flourishing of good officials in the Western and Eastern Han dynasties!
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Prefectural Instructor: Thoroughly conversant with administrative governance, and embellished with classical elegance.

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人君所以弘化理而奠宇內者乆任之法
也然維其法於不墜者必有道焉夫守令
親民之官也官與民情本相通而乆任之
法不立則官視其所居如逆旅無以從容
展錯而民咸奔走蹌蹌日覩新舊往來之
繁曾不見膏澤之洽閭閻也乃若任乆矣
法誠善矣顧天下無無弊之法儻使居官
者有淹滯之歎若强其所弗堪則亦何以
安其心而理民事哉是故設官所以爲民
===
也便官所以便民也通於斯道何乆任之
不可行乎敬述所聞爲明問復焉今夫人
君以一身居九重之上不能徧天下以布
其澤而爲之守若令者承其德意而廣施
之蘇軾曰君者父母也民赤子也守令乳
保也其言當矣然守令非乆任則循良之
績弗著何也觀夫豢牛羊之家使一人牧
之亦必假以歲月而後可以責其蕃息若
今日一人牧之明日又一人牧之則牛羊
punctuated:
人君所以弘化理而奠宇內者，乆任之法也；然維其法於不墜者，必有道焉。夫守令，親民之官也。官與民情本相通，而乆任之法不立，則官視其所居如逆旅，無以從容展錯；而民咸奔走蹌蹌，日覩新舊往來之繁，曾不見膏澤之洽閭閻也。乃若任乆矣，法誠善矣，顧天下無無弊之法，儻使居官者有淹滯之歎，若强其所弗堪，則亦何以安其心而理民事哉？是故設官所以爲民也，便官所以便民也。通於斯道，何乆任之不可行乎？敬述所聞，爲明問復焉。
今夫人君以一身居九重之上，不能徧天下以布其澤，而爲之守若令者，承其德意而廣施之。蘇軾曰：「君者，父母也；民，赤子也；守令，乳保也。」其言當矣。然守令非乆任，則循良之績弗著，何也？觀夫豢牛羊之家，使一人牧之，亦必假以歲月，而後可以責其蕃息；若今日一人牧之，明日又一人牧之，則牛羊
translation_en:
That by which the ruler expands transformative governance and stabilizes the realm within the four seas is the system of long tenure in office; yet to uphold this system so that it does not fall into ruin, there must be a proper way. Now, prefects and magistrates are officials who are close to the people. The feelings of officials and the people are inherently connected, yet if the system of long tenure is not established, officials will regard their posts as mere wayside inns, having no means to unhurriedly carry out their measures; meanwhile, the people will all be bustling and hurrying about, daily witnessing the frequent comings and goings of new and outgoing officials, without ever seeing benevolent grace saturate their鄉villages and alleys. Now suppose tenure is made long—the system is truly good. Yet in the world there is no system without abuses; if those holding office are made to sigh over being held back in stagnation, as though forced to endure what they cannot bear, then how could one set their minds at ease so that they attend to the affairs of the people? Therefore, establishing offices is for the sake of the people, and accommodating officials is the means to benefit the people. Once one comprehends this principle, why could long tenure not be put into practice? I respectfully set forth what I have heard in reply to the brilliant inquiry.

Now, the ruler, dwelling as a single person high above in the九重 ninefold palace, cannot personally reach the entire realm to spread his beneficence; rather, those who serve him as prefects and magistrates receive his virtuous intentions and disseminate them broadly. Su Shi 蘇軾 said: "The ruler is the parents; the people are the newborn infants; the prefects and magistrates are the wet nurses and guardians." His words are apt indeed! Yet if prefects and magistrates do not serve for long tenures, the achievements of upright and benevolent administration do not become manifest—why is this? Observe a household that raises cattle and sheep: if it employs one person to herd them, it must also grant him months and years before it can demand that the flock multiply and flourish. If one person herds them today, and tomorrow another person herds them, then the cattle and sheep…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
日瘠雖欲蕃息不可得矣矧守令當牧民
之責者乎故安心治民使休澤汪濊淪浹
乎無外殆非勉强朞月之間而苟以求名
者之所能也嘗考載籍而得其槩矣漢去
古未遠當文景時爲吏者長子孫遂致海
內富庶之效宣帝每拜刺史守相輒親見
問及其退也又考察所行以質其言嘗曰
太守吏民之本也數變易則民不安民知
其將久不可欺乃服從其敎化用是良吏
===
爲盛赫然稱中興焉逮及明章下詔猶有
此意漢末轉動無常見于左雄之奏斯漢
業衰矣
明興
祖宗稽古定
制百官咸以九年通考課其功過以相乘除而
黜陟焉故有附過還職之法斯卽古三載
考績之意也然此時久任之法蓋與超遷
之法兼行之矣以郡縣言之况鍾九年守
punctuated:
日瘠，雖欲蕃息，不可得矣。矧守令當牧民之責者乎？故安心治民，使休澤汪濊，淪浹乎無外，殆非勉强朞月之間，而苟以求名者之所能也。嘗考載籍而得其槩矣。漢去古未遠，當文、景時，爲吏者長子孫，遂致海內富庶之效。宣帝每拜刺史、守、相，輒親見問，及其退也，又考察所行以質其言，嘗曰：「太守，吏民之本也。數變易則民不安；民知其將久，不可欺，乃服從其敎化。」用是良吏爲盛，赫然稱中興焉。逮及明、章下詔，猶有此意。漢末轉動無常，見于左雄之奏，斯漢業衰矣。
明興，祖宗稽古定制，百官咸以九年通考，課其功過以相乘除，而黜陟焉，故有附過還職之法，斯卽古三載考績之意也。然此時久任之法，蓋與超遷之法兼行之矣。以郡縣言之，况鍾九年守
translation_en:
…will grow thinner by the day; even if one wished them to multiply and thrive, it could not be achieved. How much more so is this true of prefects and magistrates, who bear the responsibility of shepherding the people! Therefore, governing the people with a settled mind so that beneficent grace flows abundantly and permeates everywhere without exception is scarcely within the capability of those who merely force themselves for a year or a month just to seek a reputation. I have examined the historical records and grasped the general outline of this. The Han dynasty was not far removed from antiquity. During the reigns of Emperors Wen and Jing, those who served as officials remained in office long enough to raise their sons and grandsons, thereby bringing about prosperity and abundance throughout the realm. Whenever Emperor Xuan appointed a Regional Inspector, Grand Administrator, or Chancellor, he would personally grant them an audience and question them; after they withdrew, he would investigate their actions to verify their words. He once said: "The Grand Administrator is the foundation of the subalterns and the people. If he is frequently replaced, the people will be unsettled; when the people know that he will remain for a long time and cannot be deceived, they will submit to his moral instruction and transformation." Because of this, upright officials flourished, and his reign was illustriously acclaimed as a dynastic restoration. Down to the reigns of Emperors Ming and Zhang, the edicts they issued still retained this intent. By the end of the Han, transfers and replacements became erratic, as seen in the memorials of Zuo Xiong 左雄, and thus the Han enterprise declined.

With the rise of the Ming, our Imperial Ancestors examined antiquity and established institutions whereby all officials underwent a comprehensive evaluation after nine years. Their merits and faults were assessed and balanced against one another in order to demote or promote them; hence there was the statute of recording a fault while returning the official to his post, which was precisely the ancient principle of evaluating achievements every three years. Yet at that time, the practice of long tenure was in fact carried out in conjunction with the practice of exceptional promotion. Speaking in terms of prefectures and counties, Kuang Zhong 况鍾 served for nine years as Prefect of…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
蘇州此郡之久任也而趙珝擢爲諭德非
郡守中之超遷乎盧秉安十九年令東莞
此縣之久任也而王佐擢爲侍講非縣令
中之超遷乎諸如此類殆不可一一數矣
先正羅欽順曰超遷與久任相表裏超于
前自可責其後之久超于後固無負其前
之淹誠確論也惟此法不盡行人情往往
厭淹滯而喜速化抑或有所希冀於前者
之一二而益無固志蓋漸靡有然矣
===
皇上
天縱神明
冲齡御極首從輔臣之議
勅銓曹行久任之法大都郡縣遷轉以六年爲
期甚
盛典也行之旣定郡守縣令始人人灑然動志
務爲經常悠遠之圖而不敢苟且因循以
支吾于旦夕四海元元已受
庇宏矣顧有謂便于民不便于官者何歟愚生
punctuated: 蘇州，此郡之久任也；而趙珝擢爲諭德，非郡守中之超遷乎？盧秉安十九年令東莞，此縣之久任也；而王佐擢爲侍講，非縣令中之超遷乎？諸如此類，殆不可一一數矣。先正羅欽順曰：「超遷與久任相表裏，超于前自可責其後之久，超于後固無負其前之淹。」誠確論也。惟此法不盡行，人情往往厭淹滯而喜速化，抑或有所希冀於前者之一二，而益無固志，蓋漸靡有然矣。皇上天縱神明，冲齡御極，首從輔臣之議，勅銓曹行久任之法，大都郡縣遷轉以六年爲期，甚盛典也。行之旣定，郡守、縣令始人人灑然動志，務爲經常悠遠之圖，而不敢苟且因循以支吾于旦夕，四海元元已受庇宏矣。顧有謂便于民不便于官者，何歟？愚生
translation_en:
…Suzhou [for nine years]; this was an example of long tenure in a prefecture. Yet Zhao Xu 趙珝 was promoted to Admonisher (yude 諭德)—was this not an extraordinary promotion from among Prefectural Governors? Lu Bing'an 盧秉安 served nineteen years as District Magistrate of Dongguan 東莞; this was an example of long tenure in a district. Yet Wang Zuo 王佐 was promoted to Expositor-in-waiting (shijiang 侍講)—was this not an extraordinary promotion from among District Magistrates? Instances of this sort can scarcely be counted one by one. The former worthy Luo Qinshun 羅欽順 said: "Extraordinary promotion and long tenure are two sides of the same coin: if someone is given an extraordinary promotion beforehand, one can naturally hold him responsible for serving a long tenure afterward; if someone is given an extraordinary promotion afterward, it certainly does not fail to reward his prolonged stay beforehand." This is truly an incisive argument. Only when this method is not fully practiced does human nature frequently grow weary of prolonged stagnation and delight in rapid advancement, or perhaps harbor hopes for one or two of those early extraordinary promotions and thus have even less firm resolve; indeed, this has come about through gradual decline.

His Majesty, heaven-endowed with divine intelligence, ascended the throne at a young age and first followed the counsel of his Grand Secretaries, commanding the Ministry of Personnel to implement the law of long tenure, setting the term of transfer for prefectures and districts generally at six years—a most magnificent institution! Once its implementation was settled, Prefectural Governors and District Magistrates began, each and every one, to feel refreshed and stirred in their ambitions, striving to make enduring and far-reaching plans and not daring to be lax or bound by routine merely to muddle through from day to day; the common people within the four seas have already received vast protection from this. Yet there are some who say that it is convenient for the people but inconvenient for the officials—why is that? I, a foolish student,…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以為官民一體也官稱不便即非可久之
道蓋厭斁之心一生則注措舛鑿澤弗下
究四境羣黎必有皇皇蹙額室家靡寧者
矣是官之不便乃所以為民之不便不為
之一處焉不可也且以愚生所目覩其視
祖宗時猶若有差殊焉昔百官皆久任茲毋乃
獨久于郡縣耶昔悃愊無華并與超遷茲
毋乃猶有守即墨而沉淪者耶說者謂文
法之拘勝則顧慮多內外之勢懸則覬慕
===
起今豈盡無之耶
朝廷省議論假便宜若無文法掣肘之患而
利害交關之際或多巧避是顧慮之態未
盡袪也
朝廷嘉賢能
錫宴賞若無內外隔絕之殊而選除升取之間
或多干進是覬慕之態未盡變也盍不思
所以振作而鼓舞之乎夫欲為振作鼓舞
之計其道有二焉一曰嚴虛實之辨夫玉
punctuated: 以為官民一體也，官稱不便，即非可久之道。蓋厭斁之心一生，則注措舛鑿，澤弗下究，四境羣黎必有皇皇蹙額，室家靡寧者矣。是官之不便，乃所以為民之不便，不為之一處焉不可也。且以愚生所目覩，其視祖宗時猶若有差殊焉。昔百官皆久任，茲毋乃獨久于郡縣耶？昔悃愊無華，并與超遷，茲毋乃猶有守即墨而沉淪者耶？說者謂文法之拘勝則顧慮多，內外之勢懸則覬慕起，今豈盡無之耶？朝廷省議論，假便宜，若無文法掣肘之患，而利害交關之際，或多巧避，是顧慮之態未盡袪也；朝廷嘉賢能，錫宴賞，若無內外隔絕之殊，而選除升取之間，或多干進，是覬慕之態未盡變也。盍不思所以振作而鼓舞之乎？夫欲為振作鼓舞之計，其道有二焉：一曰嚴虛實之辨。夫玉
translation_en:
… believes that officials and the common people form a single body. If a measure is said to be inconvenient for officials, then it is not a policy that can endure. For once a feeling of weariness and dissatisfaction arises in them, their administrative measures become perversely at odds, and imperial grace fails to reach down to the bottom; then the common people within the four borders will inevitably be anxious with furrowed brows, their households knowing no peace. Thus, what is inconvenient for officials is precisely what becomes inconvenient for the people, and we cannot fail to find a way to address it.

Moreover, judging by what this humble student has witnessed with his own eyes, compared with the era of our Imperial Ancestors there still seems to be some discrepancy. In the past, all officials held long tenures; now, is it not the case that long tenure is applied solely to prefectures and counties? In the past, those who were sincere and unpretentious were all granted extraordinary promotions; now, are there not still those who, like the defender of Jimo, remain sunk in obscurity? Commentators say that when the constraints of legalistic rules prevail, anxieties and hesitations multiply; and when there is a wide disparity in status between the inner court and the outer provinces, covetous ambitions arise. Can it be that such things are entirely absent today?

The Court reduces empty deliberation and grants discretionary authority, as if there were no longer the problem of being hampered by legalistic rules; yet at junctures where personal advantage and disadvantage intersect, many still artfully evade responsibility—which shows that the habit of anxious hesitation has not been completely dispelled. The Court commends the worthy and capable and bestows banquets and rewards upon them, as if there were no longer any alienating distinction between inner and outer posts; yet in the process of selection, appointment, promotion, and recall to the capital, many still maneuver for advancement—which shows that the habit of covetous ambition has not been completely transformed. Why not, then, consider how to rouse and encourage them?

If we wish to devise a plan to rouse and encourage them, there are two ways to do so. The first is to strictly distinguish between emptiness and substance. A jade…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
巵華而不酤輒售波斯之價畫龍飾而不
雨每致葉公之好今有司之巧獵名譽者
何以異此乃其純心爲民者人恒弗之知
也司激揚者誠毋以鷹鸇先鸞鳳鉤鉅察
姦者一時固駭人視聽也而歲月旣久則
術窮矣必置之弗錄奉職循理者下車固
無赫赫名也而月計有餘則職盡矣必揚
之弗棄如是而吏不樂于久任未之有也
二曰酌難易之勢夫合抱之木非利器不
===
能伐九折之坂非造父不能御今有司之
才堪繁劇者何以異此若其居簡僻之地
者則不必爾也司銓衡者誠參以地方論
殿最如民淳地僻責以六年可也而衝津
省會之區卽旌異稍先焉不爲過矣中原
樂土循資叙錄可也而邊海窮荒之所卽
拔擢獨優焉不爲濫矣如是而吏不安于
久任未之前聞也嗚呼守令者牧也民則
其所牧者也牧久而民得所矣上者風也
punctuated:
巵華而不酤，輒售波斯之價；畫龍飾而不雨，每致葉公之好。今有司之巧獵名譽者，何以異此？乃其純心爲民者，人恒弗之知也。司激揚者誠毋以鷹鸇先鸞鳳。鉤鉅察姦者，一時固駭人視聽也，而歲月旣久則術窮矣，必置之弗錄；奉職循理者，下車固無赫赫名也，而月計有餘則職盡矣，必揚之弗棄。如是，而吏不樂于久任，未之有也。
二曰酌難易之勢。夫合抱之木，非利器不能伐；九折之坂，非造父不能御。今有司之才堪繁劇者，何以異此？若其居簡僻之地者，則不必爾也。司銓衡者誠參以地方論殿最。如民淳地僻，責以六年可也；而衝津省會之區，卽旌異稍先焉，不爲過矣。中原樂土，循資叙錄可也；而邊海窮荒之所，卽拔擢獨優焉，不爲濫矣。如是，而吏不安于久任，未之前聞也。
嗚呼！守令者，牧也；民則其所牧者也。牧久而民得所矣。上者，風也；
translation_en:
…cup is華麗 ornate yet holds no wine, it readily sells for the price of a Persian treasure; a painted dragon is decorative yet brings no rain, yet it always wins the fondness of Lord She (Ye Gong 葉公). How are today's local officials who cleverly hunt for reputation any different from this? Meanwhile, those whose hearts are purely devoted to the people consistently go unrecognized by others. Those in charge of censuring the corrupt and promoting the worthy must truly avoid placing hawks and falcons ahead of simurghs and phoenixes. Those who use cunning traps to ferret out villainy certainly startle people's eyes and ears for a moment, yet once months and years have passed, their tricks are exhausted; they must be set aside and not recorded for merit. Those who discharge their duties in accordance with principle certainly have no dazzling fame when they first alight from their carriages to take office, yet when the monthly reckoning shows a surplus of achievement, their duties have been fulfilled; they must be praised and not abandoned. If this is done, there will never be a case of officials not rejoicing in long tenures of office.

The second is to weigh the circumstances of difficulty and ease. Now, a tree spanning an armful cannot be felled without a sharp tool; a nine-bend mountain slope cannot be driven without a Zaofu 造父. How are today's local officials whose talents are equal to complex and demanding posts any different from this? As for those who occupy simple and out-of-the-way places, they do not need to be so. Those in charge of personnel evaluation and selection must truly take the locality into account when assessing superior and inferior performance. For instance, where the people are simple and the land is remote, holding an official responsible for a six-year tenure is acceptable; whereas in strategic thoroughfares and provincial capitals, even if special commendation comes somewhat earlier, it would not be excessive. In the pleasant lands of the Central Plain, advancing officials according to seniority is acceptable; whereas in coastal frontiers and desolate wastelands, even if promotion is uniquely generous, it would not be lavish. If this is done, it has never before been heard that officials would not be content with long tenures of office.

Alas! Prefectural and county magistrates are shepherds, and the people are those whom they shepherd. When the shepherding continues for a long time, the people find their proper place. Superiors are the wind; …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
守令則從風者也風行而守令率職矣厲
世磨鈍之權是在
廟堂有以風之耳雖然愚猶有獻焉方
今堯舜在上輔以皐夔整齊吏治之方計無遺
畫惟持而行之信如四時變而通之不膠
一定創之一時不至紛更于他日推之四
海毋爲遷就于一人如是則可以久任可
以超遷可以便民可以便吏福星載路常
泯鴻鴈于無聲棠陰滿天永享昇平之有
===
日矣愚生一得之慮如此惟進敎之幸甚
第四問
蒙而鎡
同考試官敎諭侯 批 敷陳天人感應之理甚
悉進規處尤懇切足見忠愛
考試官訓導唐 批 人君脩德歷億兆年當
如一日而天心仁愛則尤殷殷加之意堯稱警予
是也是作深得
皇上謙抑之衷而尤欲效其無已之助忠愛之悃具吐毫端矣
punctuated:
守令則從風者也。風行而守令率職矣。厲世磨鈍之權，是在廟堂有以風之耳。雖然，愚猶有獻焉：方今堯、舜在上，輔以皐、夔，整齊吏治之方，計無遺畫。惟持而行之，信如四時；變而通之，不膠一定。創之一時，不至紛更于他日；推之四海，毋爲遷就于一人。如是，則可以久任，可以超遷，可以便民，可以便吏。福星載路，常泯鴻鴈于無聲；棠陰滿天，永享昇平之有日矣。愚生一得之慮如此，惟進敎之，幸甚。

第四問
蒙而鎡
同考試官敎諭侯批：敷陳天人感應之理甚悉，進規處尤懇切，足見忠愛。
考試官訓導唐批：人君脩德，歷億兆年當如一日，而天心仁愛，則尤殷殷加之意，堯稱「警予」是也。是作深得皇上謙抑之衷，而尤欲效其無已之助，忠愛之悃，具吐毫端矣。
translation_en:
… and prefects and magistrates are those who follow the wind. When the wind blows, prefects and magistrates fulfill their duties. The power to sharpen the world andhone the dull rests simply with the imperial court inspiring them like the wind. Even so, this ignorant one still has something to offer: At present, a Yao and Shun is on high, assisted by a Gao Yao and Kui, and in the methods for ordering official administration, the plans leave nothing out. Only hold fast to them and carry them out, as trustworthy as the four seasons; adapt them and make them work, without clinging rigidly to fixed rules. What is established at one time should not come to be confusedly altered on another day; what is extended throughout the four seas should not be compromised for the sake of a single person. If this is done, then officials can be kept long in office, or they can be given extraordinary promotions; it can benefit the people, and it can benefit the officials. Lucky stars will fill the roads, forever silencing the cries of the wild geese [displaced people]; the shade of the sweet-pear tree [benevolent governance] will cover the sky, and the days of eternal peace and prosperity will arrive. Such is the humble consideration of this ignorant student; I only beg to be advanced and instructed, which would be most fortunate.

Fourth Question
Meng Erzi
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Hou comments: He sets forth the principles of the mutual resonance between Heaven and man in great detail, and where he offers remonstrance and counsel he is especially earnest, which is enough to show his loyalty and devotion.
Examiner, Assistant Instructor (xundao) Tang comments: A ruler's cultivation of virtue should remain as if a single day across billions of years, and because the mind of Heaven is benevolent and loving, he should pay even more earnest heed to it—this is what Yao meant when he spoke of "warning me." This essay deeply grasps His Majesty's humble and self-restrained heart, and seeks especially to offer tireless assistance; sincere loyalty and devotion pour forth from the tip of his brush.

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭鄭杙發揮脩德格天之旨隱
有忠讜
吾觀周禮分野之說星土州域質驗拘合
以及左氏天官五行傳逆臆傅會五勝五
德之論其亦微矣夫取應必則無徵者疎
測驗奇則示象者淺孔子作春秋二百四
十二年之間日食地震隕石退鷁之類書
之不置而未嘗牽合事應豈非以志變動
觀妖祥備憲戒救政序事而不以迹拘也
===
乎夫天人之際精祲有以相動善惡有以
相推事作乎下者象動乎上故賤臣叩心
飛霜擊於燕地庶女呼天振風襲于齊臺
衞先生爲秦畫長平之策太白蝕昴荆軻
慕燕丹之義白虹貫日精之所變如影響
之應形聲以爲寥邈曠遠而無所徵証者
非也乃今之談者不云堯湯之水旱則云
太戊之穀桑不云高宗之雊雉則云宣王
之旱魃如此則馮相保章之所觀候臺銅
punctuated:
考試官敎諭鄭杙：發揮脩德格天之旨，隱有忠讜。

吾觀《周禮》分野之說，星土州域，質驗拘合；以及左氏、天官、《五行傳》逆臆傅會、五勝五德之論，其亦微矣。夫取應必，則無徵者疎；測驗奇，則示象者淺。孔子作《春秋》，二百四十二年之間，日食、地震、隕石、退鷁之類，書之不置，而未嘗牽合事應，豈非以志變動、觀妖祥、備憲戒、救政序事，而不以迹拘也乎？夫天人之際，精祲有以相動，善惡有以相推，事作乎下者，象動乎上。故賤臣叩心，飛霜擊於燕地；庶女呼天，振風襲于齊臺；衞先生爲秦畫長平之策，太白蝕昴；荆軻慕燕丹之義，白虹貫日。精之所變，如影響之應形聲，以爲寥邈曠遠而無所徵証者，非也。乃今之談者，不云堯、湯之水旱，則云太戊之穀桑；不云高宗之雊雉，則云宣王之旱魃。如此，則馮相、保章之所觀，候臺、銅…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Zheng [comment] [? 杙 for 批]: It expounds the meaning of cultivating virtue to move Heaven, and implicitly contains loyal and forthright counsel.

When I examine the theory of astral-terrestrial correspondences (fenye) in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), with its rigid matching and verification of starry regions and terrestrial provinces, as well as the retrospective conjectures and forced correlations in the Zuo Commentary (Zuoshi), the treatise on Celestial Offices (Tianguan), and the Treatise on the Five Phases (Wuxing zhuan), along with the theories of the mutual conquest and succession of the Five Virtues—how subtle yet tenuous they are! Indeed, if one insists on an inevitable correspondence for every portent, then cases without verification will seem lax; if one seeks out strange prognostic verifications, then the meaning of the manifested signs becomes shallow. When Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), over the span of two hundred and forty-two years, he tirelessly recorded such events as solar eclipses, earthquakes, falling stones, and ospreys flying backward, yet he never forcibly matched them to specific human affairs as their responses. Was this not in order to record anomalies, observe ominous and auspicious signs, prepare admonitions and warnings, and rectify governance and order affairs, without being bound by superficial traces?

In the interaction between Heaven and humankind, quintessential sincerity and ominous vapors move one another, and good and evil propel one another; when affairs arise below, celestial signs stir above. Thus, when a lowly subject beat his breast in grief, flying frost struck the land of Yan; when a commoner woman cried out to Heaven, a fierce wind assaulted the terrace of Qi; when Master Wei planned the strategy of Changping for Qin, Venus eclipsed the Pleiades (Mao); and when Jing Ke admired the righteousness of Prince Dan of Yan, a white rainbow pierced the sun. The transformations wrought by concentrated spirit respond like a shadow to a form or an echo to a sound; to consider Heaven remote, vast, and devoid of verifiable proofs is wrong. Yet those who discuss such matters today, if they do not speak of the floods and droughts of Yao and Tang, then they speak of the paper mulberry and grain growing together under Tai Wu; if they do not speak of the crowing pheasant under Gaozong, then they speak of the drought demon under King Xuan. If this were the case, then what the Astrologers (Fengxiang) and Imperial Astronomers (Baozhang) observe, and what the observatory terrace and the bronze…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
儀之所司皆漫緩不經天人之分始暌而
恐懼脩省皆無所事矣夫徵人事則其迹
拘歸氣數則其脩怠災沴之來雖盛世或
不能無要其所以備具消弭之者固自有
道也吾考之天官星文彗孛飛流皆變星
也說者謂孛而不已則繼之以彗是彗甚
於孛也乃晏子曰君不脩政孛星將出彗
何懼焉則孛又甚於彗矣然而以西漢言
之武帝建元元狩中有孛于西北孛于東
===
方者其時外攘四夷封狼居胥平氐羌昆
明南越赤鴈白麟之瑞史不絕書宣帝地
節中有孛于西方孛于參者其時鳳凰嘉
穀白虎威鳳之祥更僕未數二君者何也
吾意其時興學郊祀正朔定歷與夫信賞
必罰綜核名實則武宣之治先之矣以東
漢言之明帝永平中有孛于天船孛于太
微者史稱其時澤臻四表遠人慕化五穀
登蠶麥善焦僥儋耳款塞章帝之建初中
punctuated: 儀之所司，皆漫緩不經，天人之分始暌，而恐懼脩省皆無所事矣。夫徵人事則其迹拘，歸氣數則其脩怠。災沴之來，雖盛世或不能無，要其所以備具消弭之者，固自有道也。吾考之天官星文，彗、孛、飛、流，皆變星也。說者謂孛而不已，則繼之以彗，是彗甚於孛也。乃晏子曰：「君不脩政，孛星將出，彗何懼焉？」則孛又甚於彗矣。然而以西漢言之，武帝建元、元狩中，有孛于西北、孛于東方者，其時外攘四夷，封狼居胥，平氐、羌、昆明、南越，赤鴈、白麟之瑞，史不絕書；宣帝地節中，有孛于西方、孛于參者，其時鳳凰、嘉穀、白虎、威鳳之祥，更僕未數。二君者何也？吾意其時興學、郊祀、正朔、定歷，與夫信賞必罰、綜核名實，則武、宣之治先之矣。以東漢言之，明帝永平中，有孛于天船、孛于太微者，史稱其時澤臻四表，遠人慕化，五穀登，蠶麥善，焦僥、儋耳款塞；章帝之建初中，
translation_en:
… the bronze armillary spheres manage would all be dismissed as vague, irrelevant, and unfounded; the division between Heaven and humanity would begin to widen, and standing in awe to cultivate and examine oneself would no longer be practiced at all. Now, if one seeks specific verification in human affairs, the connections become overly rigid; if one attributes everything to cyclical fate, self-cultivation grows lax. When calamities and noxious anomalies arrive, even a flourishing age cannot be entirely free of them; the crux lies in the fact that there is inherently a proper way to prepare for and dispel them.

When I examine the astronomical treatises and star patterns, sweeping comets (hui), bushy comets (bo), meteors (fei), and shooting stars (liu) are all anomalous stars. Commentators say that when a bushy comet does not cease, it is followed by a sweeping comet, which implies that a sweeping comet is worse than a bushy comet. Yet Master Yan (Yanzi) said: "If the ruler does not cultivate his governance, a bushy comet is about to appear—what is there to fear from a sweeping comet?" By this account, a bushy comet is even worse than a sweeping comet!

However, if we speak in terms of the Western Han: during the Jianyuan (140–135 BCE) and Yuanshou (122–117 BCE) eras of Emperor Wu, there were bushy comets appearing in the northwest and in the east. At that time, externally he repelled the four barbarian peoples, performed the feng sacrifice at Mount Langjuxu, and pacified the Di, Qiang, Kunming, and Nanyue, while auspicious omens of red wild geese and white unicorns were recorded without interruption in the histories. During the Dijie era (69–66 BCE) of Emperor Xuan, there were bushy comets appearing in the west and in the lunar lodge Shen. At that time, auspicious signs of phoenixes, wondrous grain, white tigers, and majestic phoenixes were too numerous to count even if one changed attendants to continue the tally. Why was this so for these two rulers? I suppose that because at the time they promoted schools, instituted the suburban sacrifices, rectified the calendar, and fixed the astronomical system, and furthermore maintained trustworthy rewards and certain punishments while comprehensively verifying that realities matched names, the good governance of Emperors Wu and Xuan took precedence over the anomalies.

If we speak in terms of the Eastern Han: during the Yongping era (58–75 CE) of Emperor Ming, there were bushy comets appearing in the Celestial Boat (Tianshuan) and in the Supreme Palace (Taiwei) enclosure. The histories state that at that time imperial beneficence reached to the four extremities, distant peoples yearned for his transforming influence, the five grains yielded abundant harvests, silkworms and wheat thrived, and the Jiaoyao and Dan'er peoples knocked at the frontier passes in submission. During the Jianchu era (76–84 CE) of Emperor Zhang, …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有孛于天市孛于紫宮者史稱其時蕃輔
克諧羣后德讓而鳳凰黃龍神爵甘露之
瑞合於圖書者數十百所此何也吾意其
法令分明幽枉必達內外無倖曲之私在
朝無矜嚴之色與夫深元元之愛著胎養
之令則二君之治有以桭之矣太史公曰
星變結和太上脩德其次脩政其次脩救
其次脩禳至如占雲物候息耗華南嵩高
三河之郊與夫勃碣海岱江淮之間氣候
===
青紫亦近於馮相保章之說要以德政為
上救禳為末則庶幾者我
皇上敬
天之心朝夕乾惕頃
書十二事
座右以備
觀省如所云謹
天戒任賢能親賢臣遠嬖佞明賞罰慎出入慎
起居節飲食收放心存敬畏納忠言撙節
punctuated: 有孛于天市、孛于紫宮者，史稱其時蕃輔克諧，羣后德讓，而鳳凰、黃龍、神爵、甘露之瑞合於圖書者數十百所，此何也？吾意其法令分明，幽枉必達，內外無倖曲之私，在朝無矜嚴之色，與夫深元元之愛，著胎養之令，則二君之治有以桭之矣。太史公曰：「星變結和，太上脩德，其次脩政，其次脩救，其次脩禳。」至如占雲物，候息耗，華南、嵩高、三河之郊，與夫勃碣、海岱、江淮之間，氣候青紫，亦近於馮相、保章之說；要以德政為上，救禳為末，則庶幾者。我皇上敬天之心，朝夕乾惕，頃書十二事座右，以備觀省：如所云謹天戒、任賢能、親賢臣、遠嬖佞、明賞罰、慎出入、慎起居、節飲食、收放心、存敬畏、納忠言、撙節
translation_en:
…there were comets appearing in the Celestial Market (Tianshi) and the Purple Palace (Zigong) enclosures. Yet the histories record that at that time the feudatory princes and chief ministers were in harmony, the various lords yielded to one another in virtue, and auspicious signs—such as phoenixes, yellow dragons, divine birds, and sweet dew—matching the prophetic charts and writings occurred in dozens or hundreds of places. Why was this? In my view, their laws and ordinances were clear and distinct, hidden grievances were sure to reach the throne, inside and outside the court there was no partiality or crooked favoritism, at court there were no haughty or severe countenances, and furthermore they deepened their love for the common people and promulgated ordinances for the nourishment of the unborn and infants; thus the governance of these two sovereigns had the means to感動 [? 桭, move/establish] this.

The Grand Historian (Taishigong) said: "When celestial anomalies arise and harmony is knotted [?], the highest course is to cultivate virtue, the next is to cultivate governance, the next is to cultivate relief measures, and the next is to cultivate exorcistic prayers." As for divining by cloud vapors and observing waxing and waning across the outskirts of south of Mount Hua, Mount Songgao, and the Three Rivers (Sanhe), as well as the regions between Bohai and Jieshi, the Sea and Mount Dai, and the Yangtze and Huai rivers, noting the blue and purple atmospheric signs—this too approaches the doctrines of the Astrologer-Observers (Fengxiang) and Royal Astrologers (Baozhang). In sum, if one takes virtuous governance as primary and relief and exorcism as secondary, then one comes close to the mark.

Our August Emperor, with a heart that reveres Heaven, is diligent and vigilant from morning to night. Recently He wrote twelve precepts beside His throne for His own contemplation and self-examination: namely, what are called heeding the warnings of Heaven, employing the worthy and capable, drawing close to worthy ministers, keeping away favorites and flatterers, making rewards and punishments clear, being cautious in going out and coming in, being cautious in daily routine, moderating food and drink, recovering the strayed heart, preserving reverence and awe, accepting loyal counsel, and restraining and moderating…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
用無非恐懼脩省以仰體
天心可謂至矣乃者以星變益
省躬思過朝夕不遑而又爲之振揚剔勵
簡在廷之臣而敝其吏治以回天變其於
天心仁愛扶持全安之意誠有以仰對而無遺
矣然臣子愛
君無巳之忠則猶有願效者大抵妖不勝德變
不虛生西漢之武宣尚矣然而雄才大略
長駕遠馭傾無量之費以快心狼望之北
===
而德敎不純刑名繩下趙蓋韓楊之死說
者猶謂有關漢家元氣則二君所以致之
者有自來矣東漢之明章是矣而人冤不
能理吏黠不能禁出入無節喜怒過差與
夫以刻爲明以苛爲察以輕爲德以重爲
威或者於二君有遺憾焉
今天下乂安四海承德九夷八蠻通道六服
羣辟奔
命恐後可謂太平之盛際
punctuated: 用，無非恐懼脩省，以仰體天心，可謂至矣。乃者以星變，益省躬思過，朝夕不遑，而又爲之振揚剔勵，簡在廷之臣而敝其吏治，以回天變。其於天心仁愛扶持全安之意，誠有以仰對而無遺矣。然臣子愛君無巳之忠，則猶有願效者。大抵妖不勝德，變不虛生。西漢之武、宣尚矣，然而雄才大略，長駕遠馭，傾無量之費，以快心狼望之北；而德敎不純，刑名繩下，趙、蓋、韓、楊之死，說者猶謂有關漢家元氣，則二君所以致之者有自來矣。東漢之明、章是矣，而人冤不能理，吏黠不能禁，出入無節，喜怒過差，與夫以刻爲明、以苛爲察、以輕爲德、以重爲威，或者於二君有遺憾焉。今天下乂安，四海承德，九夷八蠻通道，六服羣辟奔命恐後，可謂太平之盛際、
translation_en:
… [and economize on] expenditures—all of this is nothing other than cultivating yourself and examining your conduct in fear and trembling so as to look up and embody the mind of Heaven, which may truly be called the utmost. Recently, because of theastral anomaly, His Majesty has all the more examined himself and reflected on his faults without a moment's leisure from morning to night; moreover, on account of it he has roused and scrubbed clean the administration, selecting the ministers at court and admonishing [?] their official governance in order to turn back the heavenly anomaly. With respect to the benevolent love of Heaven's mind and its intent to support, sustain, and preserve us in complete safety, he truly has the means to look up and respond without leaving anything undone. Yet out of a subject's unending loyalty and love for his Sovereign, there is still more that I wish to offer.

In general, portents do not overcome virtue, and anomalies do not arise in vain. In the Western Han, Emperors Wu (漢武帝) and Xuan (漢宣帝) were admirable indeed. Yet for all his heroic talent and grand strategy, driving far and reining in distant lands, Emperor Wu poured out immeasurable expenditures to gratify his heart north of Langwang (狼望); while Emperor Xuan's moral instruction was impure, binding his subordinates with legalist accountability (xingming 刑名), so that regarding the deaths of Zhao Guanghan (趙廣漢), Ge Kuanrao (蓋寬饒), Han Yanshou (韓延壽), and Yang Yun (楊惲), commentators still say they affected the vital energy (yuanqi 元氣) of the House of Han. Thus, what these two rulers brought about had its origins. In the Eastern Han, Emperors Ming (漢明帝) and Zhang (漢章帝) were praiseworthy indeed. Yet people's grievances could not be redressed and cunning officials could not be curbed, goings and comings lacked restraint, and joy and anger exceeded proper measure; together with taking harshness asperspicacity, pettiness as discernment, leniency as virtue, and severity as majesty—some had lingering regrets regarding these two rulers.

Today the realm is at peace and in good order, the Four Seas receive our virtue, the Nine Yi and Eight Man tribes open roads for tribute, and the regional rulers of the Six Domains hasten to obey commands for fear of being last. It may truly be called a flourishing era of Great Peace and…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
中興之美事矣愚猶以邊烽不驚戎雖款塞
而夷情叵測則張皇之戒宜亟也百績旣
張治用成矣而
君門萬里則清問之說宜究也名實旣覈官職
辨矣而元氣所在則敦〻之體宜裕也飛
輓不後方輸足矣而民力旣竭則均節之
法宜愼也陪僕瞽御雖皆正人而情禮比
狎則逢合之端宜察也凡此皆以為之於
無形而消之其未萌所謂制人而不制以
===
天者詩曰敬天之怒無敢戲豫書曰先王
克謹天戒臣人克有常憲此亦足以觀矣
吾考之周禮有救日月之鼓又有救日月
之弓矢夏時于房弗集嗇夫庶人或馳或
走彼其弓矢何補于日月而奔走何益於
辰星耶然而有取焉者用以示敬天之意
雖知遠而難言而吾所以自盡惟此耳有
天下者覽詩書之訓規考周夏之補救則
知天之宇非遠心之宇非近可以通一無
punctuated: 中興之美事矣。愚猶以邊烽不驚，戎雖款塞，而夷情叵測，則張皇之戒宜亟也；百績旣張，治用成矣，而君門萬里，則清問之說宜究也；名實旣覈，官職辨矣，而元氣所在，則敦〻之體宜裕也；飛輓不後，方輸足矣，而民力旣竭，則均節之法宜愼也；陪僕瞽御，雖皆正人，而情禮比狎，則逢合之端宜察也。凡此皆以為之於無形，而消之其未萌，所謂制人而不制以天者。《詩》曰：「敬天之怒，無敢戲豫。」《書》曰：「先王克謹天戒，臣人克有常憲。」此亦足以觀矣。吾考之《周禮》，有救日月之鼓，又有救日月之弓矢；夏時于房弗集，嗇夫庶人或馳或走。彼其弓矢何補于日月，而奔走何益於辰星耶？然而有取焉者，用以示敬天之意。雖知遠而難言，而吾所以自盡惟此耳。有天下者，覽《詩》、《書》之訓規，考周、夏之補救，則知天之宇非遠，心之宇非近，可以通一無
translation_en: … and a splendid achievement of dynastic restoration. Yet in my humble view, although the frontier beacons are undisturbed and the western tribes have knocked at the passes in submission, barbarian intentions are unfathomable, so the precaution of maintaining military readiness should be urgent. Although the hundred achievements have been extended and administrative efficacy accomplished, the Sovereign's gates are ten thousand li away, so the principle of inquiring clearly into the people's plight should be thoroughly investigated. Although titles and realities have been verified and official duties distinguished, where the vital energy of the state resides, the substance of generous and sincere governance [?] should be made abundant. Although rapid grain transport does not lag and regional tribute is sufficient, the people's strength is already exhausted, so methods of equalization and moderation should be handled with care. Although the attendant servants, blind musicians, and personal attendants are all upright men, when feelings and礼儀 become overly familiar and intimate, the beginnings of sycophancy and pandering should be scrutinized. All of these are ways to act upon things while they are still formless and dispel them before they have sprouted—what is meant by governing through human effort rather than leaving control to Heaven [?]. The Book of Odes (Shi) says: "Revere the anger of Heaven, and presume not to indulge in sport and idleness." The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "The former kings were able to be謹 cautious toward the warnings of Heaven, and their ministers and people were able to uphold the constant laws." This too is sufficient to observe the principle. When I examine the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), there are drums for rescuing the sun and moon, and there are also bows and arrows for rescuing the sun and moon; in the Xia dynasty, when the sun and moon did not meet harmoniously in the Fang lodge, the minor officials (sefu) and commoners either galloped on horseback or ran on foot. What help could their bows and arrows be to the sun and moon, and what benefit could their running about bring to the celestial bodies? Yet the reason something is taken from these practices is that they serve to display the intention of revering Heaven. Although one knows that Heaven is distant and difficult to speak of, this alone is how we exhaust our own sincerity. If he who possesses the empire peruses the instructive norms of the Odes and Documents and examines the remedial rituals of the Zhou and Xia, he will know that the realm of Heaven is not far off and the realm of the mind is not merely near, and that they can be united into one without…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
間矣故君臣和則三台平矣王道成則斗
魁明矣萬事順則七政齊矣賢人出則龍
角見矣王道被草木則營室歷九象而可
觀矣陰陽和萬物榮則天一出閶闔而有
光矣其動也若機括其應也若影響蓋未
有有其事而無其驗者要在識治者之求
端焉耳雖然天之理至微而其變徵即不
必牽合求配要亦非無因而至者故惟有
道之主爲能順天使天之權常爲人用可
===
靜可動而不可與變星官曆家占候推測
若步筭之不得不然而吾心已自有天矣
不然俟其變而後圖之雖金泥玉簡登封
禱祀對格之祕如此猶不免土龍芻狗耳
大抵天下之勢倚伏剝復乘除之數往往
而是故守文太平之世無驕陽伏陰當是
時最苦無變狃於故常而不知振至於一
敝不可救起夫惟時有小小星異提撕警
惕日相尋於無逸以求其所謂偏而不舉
punctuated: 間矣。故君臣和則三台平矣，王道成則斗魁明矣，萬事順則七政齊矣，賢人出則龍角見矣，王道被草木則營室歷九象而可觀矣，陰陽和、萬物榮則天一出閶闔而有光矣。其動也若機括，其應也若影響，蓋未有有其事而無其驗者，要在識治者之求端焉耳。雖然，天之理至微，而其變徵即不必牽合求配，要亦非無因而至者。故惟有道之主爲能順天，使天之權常爲人用，可靜可動，而不可與變。星官、曆家占候推測，若步筭之不得不然而吾心已自有天矣。不然，俟其變而後圖之，雖金泥玉簡、登封禱祀，對格之祕如此，猶不免土龍芻狗耳。大抵天下之勢，倚伏、剝復、乘除之數，往往而是。故守文太平之世，無驕陽伏陰，當是時最苦無變，狃於故常而不知振，至於一敝不可救起。夫惟時有小小星異，提撕警惕，日相尋於無逸，以求其所謂偏而不舉
translation_en: …interstice. Therefore, when sovereign and minister are in harmony, the Three Terraces (Santai) are level; when the Kingly Way is accomplished, the bowl of the Northern Dipper (Doukui) is bright; when the myriad affairs go smoothly, the Seven Regulators (Qizheng) are aligned; when worthy men emerge, the Dragon's Horns (Longjiao) appear; when the Kingly Way extends to grasses and trees, the Encampment (Yingshi) passes through the nine phenomena and may be observed; and when yin and yang are in harmony and the myriad things flourish, Celestial Unity (Tianyi) emerges from the Gate of Heaven (Changhe) and shines forth. Its movement is like a crossbow trigger; its response is like shadow and echo. Indeed, there has never been a case where the deed existed without its corresponding verification; the key lies simply in those who understand governance seeking the beginnings thereof. Even so, the principles of Heaven are most subtle, and while one need not force correspondences and seek exact matches for its portentous anomalies, in essence they never arrive without a cause. Thus, only a ruler who possesses the Way is able to accord with Heaven, causing the authority of Heaven constantly to serve human use—capable of stillness and capable of movement, yet never giving rise to anomalies. Astrologers and calendar specialists divine, observe, and conjecture, as though the astronomical calculations could not be otherwise, yet within our own mind there is already Heaven itself. Otherwise, if one waits for anomalies to occur before taking measures against them, even with gold-paste and jade-slip inscriptions, ascending to perform the Feng sacrifice and praying at the altars—with esoteric rites of communion and response such as these—they will still amount to no more than clay dragons and straw dogs. On the whole, in the tendencies of the realm, the cycles of fortune and misfortune, decay and return, waxing and waning are everywhere thus. Therefore, in an age of peace that maintains the established order, when there is neither scorching yang nor lurking yin, the greatest affliction at such a time is the absence of anomalies: people grow accustomed to old routines and do not know how to rouse themselves, until once things collapse they can no longer be rescued. Only when from time to time there are minor stellar anomalies to awaken and put them on guard, so that day after day they pursue untiring diligence in order to seek out whatever is lopsided and unaddressed…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之處然後天下之治可以常振而不廢乂
安而不危然則其無變者乃其所以爲變
而有變者其固所以爲無變也歟
第五問
牛大緯
同考試官教諭梁批談時務者類多勦襲此
作籌畫精詳議論剴切重責實效爲經久計有用
之才也錄之
考試官訓導唐批安民者苦於議兵防盜
===
者憚於去兵計難兩得也矧可憂者不止盜哉是
作明於調停均節之術以禦夷以弭盜以乂安元
元期臻實效得算多矣經濟旣具隨試咸宜良爲
國家得人慶
考試官教諭鄭批以責實談時務善於擘
劃矣
弭盜之法必知其源之所在於其内外名
實之間而圖之則無兵刃而安無障塞而
固矣今之雜處山麓教令之所不馴閭伍
punctuated:
之處，然後天下之治可以常振而不廢、乂安而不危。然則其無變者，乃其所以爲變；而有變者，其固所以爲無變也歟！
第五問
牛大緯
同考試官教諭梁批：談時務者類多勦襲，此作籌畫精詳，議論剴切，重責實效，爲經久計，有用之才也，錄之。
考試官訓導唐批：安民者苦於議兵，防盜者憚於去兵，計難兩得也，矧可憂者不止盜哉！是作明於調停均節之術，以禦夷，以弭盜，以乂安元元，期臻實效，得算多矣。經濟旣具，隨試咸宜，良爲國家得人慶。
考試官教諭鄭批：以責實談時務，善於擘劃矣。
弭盜之法，必知其源之所在，於其内外、名實之間而圖之，則無兵刃而安，無障塞而固矣。今之雜處山麓，教令之所不馴，閭伍…
translation_en:
…places, and only then can the governance of the empire be constantly revitalized without falling into neglect, and remain peaceful and secure without falling into danger. If this is so, then having no anomalies is precisely what brings about upheaval, whereas having anomalies is indeed what prevents upheaval!

Fifth Question
Niu Dawei 牛大緯
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Liang: Those who discuss current affairs mostly plagiarize and repeat old clichés. This essay's planning is precise and detailed, and its arguments are incisive and to the point. It places heavy emphasis on demanding practical results and plans for the long term. He is a man of useful talent; let this be recorded for publication.
Comment by Examiner Assistant Instructor Tang: Those who seek to pacify the people are troubled by discussions of military action, while those who guard against bandits dread the disbanding of troops; it is difficult to devise a plan that achieves both, especially when what is worrisome is not merely bandits! This essay is clear in the art of harmonizing and balancing measures—to defend against foreign peoples, to suppress bandits, and to bring peace and security to the common people—aiming to achieve practical results, and its winning calculations are many. Since his statecraft is already well-formed, wherever he is employed he will be well-suited; truly, we may rejoice for the state in having obtained such a man.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zheng: Discussing current affairs by demanding practical realities, he is truly skilled at strategic planning.

In the method of suppressing bandits, one must know where their source lies, and plan for them by distinguishing between the internal and the external, the nominal and the actual; then, without weapons and blades there will be peace, and without frontier barriers there will be security. Nowadays, those who live interspersed at the foot of the mountains, untamed by instruction and decrees, and who into the neighborhood registers…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之所不比與夫土著不毛之夫幾棬握之
利走死地如驚者內寇也風濤出沒攘奪
虔劉螘聚蟊屯去來飄忽舷居而水食者
外寇也患在內者根據難拔患在外者迅
疾莫測要之內借外以為聲援外待內以
為指縱二者今昔之所以駸尋莫禁有然
矣夫粤天下之澤國也負山阻海其民有
魚鹽之利果蓏螺蛤不待賈而足稍耕耨
之足給一歲然而甹窳偷生急末作喜攻
===
戰以侵伐亦其天性也語曰涓涓不息將
成江河綿綿不絕將尋斧柯大抵天下事
有形而圖之者易無形而圖之者難兩軍
相當形勢險易奇正去來之變要可抵掌
而談也攻城略地乗銳犯堅阨塞要害之
處可以指畫而定也惟夫無形之幾微隱
潜伏包藏媒胎觀其外若無所見而其實
有不測之隱憂急之則亟而害小緩之則
遲而害大起而騷除之則狃於目前數十
punctuated: 之所不比，與夫土著不毛之夫，幾棬握之利，走死地如驚者，內寇也；風濤出沒，攘奪虔劉，螘聚蟊屯，去來飄忽，舷居而水食者，外寇也。患在內者根據難拔，患在外者迅疾莫測。要之，內借外以為聲援，外待內以為指縱，二者今昔之所以駸尋莫禁，有然矣。夫粤，天下之澤國也，負山阻海，其民有魚鹽之利，果蓏螺蛤，不待賈而足，稍耕耨之，足給一歲。然而甹窳偷生，急末作，喜攻戰以侵伐，亦其天性也。語曰：「涓涓不息，將成江河；綿綿不絕，將尋斧柯。」大抵天下事，有形而圖之者易，無形而圖之者難。兩軍相當，形勢險易，奇正去來之變，要可抵掌而談也；攻城略地，乗銳犯堅，阨塞要害之處，可以指畫而定也。惟夫無形之幾，微隱潜伏，包藏媒胎，觀其外若無所見，而其實有不測之隱憂。急之則亟而害小，緩之則遲而害大；起而騷除之，則狃於目前數十
translation_en:
…cannot be registered into neighborhood units, along with those native inhabitants of barren lands who covet a handful of profit [?] and rush into fatal ground as if startled [or: like stampeding horses]—these are the internal bandits. Those who appear and disappear amidst wind and waves, plundering and slaughtering, gathering like ants and swarming like locusts, coming and going like a whirlwind, living aboard ship and feeding off the waters—these are the external bandits. When the trouble lies within, its roots are hard to pull up; when the trouble lies without, its swiftness is impossible to fathom. In sum, the internal bandits borrow the external ones as backup and support, while the external bandits rely on the internal ones for direction and guidance. That both have gradually spread from past to present without anyone being able to stop them is indeed for this reason.

Now Guangdong is a watery country of the realm. Backed by mountains and fronted by the sea, its people enjoy the profits of fish and salt; fruits, melons, snails, and clams are sufficient without waiting for merchants, and with only a little plowing and weeding, there is enough to supply a whole year. Yet they live indolently and improvidently [?], are eager for secondary occupations, and delight in attacking, fighting, and raiding—this too is their natural disposition. As the saying goes: "If a trickle does not cease, it will become a great river; if a fine thread is not cut, it will require an axe and handle."

Broadly speaking, in the affairs of the world, what has visible form is easy to plan against, whereas what is formless is hard to plan against. When two armies face each other, the险and easy features of the terrain and the shifts of unorthodox and orthodox tactics in advancing and retreating can, in essence, be discussed while clapping one's hands. In storming cities and seizing territory, riding momentum to assault strongholds, the strategic passes and vital points can be settled by pointing and mapping them out. Only the formless incipient springs of action—subtle, hidden, and lying low, harboring and gestating the seeds of trouble—seem when viewed from the outside as though nothing is there, yet in reality hold unfathomable hidden anxieties. If one presses them urgently, the crisis comes quickly and the harm is small; if one treats them laxly, the crisis comes late and the harm is great. Yet if one rises up to sweep them away, people are so accustomed to the present abuses accumulated over several…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
年積習之敝而莫能頓捄所謂時之不得
不然而勢之不容不然者其惟汰游靡練
土兵爲之其未有而制之其未動斯爲
今日之要務乎粵之稱兵有年矣平定之後
可以萬全無虞而執事猶有不必然之慮
者毋亦有見於向之所謂幾而爲萬億年
無疆之策乎夫自番州而上接牂牁九疑
此嶺南界也其地番夷市舶交易蓋自唐
結好立戶而已然矣洪武初令商番止集
===
舶所乃後稍稍築私室於灣澳以便交易
則已有雜居之意矣嘉靖間盜發禁之徙
去尋又別集今之香山濠鏡澳林林然聚
也夫市之可也居之不可也乃今則居矣
居而聯絡矣又或匿亡命畜死士矣而漳
潮無藉蚊附而蠅集矣官爲之榷則任其
便而譁然齮齕莫誰何矣今承平旣久
國家威靈萬無一失脫有不測何以待之今
成者卽不可亟毀廢者勿令其續成又禁
punctuated: 年積習之敝，而莫能頓捄。所謂時之不得不然而勢之不容不然者，其惟汰游靡、練土兵，爲之其未有，而制之其未動，斯爲今日之要務乎！粵之稱兵有年矣，平定之後，可以萬全無虞，而執事猶有不必然之慮者，毋亦有見於向之所謂幾，而爲萬億年無疆之策乎？夫自番州而上，接牂牁、九疑，此嶺南界也。其地番夷市舶交易，蓋自唐結好立戶而已然矣。洪武初，令商番止集舶所，乃後稍稍築私室於灣澳以便交易，則已有雜居之意矣。嘉靖間，盜發禁之，徙去，尋又別集，今之香山濠鏡澳林林然聚也。夫市之可也，居之不可也。乃今則居矣，居而聯絡矣，又或匿亡命、畜死士矣，而漳、潮無藉蚊附而蠅集矣，官爲之榷，則任其便而譁然齮齕，莫誰何矣。今承平旣久，國家威靈，萬無一失，脫有不測，何以待之？今成者卽不可亟毀，廢者勿令其續成，又禁
translation_en:
…years of accumulated bad habits, so that they cannot be suddenly remedied. As for what the times make unavoidable and the circumstances do not allow to be otherwise, does it not lie solely in culling out the idle and extravagant, training the local troops, acting upon things before they exist, and controlling them before they stir—is not this the urgent task of today?

Guangdong has seen military campaigns for years now. After its pacification, one might consider it completely secure and free from worry; yet if Your Honor still harbors concerns over what is not necessarily certain, is it not because you have perceived what was earlier called the subtle incipient signs, and are formulating a boundless plan for myriad ages to come?

Now, from Panzhou (Guangzhou) upward, connecting to Zangke and Mount Jiuyi, is the territory of the Lingnan circuit. In this region, foreign maritime trading vessels have conducted commerce—something that has been so ever since the Tang dynasty established friendly relations and set up households for them. At the beginning of the Hongwu era (1368–1398), foreign merchants were ordered to gather only at the Maritime Trade Superintendency. Later, however, they gradually built private dwellings in the bays and coves to facilitate trade, thus already showing an intention to live interspersed with the local population. During the Jiajing era (1522–1566), when piracy broke out, they were prohibited and moved away, yet before long they gathered elsewhere; today, at Haojing'ao (Macau) in Xiangshan, they congregate in dense multitudes. Now, trading with them is permissible, but letting them reside there is not. Yet today they do reside there, and residing there, they have formed connected settlements; moreover, some harbor fugitives and maintain men ready to die, while shiftless rogues from Zhangzhou and Chaozhou cling to them like mosquitoes and swarm like flies. When officials levy taxes on them, they act at their own convenience, clamorously bickering and snapping, so that no one dares challenge them. Now, peace has lasted a long time, and through the awesome majesty of the Dynasty, there is not one chance in ten thousand of a mishap; yet should the unexpected occur, how would we deal with it? Even if the structures already built cannot be hastily demolished, those that fall into ruin should not be allowed to be rebuilt, and we should further prohibit…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其來者不得附益如洪武中只就舶所故
事數年之後以次散落是亦陰折其武悍
之氣而剝落其附比之黨也或者其庶幾
矣不然吾見其寖以滋蔓昌熾而不可圖
也合浦欽靈山雷此海北界也其俗類西
粤地磽埆不耕作民以採珠爲業然自吳
已有禁矣唐宋間尋弛尋復至洪武中猶
復採取已而禁嚴民以饑困然大盜巨艘
掠而取之而不得則攻埋椎剽久而戍者
===
私焉陽浮而陰示其意旣乃半其入則取
其沒而得者掌握錐刀之末抵死鉗釱載
道亦可憫也先是烏兔白鴿二寨面峙夾
而戍已廢烏兔而並於白鴿益單弱莫濟
盜公行無禁矣議者欲復烏兔嚴其戍而
差其罪劫殺爲上從者次之沒而得者末
減之是亦救敝之微權乎不然吾莫知其
所終也已瓊崖亦南溟之一都會也則黎
岐爲急盤據山峒郡縣環乎其外進有所
punctuated:
其來者不得附益，如洪武中只就舶所故事，數年之後以次散落，是亦陰折其武悍之氣，而剝落其附比之黨也，或者其庶幾矣。不然，吾見其寖以滋蔓昌熾而不可圖也。

合浦、欽、靈山、雷，此海北界也。其俗類西粤，地磽埆不耕作，民以採珠爲業。然自吳已有禁矣，唐、宋間尋弛尋復，至洪武中猶復採取，已而禁嚴，民以饑困。然大盜巨艘掠而取之，而不得則攻埋椎剽。久而戍者私焉，陽浮而陰示其意，旣乃半其入。則取其沒而得者，掌握錐刀之末，抵死鉗釱載道，亦可憫也。先是，烏兔、白鴿二寨面峙夾而戍，已廢烏兔而並於白鴿，益單弱莫濟，盜公行無禁矣。議者欲復烏兔，嚴其戍而差其罪：劫殺爲上，從者次之，沒而得者末減之。是亦救敝之微權乎！不然，吾莫知其所終也已。

瓊、崖亦南溟之一都會也，則黎、岐爲急。盤據山峒，郡縣環乎其外，進有所
translation_en:
…newcomers from joining to swell their ranks—following the precedent of the Hongwu era (1368–1398) whereby trade was conducted solely at the anchorage of the ships—then after a few years they will gradually disperse one after another. This would also secretly break their fierce and martial spirit and strip away the factions that collude with them; perhaps this might come close to solving the problem. Otherwise, I foresee that they will gradually spread, flourish, and become impossible to control.

Hepu 合浦, Qin 欽, Lingshan 靈山, and Lei 雷 form the Haibei 海北 region. Their customs resemble those of western Guangdong and Guangxi (Xiyue 西粤); the land is barren and stony, unsuited for farming, so the people make their living by diving for pearls. Yet prohibitions on this have existed since the Wu 吳 dynasty [of the Three Kingdoms]. During the Tang and Song dynasties, the ban was repeatedly relaxed and restored. Down to the Hongwu era, pearl harvesting was still carried out, but soon afterward the prohibition was made strict, and the people suffered from hunger and hardship. Nevertheless, great bandits in huge vessels plunder and seize the pearls, and when they fail to get them, they attack, rob, and murder [? 攻埋椎剽]. Over time, the garrison soldiers entered into private collusion with them, outwardly patrolling on the water while secretly signaling their intentions, and eventually taking half of the haul. Meanwhile, those caught diving for pearls—holding a mere trifle of profit in the palms of their hands—are sentenced to death or fill the roads in neck-collars and leg-irons, which is truly pitiable. Previously, the two stockades of Wutu 烏兔 and Baige 白鴿 stood facing each other to guard the area from both sides. Later, Wutu was abolished and merged into Baige, making the defense even more isolated, weak, and ineffective, so that bandits now operate openly without restraint. Commentators wish to restore the Wutu stockade, tighten its garrison, and grade the offenses: making robbery and murder the highest crime, being an accomplice the next, and diving to obtain pearls the lightest, subject to reduced punishment. Would this not be a subtle expedient for remedying the present abuses? Otherwise, I do not know how it will all end.

Qiong 瓊 and Yai 崖 [Hainan Island] also constitute a major metropolis of the Southern Sea, and there the Li 黎 and Qi 岐 peoples are the most urgent problem. Entrenched in the mountain valleys, with the prefectures and counties encircling them on the outside, when they advance they have something to…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
掠而退有所守彼無外憂而我有内患蓋
自職方以來千六百年餘靡有寧日元至
元間大舉空其巢窟勒五指山嘉靖間渡
師直擣其穴賊迸首就死可謂偉矣然皆
未有善後之略以故隨散隨聚其舉之也
未覩目前一息之安而調發傳置儲芻之
費不待遠計瓊崖之間固已數十萬矣如
此即累舉何益也議者欲於大兵之後乗
其威力從瓊至崖千里而遥自儋至萬六
===
百餘里橫徑以十字通道直走其峒洞胸
達背爪分之然後邑里亭障衣冠禮樂而
沙灣羅合郎温嶺脚諸峒悉為坦途是亦
一勞永逸之計而瓊之民或者其少息也
自春恩陽電而上亘高凉蒼梧亦嶺西一
都會也其間徭浪最著從晉康都城走高
要楊柳兩山之間如大牛石歌村石龜古
種古蓬上馬綿邈千餘里皆為巢窟往時
劫高州破其城嗣後出沒莫禁蓋我聚而
punctuated:
掠，而退有所守，彼無外憂而我有内患，蓋自職方以來，千六百年餘靡有寧日。元至元間，大舉空其巢窟，勒五指山；嘉靖間，渡師直擣其穴，賊迸首就死，可謂偉矣。然皆未有善後之略，以故隨散隨聚。其舉之也，未覩目前一息之安，而調發、傳置、儲芻之費，不待遠計，瓊、崖之間固已數十萬矣。如此，即累舉何益也？議者欲於大兵之後，乗其威力，從瓊至崖千里而遥，自儋至萬六百餘里，橫徑以十字通道，直走其峒，洞胸達背、爪分之，然後邑里、亭障、衣冠、禮樂，而沙灣、羅合、郎温、嶺脚諸峒悉為坦途。是亦一勞永逸之計，而瓊之民或者其少息也。
自春、恩、陽、電而上，亘高凉、蒼梧，亦嶺西一都會也。其間徭、浪最著，從晉康、都城走高要、楊柳兩山之間，如大牛、石歌村、石龜、古種、古蓬、上馬，綿邈千餘里，皆為巢窟。往時劫高州，破其城，嗣後出沒莫禁。蓋我聚而
translation_en:
…plunder, and when retreating they have strongholds to defend. They have no external worries, while we suffer from an internal affliction; indeed, for over sixteen hundred years since the region was brought onto the imperial registers, there has scarcely been a day of peace. During the Zhiyuan era of the Yuan dynasty (1264–1294), a grand campaign emptied out their lairs and an inscription was carved on Mount Wuzhi; during the Jiajing era (1522–1566), troops crossed the sea and struck directly at their dens, and the rebels scattered their heads and went to their deaths—feats that may truly be called magnificent. Yet in neither case was there a strategy for post-campaign rehabilitation, and for that reason no sooner were they dispersed than they gathered again. When such campaigns are launched, before one even witnesses a single breath of immediate peace, the expenses for troop mobilization, post-relay transport, and provisions and fodder—without needing to reckon the long term—have already reached several hundred thousand taels within Qiongzhou and Yazhou alone. Being so, even if campaigns are launched repeatedly, what is the benefit? Commentators propose that in the wake of a major military expedition, riding upon its awe-inspiring might, one should cut a cross-shaped network of thoroughfares running over a thousand li from Qiongzhou to Yazhou and over six hundred li from Danzhou to Wanzhou, driving straight through their mountain valleys (dong) to pierce them front to back and divide them up like the claws of a paw. Thereafter, with settlements, border outposts, proper dress, and rites and music established, all the valleys such as Shawan, Luohe, Langwen, and Lingjiao will become level highways. This too is a plan for eternal ease at the cost of a single effort, whereby the people of Qiongzhou may perhaps enjoy a brief respite.

Proceeding upward from Yangchun, Enping, Yangjiang, and Dianbai, and stretching across Gaoliang and Cangwu, lies another metropolis of the region west of the Passes (Lingxi). Among the peoples there, the Yao and the Lang are the most prominent. Running from Jinkang and Ducheng between the two mountain ranges of Gaoyao and Yangliu, places such as Daniushi, Gecun, Shigui, Guzhong, Gupeng, and Shangma stretch far and wide for more than a thousand li, all serving as their lairs.
