In former times they raided Gaozhou and breached its city walls, and thereafter they have appeared and disappeared without anyone being able to check them. This is because when we mass our forces,…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
彼散我進而彼退我厚集其陳而彼星落
以伺吾釁近一舉蕩平為東安西寧二都
界兩山之間而統之於羅定州候燧亭障
為函夏經略虜於是狼奔鳥遯無復逸志
是誠千載一會也但其招揷安輯愚以為
園田漆林之類宜悉以付之勿與之競豪
眇而履畝之稅不必煩劇新民復業者任
之其不能盡墾者姑令屯兵雜耕如孔明
渭濱之事而又聚其兵力營堡千百為屯
===
統以偏裨勿令使分即有流劫相機鵰勦
數年之後可以衽席而為樂土之民矣昔
人有言夷狄而中國則中國之中國而夷
狄則夷狄之夫商番之居内地者始於内
地綱紀潜通勾致一二莫覺既乃蔓衍莫
禁而因有所要其中籍者率濫惡所輸無
幾而其奇贏不訾者大抵揚航去不報籍
以故
國計日絀籌策莫措此未必不有以導之如
punctuated: 彼散，我進而彼退，我厚集其陳而彼星落以伺吾釁。近一舉蕩平，為東安、西寧二都，界兩山之間，而統之於羅定州。候燧亭障，為函夏經略，虜於是狼奔鳥遯，無復逸志，是誠千載一會也。但其招揷安輯，愚以為園田、漆林之類，宜悉以付之，勿與之競豪眇，而履畝之稅，不必煩劇。新民復業者任之，其不能盡墾者，姑令屯兵雜耕，如孔明渭濱之事。而又聚其兵力，營堡千百為屯，統以偏裨，勿令使分，即有流劫，相機鵰勦，數年之後，可以衽席而為樂土之民矣。昔人有言：「夷狄而中國，則中國之；中國而夷狄，則夷狄之。」夫商番之居内地者，始於内地綱紀潜通，勾致一二，莫覺；既乃蔓衍莫禁，而因有所要。其中籍者率濫惡，所輸無幾，而其奇贏不訾者，大抵揚航去不報籍。以故國計日絀，籌策莫措，此未必不有以導之，如
translation_en: … they scatter; when we advance, they retreat; when we mass our battle formations in strength, they disperse like stars to watch for an opening against us. Recently, at a single stroke they were swept away and pacified, and the two county seats of Dong'an and Xining were established, demarcating the territory between the two mountains and placing them under the jurisdiction of Luoding Subprefecture. With beacon towers and frontier barriers set up to organize the heartland, the bandits have fled like wolves and scattered like birds, no longer harboring ambitions of rebellion—this is truly an opportunity of a thousand years. Yet as for recruiting, resettling, and pacifying the populace, I humbly believe that gardens, fields, lacquer groves, and the like should all be handed over to them without competing over every tiny fraction, and the land tax per *mu* need not be made burdensome. Let the new subjects and those returning to their livelihoods manage what they can, and for the land they cannot fully bring under cultivation, let garrison soldiers be assigned for the time being to farm interspersed among them, just as Kongming (Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮) did along the banks of the Wei River. Furthermore, we should concentrate our military forces into fortified camps of hundreds or thousands as agricultural colonies, commanded by subordinate generals so that their strength is not divided. Even if there are roving raids, we can seize the opportunity to swoop down and exterminate them; after a few years, the people will be able to sleep securely on their mats and become subjects of a happy land. An ancient once said: "When barbarians behave like the Central States, treat them as the Central States; when those of the Central States behave like barbarians, treat them as barbarians." As for the foreign merchants who reside in the interior, it began when brokers and agents in the interior secretly communicated with them, luring in one or two without anyone noticing; eventually they spread so widely that they could not be prohibited, and consequently began making demands. The goods that are registered among them are generally shoddy and inferior, yielding very little in revenue, whereas those who make immeasurable profits mostly hoist sail and depart without reporting for registration. For this reason, the finances of the Dynasty grow more depleted by the day and fiscal planners have no measures to take. This is not necessarily without someone guiding them, just like…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
中行說敎匈奴故事是中國而夷狄之所
以可惡也然則夷夏之禁防其可以不嚴
乎夫利百物之所生也天地之所載也而
或專之爲害多矣考之咸通開寶中有弛
廉州珠禁罷嶺南媚川採珠者
國初洪熙中間一行之然亦未聞有啓爭肇
釁之事也今旣不可遽弛而防戍又如此
疎闊是不亦重抑細民而爲巨盜利藪耶
宜其刀鋸沒溺至死而不避也黎岐十字
===
之議是矣然興師十萬日費千金益以渡
海之難又況粤之兵食入不給其所出卽
欲大興何所仰給考之宣弘間落窯黎亭
諸酋竊發皆以兵備統漢達官軍討平之
雖未必長治久安之策要之號令嚴明備
禦有賴亦一面之干城也至如西嶺之事
又不必慮者蓋其始也險阸相迫則攻之
難其旣也出沒飄忽則守之難今而攻則
擣穴矣守則連城列障矣其惟寬其傜賦
punctuated: 中行說敎匈奴故事，是中國而夷狄之，所以可惡也。然則夷夏之禁防，其可以不嚴乎？夫利，百物之所生也，天地之所載也，而或專之，爲害多矣。考之咸通、開寶中，有弛廉州珠禁、罷嶺南媚川採珠者。國初、洪熙中，間一行之，然亦未聞有啓爭肇釁之事也。今旣不可遽弛，而防戍又如此疎闊，是不亦重抑細民而爲巨盜利藪耶？宜其刀鋸、沒溺，至死而不避也。黎岐十字之議是矣，然興師十萬，日費千金，益以渡海之難；又況粤之兵食，入不給其所出，卽欲大興，何所仰給？考之宣、弘間，落窯、黎亭諸酋竊發，皆以兵備統漢、達官軍討平之。雖未必長治久安之策，要之號令嚴明，備禦有賴，亦一面之干城也。至如西嶺之事，又不必慮者。蓋其始也，險阸相迫，則攻之難；其旣也，出沒飄忽，則守之難。今而攻則擣穴矣，守則連城列障矣，其惟寬其傜賦，
translation_en:
… the precedent of Zhonghang Yue 中行說 instructing the Xiongnu; this is why those of the Central States who behave like barbarians are detestable. That being so, how can the restrictions and defenses between barbarians and Chinese not be strict?

Now, profit is what gives birth to the hundred things and what Heaven and Earth sustain; yet when someone monopolizes it, the harm is great indeed. Examining the Xiantong 咸通 (860–874) and Kaibao 開寶 (968–976) eras, there were instances of relaxing the prohibition on pearls in Lianzhou 廉州 and abolishing the Meichuan 媚川 pearl-diving corps in Lingnan 嶺南. At the beginning of our dynasty and during the Hongxi 洪熙 era (1425), pearl-gathering was practiced on occasion, yet we never heard of it provoking strife or initiating hostilities. Now, since the prohibition cannot be suddenly relaxed, and yet the defense garrisons are so lax and sparse, does this not heavily suppress the common people while creating a haven of profit for great bandits? It is no wonder that they brave the blade, the saw, and drowning, not shrinking even unto death.

The proposal to cut crossroads through the Li 黎 and Qi 岐 territories is sound indeed; however, raising an army of a hundred thousand costs a thousand pieces of gold a day, compounded by the difficulty of crossing the sea. Moreover, military provisions and revenues in Guangdong are insufficient to cover expenditures—even if we wished to launch a major campaign, what could we rely on for supplies? Examining the Xuande 宣德 (1426–1435) and Hongzhi 弘治 (1488–1505) eras, when the chieftains of Luoyao 落窯 and Liting 黎亭 covertly rose up, in every case Military Defense circuits led Chinese and Mongol government troops to suppress and pacify them. Although this may not be a strategy for perpetual order and lasting peace, in sum, when commands are strict and clear and defenses are reliable, it serves as a bulwark for one region.

As for the affairs of the Western Mountains (Xiling 西嶺), they are even less cause for worry. For in the beginning, their险要 defiles pressed close together, making them difficult to attack; subsequently, the rebels appeared and disappeared unpredictably, making it difficult to defend against them. Now, in attacking we have struck straight into their lairs, and in defending we have linked walled forts and arrayed barricades. Only by relaxing their corvée labor and taxes, …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
節其物力以維結其心使其不樂於夷俗
之無法而苦於官府之有法則數年之後
與漢人無異矣雖然變故不時有治平不
忘戰惟智者爲能圖危於無形而消患於
未萌東粤之最急者莫大於兵食古者寓
兵於農軍藏於六鄉將寓於六卿以伍兩
卒旅師軍而寓於井邑丘甸縣鄙以振旅
茇舍治兵大閱而寓於蒐苗獮狩有事則
爲兵無事則爲農故不煩均節而財自給
===
今兵農旣分而屯田之制又寢以廢弛於
是有白徒游食以糜民財物力安得不蹙
令行間無謁客矣士伍無頂名矣劔戟無
脃弱矣其要在於徇名責實起居必精動
靜必一訓練必習責成於大將而毋拘束
於文法寇至而能摧鋒者賞之失事者罰
之則營衞固而備禦周而民得盡力矣此
實其源之所在所謂無形之險而難圖者
內患外患其究在此故曰知其源之所在
punctuated: 節其物力，以維結其心，使其不樂於夷俗之無法，而苦於官府之有法，則數年之後，與漢人無異矣。雖然，變故不時有，治平不忘戰，惟智者爲能圖危於無形，而消患於未萌。東粤之最急者，莫大於兵食。古者寓兵於農，軍藏於六鄉，將寓於六卿；以伍、兩、卒、旅、師、軍而寓於井、邑、丘、甸、縣、鄙；以振旅、茇舍、治兵、大閱而寓於蒐、苗、獮、狩。有事則爲兵，無事則爲農，故不煩均節而財自給。今兵農旣分，而屯田之制又寢以廢弛，於是有白徒游食以糜民財，物力安得不蹙？令行間無謁客矣，士伍無頂名矣，劔戟無脃弱矣，其要在於徇名責實：起居必精，動靜必一，訓練必習，責成於大將而毋拘束於文法；寇至而能摧鋒者賞之，失事者罰之，則營衞固而備禦周，而民得盡力矣。此實其源之所在，所謂無形之險而難圖者，內患外患，其究在此。故曰：知其源之所在，
translation_en:
… economize their material resources so as to bind their hearts to us, ensuring they do not delight in the lawlessness of barbarian customs while suffering under the regulations of the authorities—then after a few years, they will be no different from Han Chinese.

Even so, unforeseen crises arise at any time, and in eras of peace and order one must not forget warfare; only the wise are able to plan against danger while it is still formless and eliminate trouble before it sprouts. Among the most urgent matters in eastern Guangdong, none is greater than troops and provisions. In antiquity, soldiers were lodged among the farmers: the armies were stored within the Six Districts, and the generals were lodged among the Six Ministers; the military units of five, twenty-five, one hundred, five hundred, two thousand five hundred, and twelve thousand five hundred men were lodged within the rural divisions of wells, hamlets, mounds, tracts, districts, and marches; and the military exercises of arraying cohorts, pitching camp, drilling troops, and grand reviews were lodged within the spring, summer, autumn, and winter hunts. When emergencies arose they served as soldiers, and when there was peace they worked as farmers; thus, without the trouble of equalizing and economizing, resources were naturally sufficient.

Now, soldiers and farmers have already been separated, and the system of military farms (tuntian) has gradually fallen into neglect and decay. Consequently, there are unattached idlers who eat without working and waste the people's wealth—how could our material resources not be straitened? Suppose that within the ranks there are no longer parasitic guests seeking favors, among the squads there are no longer substitute names on the rosters, and among the swords and halberds there are no longer brittle and weak weapons; the essential point lies in demanding actual performance to match the title: daily routines must be disciplined, movement and rest must be unified, and training and drills must be thoroughly practiced. Hold the senior commanders responsible for results and do not bind them with petty legalisms; when raiders arrive, reward those who can break their vanguard and punish those who fail in their duty. Then the camps and guards will be secure, the defenses will be comprehensive, and the common people will be able to devote their full strength to their livelihoods. This is truly where the source of the matter lies. As for what is called the formless strategic peril that is difficult to plan against, the ultimate root of both internal and external troubles lies right here. Therefore it is said: if one knows where the source lies, …

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於其内外名實之間而圖之則無兵刃而
安無障塞而固矣
punctuated: 於其内外、名實之間而圖之，則無兵刃而安，無障塞而固矣。
translation_en: …between inner and outer, name and reality, and attends to it, then there will be peace without weapons and security without fortifications.

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
廣東鄉試錄成師錫以職事
宜序末簡竊謂人才之興關
乎氣運而振作培植恃
聖人在位與運應也唐虞三代卓
乎尚已
明興
===
高皇帝設科取士諸所創規條纖
悉具至徵文學畀之典試士
抱策入者不得以名通何權
一而範周也當其時風淳俗
樸有司靡敢飾名實炫觀聽
而
聖祖宸慮之嚴乃此以故士益敦
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序
《廣東鄉試錄》成，師錫以職事，宜序末簡。竊謂人才之興，關乎氣運，而振作培植，恃聖人在位，與運應也。唐、虞、三代，卓乎尚已。明興，高皇帝設科取士，諸所創規條，纖悉具至。徵文學畀之典試，士抱策入者，不得以名通。何權一而範周也！當其時，風淳俗樸，有司靡敢飾名實、炫觀聽，而聖祖宸慮之嚴乃此。以故士益敦
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

Now that the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination has been completed, I, [Zhang] Shixi, by virtue of my official duties, ought to write a postface for its final pages. I humbly believe that the rise of men of talent is tied to the turning of cosmic fortune, yet rousing and cultivating them depends upon a sage ruler occupying the throne and responding to that fortune. The eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties stand loftily supreme in antiquity. With the rise of the Ming, the August Emperor Gao established the civil examination system to select scholars, and all the regulations he instituted were thorough in every detail. Literary scholars were summoned and entrusted with presiding over the examinations, while candidates who entered carrying their writing tablets were prevented from having their names known to the examiners. How unified was the authority, and how comprehensive the institutional framework! At that time, customs were pure and mores simple; the authorities dared not embellish name and reality to dazzle the eyes and ears of the public, and yet the Sacred Ancestor's imperial foresight was already this strict. For this reason, scholars increasingly esteemed…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
本尚質發爲文詞務根極理
要非經訓不言一入爲吏則
逡逡守法度他有卓犖奇偉
亦皆從繩墨注厝非有泛駕
而馳者一時人才誠足肩唐
虞駕三代謂
聖人所振作非歟
===
列聖紹休
代光文敎
世廟初嘗出京朝官柄試事蓋仰
繩
祖武廣厲而振德之也頃者
皇上眷念賓賢
懿典
punctuated:
本尚質，發爲文詞，務根極理要，非經訓不言；一入爲吏，則逡逡守法度，他有卓犖奇偉，亦皆從繩墨注厝，非有泛駕而馳者。一時人才，誠足肩唐虞、駕三代，謂聖人所振作，非歟？
列聖紹休，代光文敎。世廟初，嘗出京朝官柄試事，蓋仰繩祖武，廣厲而振德之也。頃者皇上眷念賓賢懿典，
translation_en:
…substance and valued simplicity. When expressed in literary compositions, they strove to ground themselves thoroughly in essential principles and spoke of nothing that was not taught in the Classics. Once they entered office as officials, they respectfully and cautiously abided by the laws and regulations; even when others among them possessed extraordinary and outstanding talents, all likewise took their measures in accordance with the plumb-line of the rules, with none kicking over the traces and galloping wildly. The men of talent of that age were truly sufficient to stand shoulder to shoulder with those of Tang and Yu and to surpass those of the Three Dynasties. Could one say this was not due to the rousing and inspiration of the Sage?

Successive Emperors inherited the splendid legacy, generation after generation glorifying cultural education. At the beginning of the reign of Shizong (the Jiajing Emperor), officials of the capital court were once sent out to take charge of examination affairs; this was indeed to look up and follow in the footsteps of the Imperial Ancestor, broadly encouraging and rousing them to virtue. Recently, His Majesty, mindfully cherishing the admirable canon of welcoming the worthy as guests,…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諮之輔臣
下言官之請
允禮卿之議一遵
成憲申爲
令傳示四方師錫奉檄至東粤
未及席則御史以典試
詔旨至伏讀未畢則又以五事
===
詔旨至師錫偕同事津津色喜以
謂
皇上作人
睿慮同符
聖祖固如此哉比及鎖院乃窮日
夜力手自披校期采荆山而
探滄海俾無遺珎焉顧藻績
punctuated: 諮之輔臣，下言官之請，允禮卿之議，一遵成憲，申爲令，傳示四方。師錫奉檄至東粤，未及席，則御史以典試詔旨至；伏讀未畢，則又以五事詔旨至。師錫偕同事津津色喜，以謂皇上作人睿慮，同符聖祖，固如此哉！比及鎖院，乃窮日夜力，手自披校，期采荆山而探滄海，俾無遺珎焉。顧藻績
translation_en: …consulted the Grand Secretaries, sent down the requests of the speaking officials, and approved the deliberations of the Minister of Rites; adhering entirely to the established statutes, he reiterated them as an ordinance and promulgated them to the four quarters. Having received the summons, I, Shixi (師錫), arrived in eastern Yue [Guangdong]. Before my seat had even warmed, the Censor arrived with the imperial decree regarding the administration of the examination; before I had finished bowing to read it, another imperial decree setting forth five stipulations arrived. Together with my colleagues, I was filled with joyful animation, saying to ourselves: "Is not His Majesty's sage solicitude in cultivating men truly in such complete accord with the Sacred Ancestor!" When the time came to enter the locked examination compound, we exhausted our strength day and night, personally opening and collating the scripts with our own hands, hoping to gather jade from Mount Jing and plumb the vast sea so that no precious gem would be left behind. Yet ornate embellishment…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
毀質雕鏤亂眞師錫鰓鰓焉
是懼乃竊持三術用探厥蘊
其沉涵道眞厭飫理奧者聖
學昭也博大宏衍周詳通敏
者政體具也幹以正直澤之
忠厚者節槩正也此師錫之
所采以告成事以塞責也鹿
===
鳴旣歌多士畢集乃進而告
之曰休爾多士其尚知
聖天子掄才至意乎
天子神聖嘉與海內賢雋共臻至
理
御寓以來蓋三論民秀於鄉矣而
督有司
punctuated:
毀質，雕鏤亂眞，師錫鰓鰓焉是懼。乃竊持三術，用探厥蘊：其沉涵道眞、厭飫理奧者，聖學昭也；博大宏衍、周詳通敏者，政體具也；幹以正直、澤之忠厚者，節槩正也。此師錫之所采以告成事、以塞責也。

《鹿鳴》旣歌，多士畢集，乃進而告之曰：「休！爾多士，其尚知聖天子掄才至意乎？天子神聖，嘉與海內賢雋共臻至理，御寓以來，蓋三論民秀於鄉矣。而督有司
translation_en:
…destroys substance, and intricate carving confounds the genuine; of this, I, Shixi, was anxiously fearful. Thus I privately held to three criteria by which to probe their depths: where one is deeply immersed in the truth of the Way and saturated with the profundities of principle, the sage learning is made manifest; where one is broad, grand, comprehensive, and perspicacious, the essentials of governance are complete; where one's substance is uprightness and one is enriched with loyalty and generosity, moral integrity is sound. Such are what I, Shixi, have selected in order to report the completion of the task and to fulfill my responsibility.

After the "Lu Ming" ode was sung and the many scholars had all assembled, I stepped forward and addressed them, saying: "Splendid! Do all you scholars truly understand the Sacred Son of Heaven's utmost intention in selecting talent? The Son of Heaven is divinely sage, and delights in joining with the worthy and outstanding men within the seas to attain supreme governance together. Since ascending the throne to rule the realm, He has thrice evaluated the finest of the people in the provinces. Yet the imperial decrees supervising the authorities…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詔旨視昔有加上體
祖宗心下以端多士之習默焉鼓
舞將用之也爾多士其何以
稱
上意乎夫士窮居草茅坐誦書史
誠願得一見
天子披忠愫或受
===
命為吏舉平生稍施行之乃至有
顛越所挾持捐若弁髦弗遑
顧學名見道而以文姦才稱
練達而以濟慾事務苛細而
以沽名則師錫向之三術無
乃三懼乎
聖天子在上雖殊方偏國猶輸忠
punctuated: 詔旨視昔有加，上體祖宗心，下以端多士之習，默焉鼓舞，將用之也。爾多士其何以稱上意乎？夫士窮居草茅，坐誦書史，誠願得一見天子，披忠愫，或受命為吏，舉平生稍施行之。乃至有顛越所挾持，捐若弁髦，弗遑顧。學名見道而以文姦，才稱練達而以濟慾，事務苛細而以沽名，則師錫向之三術，無乃三懼乎？聖天子在上，雖殊方偏國，猶輸忠
translation_en:
…the imperial decrees supervising the authorities have been even more stringent than in the past. Above, He embodies the mind of the imperial ancestors; below, He rectifies the habits of the many scholars, silently inspiring them as He prepares to employ them. How, then, will you scholars match the Sovereign's intent?

When a scholar lives in obscurity in a thatched hut, sitting and reciting the books and histories, he truly wishes to gain a single audience with the Son of Heaven to pour forth his loyal sincerity, or to receive a commission as an official and put some part of his lifelong learning into practice. Yet there are those who overturn the principles they once held, casting them aside like a useless cap without a second thought. When one's learning is reputed to have perceived the Way, yet is used to gloss over wickedness; when one's talent is praised as experienced and capable, yet is used to indulge desires; when in official affairs one focuses on petty, harsh details in order to fish for fame—then have not the three paths formerly recommended to the throne become three causes for dread?

With the Sacred Son of Heaven reigning above, even distant regions and peripheral states offer up their loyal…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
款歸命
闕下奉
政令惟謹而況多士漸摩
聖澤視齊民不啻百倍視慕化來
者不啻千倍一朝際風雲躡
文陛而立以自附於當世名賢
長者後忍令先資灋之一至
===
此哉先民有言上不負天子
下不負所學爾多士習聞之
矣乃稱其不負者何在師錫
不敏竊謂不負其心而已何
者忠信之性固多士所素植
也誠堅忠信之素衷奉不負
之成訓以仰副
punctuated: 款歸命闕下，奉政令惟謹。而況多士漸摩聖澤，視齊民不啻百倍，視慕化來者不啻千倍；一朝際風雲，躡文陛而立，以自附於當世名賢長者後，忍令先資灋之，一至此哉！先民有言：「上不負天子，下不負所學。」爾多士習聞之矣，乃稱其不負者何在？師錫不敏，竊謂不負其心而已。何者？忠信之性，固多士所素植也。誠堅忠信之素衷，奉不負之成訓，以仰副
translation_en: …sincerity and submit in allegiance at the foot of the imperial palace, obeying government decrees with the utmost reverence. How much more so should you many scholars, who have been steeped in and refined by the sacred grace—more than a hundredfold compared to the common people, and more than a thousandfold compared to those who come out of admiration for our civilizing influence! Once you encounter a propitious moment of wind and clouds, ascend the ornate steps of the throne room, and stand there to align yourselves behind the renowned worthies and elders of the age, how could you bear to let what you first presented as your pledge of service be cast aside [?], coming to such a pass as this! The ancients had a saying: "Above, do not fail the Son of Heaven; below, do not fail what you have learned." You many scholars have heard this often enough, yet wherein lies the fulfillment of "not failing"? Though I, Shi Xi, am of limited ability, I venture to say that it is simply a matter of not failing one's own heart. Why is this? Because a nature of loyalty and trustworthiness is indeed what you many scholars have long cultivated. If you truly hold fast to your long-cherished heart of loyalty and trustworthiness, and uphold the established precept of "not failing" so as to reverently fulfill…

title: 萬曆七年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上側席
盛心而
聖祖設科不爲希寵藉手則豈特
多士之休而主司聲榮亦與
斯錄俱矣勗乎哉
浙江湖州府儒學訓導臣師
錫謹序
punctuated:
皇上側席盛心，而聖祖設科不爲希寵藉手，則豈特多士之休，而主司聲榮亦與斯錄俱矣。勗乎哉！
浙江湖州府儒學訓導臣師錫謹序。
translation_en:
… His Majesty's earnest heart in sitting on the edge of his mat to await worthies, and so that the Sacred Ancestor's institution of the examinations does not serve merely as a stepping-stone to curry favor, then not only will this be the glory of you many scholars, but the renown and honor of the examiners will also endure alongside this record. Exert yourselves!
Respectfully prefaced by your servant Shi Xi 師錫, Assistant Instructor of the Confucian School of Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.
